<h1 id="growthbook-rest-api">GrowthBook REST API v5.1.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

GrowthBook offers a full REST API for interacting with the application.

Request data can use either JSON or Form data encoding (with proper `Content-Type` headers). All response bodies are JSON-encoded.

The API base URL for GrowthBook Cloud is `https://api.growthbook.io/api`. For self-hosted deployments, it is the same as your API_HOST environment variable (defaults to `http://localhost:3100/api`). The rest of these docs will assume you are using GrowthBook Cloud.

## Versioning

Endpoints are versioned by path prefix:

- `/v1/...` — stable, widely-supported endpoints
- `/v2/...` — updated endpoints with improved shapes (e.g. unified per-rule environment scope for feature flags)

New integrations should prefer v2 where available. Feature-flag and metric v1 routes are deprecated: they are tagged **LEGACY** in the sidebar and collapsed by default. Use the matching v2 group when both exist.

## Authentication

We support both the HTTP Basic and Bearer authentication schemes for convenience.

You first need to generate a new API Key in GrowthBook. Different keys have different permissions:

- **Personal Access Tokens**: These are sensitive and provide the same level of access as the user has to an organization, or less if the token's permissions are limited. These can be created by going to `Personal Access Tokens` under your user menu. Members with the API Keys **Manage members' tokens** permission can disable a member's token under `Settings -> Manage PATs`, and admins can require new tokens to expire within a maximum lifetime.
- **Secret Keys**: These are sensitive and provide the level of access of the role they are given, which can be any built-in or custom role, with optional per-project role overrides and environment limits. Managing Secret Keys on behalf of an organization takes the [API Keys permissions](/account/user-permissions). These can be created by going to `Settings -> API Keys`, where Admins can also require new Secret Keys to expire within a maximum lifetime.

If using HTTP Basic auth, pass the Secret Key as the username and leave the password blank (when using curl, add `:` at the end of the secret to indicate an empty password)

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/features \
  -u secret_abc123DEF456:
```

If using Bearer auth, pass the Secret Key as the token:

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/features \
-H "Authorization: Bearer secret_abc123DEF456"
```

If a key has an expiration date, every response includes it in the `X-GrowthBook-Key-Expires-At` header (ISO 8601), so scripts can warn before the key stops working. Requests made with an expired key fail with a `401` that says where to create a replacement. See [Expiration](/integrations/ai-agents/api-keys#expiration) for choosing a key's expiration, the warnings before it lapses, and the organization policies.

## Naming who asked

Requests made with a Secret Key may add an `X-GrowthBook-Requested-By` header naming the organization member who asked for the change, as a user id or an email address. History, revision logs and webhooks show that member next to the key.

Each key acts as **System** (the default) or **User**, set under `Settings -> API Keys`:

- **System**: the header is optional. The key acts as itself, with its own permissions, and the named member is only recorded in history.
- **User**: a request without the header is rejected with a 400. The request acts as the named member, with only what both the key and the member can do, so the header can narrow a key but never widen it. Drafts, owners, `mine` filters and reviews are the member's. The member's rights over their own drafts, comments and verdicts apply only where the key's own role allows the same action.

A System key, or any key that names no one, acts as itself: it can draft and review with its own permissions, and its verdicts are judged on its role. A key belongs to no team, so its approval never satisfies a rule that requires approval from a team. No one can rule on a draft they created, and a key acting as itself can't rule on a draft it created or edited. An approval a User key gives counts only where both the key and the member could approve, and stops counting if the key is disabled, expires or is deleted. Because the header isn't verified, whoever holds the key can act as any member. A value that does not match a member of the organization is rejected with a 400. A create request that omits `owner` defaults it to the member a User key names. Scheduled and auto-publishes run later with the permissions of the request that armed them, and don't run if that member has left the organization, the key has expired, or the key no longer acts as User. Personal Access Tokens and OAuth tokens already act as their user and reject the header.

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/features \
-H "Authorization: Bearer secret_abc123DEF456" \
-H "X-GrowthBook-Requested-By: alice@example.com"
```

## Naming and human review

People review what the API creates in the GrowthBook UI.

- Keep keys and names short (2-5 words). Follow your organization's Feature Flag key format (`featureRegexValidator` and `featureKeyExample` in `GET /v1/settings`), or use kebab-case if it has none. Feature Flag keys can't be changed after creation, and an experiment's tracking key shouldn't change after launch.
- Put context (why, plan, tickets, links) in `description`, not in names or keys.
- Group with `tags`, not name prefixes. Projects (`project` or `projects`) control access and where a resource can be used, so set them deliberately instead of using them as labels.
- To create a Feature Flag disabled with `POST /v2/features`, list every environment in `environments` with `enabled: false` (on `POST /v1/features`, each entry also needs `rules: []`). An environment you leave out uses its default state, which may be enabled.
- Leave publishing and production changes to a person unless asked.
- If a request is blocked (an approval requirement, a warning, a Custom Hook, schema validation or a permission error), stop and ask a person. Don't retry with an override field, a different key or another workaround unless a person asked you to. If a write answers `202` with a `confirmation`, give a person its `url` and wait (see [Waiting for confirmation](#waiting-for-confirmation)).

## Waiting for confirmation

A key can require a person to confirm some writes before they run (see [API Keys for Agents](/integrations/ai-agents/api-keys#require-confirmation)). A held write doesn't run. It answers `202 Accepted` with the confirmation, a `Location` header to poll, and a `Retry-After` header with the seconds to wait between polls:

```json
{
  "confirmation": {
    "id": "cnf_abc123",
    "status": "pending",
    "actions": [
      { "action": "feature.publish", "environments": ["production"] }
    ],
    "summary": "Publish revision 3 of checkout-redesign",
    "url": "https://app.growthbook.io/confirmations/cnf_abc123",
    "expiresAt": "2026-10-15T18:00:00.000Z",
    "response": null,
    "note": null
  },
  "message": "A person must confirm this in GrowthBook. Give them the url, then poll the Location."
}
```

Give the person the `url`, then poll [`GET /v1/confirmations/{id}`](/api/meta/operation/getConfirmation). Pass `wait` (in seconds, up to 30) to hold the poll open until the status changes:

```bash
curl "https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/confirmations/cnf_abc123?wait=30" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer secret_abc123DEF456"
```

| `status`    | Meaning                                                                                                               |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pending`   | Waiting for a person, until `expiresAt` (an hour after the request)                                                   |
| `running`   | Confirmed, and running now                                                                                            |
| `completed` | It ran. `response` holds the status and body the request returned, which may be an error                              |
| `rejected`  | A person declined it, and nothing ran                                                                                 |
| `expired`   | Nobody decided in time, or it acts on something that changed after it was held (with a `400` `response`). Nothing ran |

`note` carries anything the person left for the agent when they decided. `actions` lists what the request was held for, each with the environments it touches.

- Only the key that made the request, or another token of the same person, can read the confirmation.
- Sending the same request again while it's pending returns the same confirmation.
- A request that publishes, reverts or archives, or that changes a Feature Flag or an Experiment's status, schedule, targeting or traffic, isn't run if what it acts on changed after it was held. Other writes, such as editing settings or a draft, run as sent, so they can overwrite changes made while they waited.
- A confirmed request runs once, with the key's permissions (or the member's role it assumes), not the confirmer's. Send it again to retry, which asks for a new confirmation.
- Confirming isn't a review approval.

## Errors

The API may return the following error status codes:

- **400** - Bad Request - Often due to a missing required parameter
- **401** - Unauthorized - No valid API key provided
- **402** - Request Failed - The parameters are valid, but the request failed
- **403** - Forbidden - Provided API key does not have the required access
- **404** - Not Found - Unknown API route or requested resource
- **409** - Conflict - The resource changed since it was read, or its state blocks the request, such as an experiment start's checklist. `code` names which.
- **422** - Unprocessable Entity - The request is valid, but a warning, validation rule, approval requirement, or another publishing gate blocked it. Do not assume that `ignoreWarnings` clears every 422 response.
- **429** - Too Many Requests - You exceeded the rate limit of 60 requests per minute, or the limit your self-hosted server sets. Try again later.
- **5XX** - Server Error - Something went wrong on GrowthBook's end (these are rare)

The response body will be a JSON object with the following properties:

- **message** - Information about the error

### Publishing gates

Automated callers, including AI agents, should report a blocked response to a person instead of retrying with an override. Use an override only when a person has explicitly asked for it.

Publish and experiment start responses include a `gates` array that explains every blocker:

- `type`, `severity`, and `messages` identify the problem.
- `override` names the request-body field that can bypass it. This is `ignoreWarnings` for warnings, `skipSchemaValidation` for schema and invariant failures, `skipHooks` for Custom Hook rejections, or `skipChecklist` for an experiment start's launch checklist items. A value of `null` means there is no request-body override.
- `requiresPermission` identifies any additional permission needed to use the override.
- `resolution` provides an API action, method, and path when the blocker must be resolved another way.

For example, an approval gate is cleared by approving the revision or by using a caller with **Bypass draft approvals** access. A Config lock is cleared through the unlock route in `resolution`.

When a successful publish bypasses a gate, the response includes `bypassedGates`. Each entry reports the gate `type` and how it was bypassed in `via`, which is one of `ignoreWarnings`, `skipSchemaValidation`, `skipHooks`, `skipChecklist`, `bypassApprovalPermission`, `restApiBypassesReviews`, or `revertsBypassApproval` (reverts only). This field is omitted when no gates were bypassed.

### Request flags

Every refusal a request can get past with a flag:

| Flag                      | Where        | Gets past                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ignoreWarnings`          | Body         | Warnings (`422`)                                                                                             |
| `skipSchemaValidation`    | Body         | Schema and invariant failures, with **Bypass draft approvals** access                                        |
| `skipHooks`               | Body         | Custom Hook rejections                                                                                       |
| `skipChecklist`           | Body         | An experiment start's incomplete launch checklist items (`409` `checklist_incomplete`), but not its blockers |
| `allowUnscopedRules`      | Body         | A rule for All Environments and All Projects where the organization requires a scope (`422` `unscoped_rule`) |
| `overrideDraftLimit=true` | Query string | Creating a draft past the draft limit                                                                        |

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://api.growthbook.io/api">https://api.growthbook.io/api</a> - GrowthBook Cloud

* <a href="https://localhost:3100/api">https://localhost:3100/api</a> - Self-hosted GrowthBook

# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer If using Bearer auth, pass the Secret Key as the token:
```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/features   -H "Authorization: Bearer secret_abc123DEF456"
```

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: basic If using HTTP Basic auth, pass the Secret Key as the username and leave the password blank:
```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/features   -u secret_abc123DEF456:
# The ":" at the end stops curl from asking for a password
```

`GET /v1/projects`

```json
      "allowTargeting": true,

        "confidenceLevel": 0,
        "pValueThreshold": 0
      }

  ],
  "limit": 0,
  "offset": 0,
  "count": 0,
  "total": 0,
  "hasMore": true,
  "nextOffset": 0
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response|Inline|

<h3 id="get-all-projects-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projects|[[Project](#schemaproject)]|true|none|none|
|limit|integer|true|none|none|
|offset|integer|true|none|none|
|count|integer|true|none|none|
|total|integer|true|none|none|
|hasMore|boolean|true|none|none|
|nextOffset|integer \| null|true|none|none|
|» *anyOf*|integer|false|none|none|
|» *anyOf*|null|false|none|none|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

## Create a single project

<a id="opIdpostProject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/projects \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "owner": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "publicId": "string",
    "settings": {
      "statsEngine": "string",
      "confidenceLevel": 0,
      "pValueThreshold": 0
    },
    "restrictAccess": true,
    "allowTargeting": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/projects`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "owner": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "publicId": "string",
  "settings": {
    "statsEngine": "string",
    "confidenceLevel": 0,
    "pValueThreshold": 0
  },
  "restrictAccess": true,
  "allowTargeting": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-single-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Short display name. Put details in `description`.|
|» owner|body|string|false|The userId or email address of the owner. If an email address is provided, it will be used to look up the userId of the matching organization member. If an ID is provided, it will be validated as existing in the organization. When omitted, it defaults to the requesting member: a personal access token's owner, or the member an organization API key assumes. An organization API key acting as itself leaves it empty.|
|» description|body|string|false|Put context here, not in the name.|
|» publicId|body|string|false|URL-safe slug (lowercase letters, numbers, dashes). Auto-generated from name if not provided.|
|» settings|body|object|false|Project settings that, when set, override the organization settings.|
|» » statsEngine|body|string|false|Stats engine.|
|» » confidenceLevel|body|number|false|Bayesian chance-to-win threshold (stored as decimal, e.g. 0.95).|
|» » pValueThreshold|body|number|false|Frequentist p-value threshold (e.g. 0.05).|
|» restrictAccess|body|boolean|false|When true, only members with an explicit role on this Project (directly or via a team) can access it. Members with the manageTeam permission retain access. Requires a Pro or Enterprise plan.|
|» allowTargeting|body|boolean|false|Whether Feature Flags owned by other Projects may add this Project to their Targeting Projects. Defaults to true. Turning it off blocks new targeting (and All Projects); existing targeting is kept.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "project": {
    "id": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "dateCreated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "dateUpdated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "description": "string",
    "publicId": "string",
    "restrictAccess": true,
    "allowTargeting": true,
    "owner": "string",
    "ownerEmail": "string",
    "settings": {
      "statsEngine": "string",
      "confidenceLevel": 0,
      "pValueThreshold": 0
    }
  }
}
```

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "confirmation": {
    "id": "string",
    "status": "pending",
    "actions": [
      {
        "action": "feature.create",
        "environments": [
          "string"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "summary": "string",
    "url": "string",
    "expiresAt": "string",
    "response": {
      "status": 0,
      "body": null
    },
    "note": "string"
  },
  "message": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-single-project-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Resource created|Inline|
|202|Accepted|Held until a person confirms it in GrowthBook. Poll the Location until the confirmation completes.|[ConfirmationHeld](#schemaconfirmationheld)|

<h3 id="create-a-single-project-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project|[Project](#schemaproject)|true|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Location|string||The confirmation to poll|
|202|Retry-After|integer||Seconds to wait before polling|

<h1 id="growthbook-rest-api-features-v2">features-v2</h1>

Control your feature flags programmatically.

Rules are returned as a unified top-level array; each rule carries `allEnvironments` / `environments` scope fields instead of being bucketed by environment.

## Get all features

<a id="opIdlistFeaturesV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/features \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/features`

`POST /v2/features`

Creates a new Feature Flag. The caller needs Create access in its Project, plus Publish access for any environment the Feature Flag starts enabled in — one that starts disabled everywhere needs Create alone. Rules are supplied as a top-level `rules` array; each rule includes `allEnvironments` / `environments` scope fields.

### Naming for human review

The `id` is the Feature Flag's permanent name in the UI and code. Keep it short (`checkout-express-pay`) and put context in `description`. To create it disabled, list every environment in `environments` with `enabled: false`.

### Config-backed features (Config mode)

A JSON feature can be backed by a shared **config** — the config supplies the base JSON value and schema, and the feature's *rule* values become override *patches* merged on top (nested objects deep-merge; arrays and scalars replace). The default value is exactly a config with no overrides (see below). Config backing is set exclusively through dedicated fields — never a raw `$extends: ["@config:…"]` inside a value string (that is rejected). `@const:` references inside values still work.

- **Top-level (`baseConfig`):** set `valueType: "json"` and `baseConfig: "<configKey>"` to put the Feature Flag in Config mode. The config must be live. This is the family root and the base the default value patches.
- **Default value:** unlike rules, the default is exactly a config with no overrides of its own — send `defaultValue: "{}"` to use `baseConfig`. To resolve the default to a *descendant* of `baseConfig` instead, set `defaultValueConfig` to that descendant's key (it must be within `baseConfig`'s family); omit/null to use `baseConfig` directly.
- **Rules & experiment variations:** each carries its own `config` field naming the family config that value patches (omit/null to patch the base). `value` is the override patch.

Example:

```json
{
  "id": "checkout-config",
  "valueType": "json",
  "baseConfig": "purchase-flow",
  "defaultValue": "{}",
  "rules": [
    { "type": "force", "config": "purchase-flow-vip", "value": "{\"maxItems\": 20}", "allEnvironments": true }
  ]
}
```

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "archived": true,
  "description": "string",
  "owner": "string",
  "project": "string",
  "targetingAllProjects": true,
  "targetingProjects": [
    "string"
  ],
  "valueType": "boolean",
  "defaultValue": "string",

        }
```

<h3 id="create-a-single-feature-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|skipSchemaValidation|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `skipSchemaValidation` in the request body instead.|
|ignoreWarnings|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `ignoreWarnings` in the request body instead.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» id|body|string|true|Unique, permanent key, shown as the Feature Flag's name in the UI and used in code. Keep it short. If `featureRegexValidator` in `GET /api/v1/settings` is set, follow it (`featureKeyExample` shows the format); otherwise use kebab-case (e.g. `checkout-express-pay`). Put context in `description`.|
|» archived|body|boolean|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|Markdown. What the Feature Flag gates and why, rollout plan, and links. Put context here, not in the key.|
|» owner|body|string|false|The userId or email address of the owner. If an email address is provided, it will be used to look up the userId of the matching organization member. If an ID is provided, it will be validated as existing in the organization. When omitted, it defaults to the requesting member: a personal access token's owner, or the member an organization API key assumes. An organization API key acting as itself must send it, or the request fails with a 400.|
|» project|body|string|false|An associated project ID|
|» targetingAllProjects|body|boolean|false|Make this feature discoverable in — and served to — every project, beyond its primary `project`. Requires the `targetFeatures` permission (FlagsTarget policy) unscoped to any project. Governance stays with `project`.|
|» targetingProjects|body|[string]|false|Secondary project IDs this feature is targeted in and served to, beyond its primary `project`. Adding a project requires the `targetFeatures` permission (FlagsTarget policy) in that project. Governance stays with `project`.|
|» valueType|body|string|true|The data type of the feature payload. Boolean by default.|
|» defaultValue|body|string|true|Default value when feature is enabled. Type must match `valueType`. In Config mode (`baseConfig` set) the default must be exactly a config with no overrides: send `"{}"` to use `baseConfig`, or set `defaultValueConfig` to point at a descendant.|
|» baseConfig|body|string \| null|false|Key of the config backing this flag ("Config mode"). Requires `valueType: "json"` and a live config. The config supplies the base JSON and schema; `defaultValue` and rule values are override patches on top. null or omitted for a plain flag.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» defaultValueConfig|body|string \| null|false|Optional. A config within `baseConfig`'s family that the default value resolves to instead of `baseConfig` itself. null or omitted means the default is `baseConfig`. The default is exactly this config and carries no overrides of its own.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags for filtering and grouping. Use these instead of encoding groups in names.|
|» rules|body|[object]|false|Feature rules. Each rule carries its own environment scope via `allEnvironments` / `environments`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » description|body|string|false|Short note on why the rule exists (e.g. `Beta testers only`).|
|» » condition|body|string|false|none|
|» » savedGroups|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » » match|body|string|true|none|
|» » » ids|body|[string]|true|none|
|» » savedGroupTargeting|body|[object]|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated — use `savedGroups`. Accepted so a GET response can be posted back unchanged; `savedGroups` takes precedence if both are sent.|
|» » » matchType|body|string|true|none|
|» » » savedGroups|body|[string]|true|none|
|» » pendingRamp|body|object|false|Read-only; ignored on write. Accepted so a GET response can be posted back unchanged.|
|» » rampScheduleId|body|object|false|Read-only; ignored on write. Accepted so a GET response can be posted back unchanged.|
|» » scheduleType|body|object|false|Read-only; ignored on write. Accepted so a GET response can be posted back unchanged.|
|» » prerequisites|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » » id|body|string|true|Feature ID|

|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Resource created|Inline|
|202|Accepted|Held until a person confirms it in GrowthBook. Poll the Location until the confirmation completes.|[ConfirmationHeld](#schemaconfirmationheld)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="create-a-single-feature-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|feature|[FeatureV2](#schemafeaturev2)|true|none|none|

Status Code **422**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|message|string|true|none|none|
|code|string|true|none|none|
|details|[ApiErrorUnscopedRuleDetails](#schemaapierrorunscopedruledetails)|true|none|none|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|code|unscoped_rule|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Location|string||The confirmation to poll|
|202|Retry-After|integer||Seconds to wait before polling|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, basicAuth
</aside>

## Get a single feature

<a id="opIdgetFeatureV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/features/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/features/{id}`

<h3 id="get-a-single-feature-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The id of the requested resource|
|withRevisions|query|string|false|Also return feature revisions (all, draft, or published statuses)|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|withRevisions|all|
|withRevisions|drafts|
|withRevisions|published|
|withRevisions|none|

`POST /v2/features/{id}`

Updates the Feature Flag and immediately publishes a new revision. The caller needs Edit access in the Feature Flag's Project and Publish access for every affected environment. When approval is required, use the revision endpoints instead, unless the caller can bypass draft approvals.

Other top-level fields are patch-merged: omit a field to leave it unchanged. The `rules` field, when supplied, replaces the entire `rules` array in one operation. To preserve existing rules, fetch the Feature Flag, update the returned `rules` array, and send the complete array back. Safe-rollout rules round-trip through `safeRolloutId`; use `POST /v2/features/:id/revisions/:version/rules` to create new ones.

This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» allowUnscopedRules|body|boolean|false|When the organization requires rules to target specific environments or Projects, set to true to save a rule that applies to All Environments and All Projects. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Deletes a single feature

<a id="opIddeleteFeatureV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/features/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/features/{id}`

Permanently deletes a Feature Flag and all of its revisions. The caller needs Archive & delete access. Deleting a live Feature Flag also requires Publish access for every environment where it is enabled and the organization setting "REST API always bypasses approval requirements". Otherwise, archive the Feature Flag before deleting it.

## Toggle a feature in one or more environments

<a id="opIdtoggleFeatureV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/features/string/toggle \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "reason": "string",
    "comment": "string",
    "environments": {
      "property1": true,
      "property2": true
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v2/features/{id}/toggle`

Enables or disables a Feature Flag in one or more environments and immediately publishes the change. The caller needs Publish access for every environment in the request. When approval is required, use a draft revision instead, unless the caller can bypass draft approvals.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "reason": "string",
  "comment": "string",
  "environments": {
    "property1": true,
    "property2": true
  }
}
```

## Revert a feature to a specific revision

<a id="opIdrevertFeatureV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/features/string/revert \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "revision": 0,
    "comment": "string",
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`POST /v2/features/{id}/revert`

Restores a previously published revision and immediately publishes the result as a new revision. The caller needs Revert access for every affected environment. When approval is required, the request is allowed only if the caller holds the `FlagsBypassApprovals` policy, or the organization enables either "REST API always bypasses approval requirements" or "Allow reverts without approval".

If the restored values no longer match the Feature Flag's current value type or JSON schema, or restoring an archived state would archive a flag that live flags or experiments still depend on, the API returns 422 with `warnings`. Send `"ignoreWarnings": true` to acknowledge those warnings and continue.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "revision": 0,
  "comment": "string",
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="revert-a-feature-to-a-specific-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The id of the requested resource|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» revision|body|number|true|none|
|» comment|body|string|false|none|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Get stale status for one or more features

<a id="opIdgetFeatureStaleV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/stale-features?ids=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/stale-features`

<h3 id="get-stale-status-for-one-or-more-features-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ids|query|string|true|Comma-separated list of feature IDs (URL-encoded if needed). Example: `my_feature,another_feature`<br>|

> 200 Response

```json

        },

          "isStale": true,
          "reason": "no-rules",
          "evaluatesTo": "string",
          "tempRollout": "temp-rollout"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

<h1 id="growthbook-rest-api-feature-revisions-v2">feature-revisions-v2</h1>

Draft revisions for feature flags, including rules, scheduling, and approval workflows.

Revision `rules` is a flat array with per-rule scope fields.

## List revisions across all features

<a id="opIdlistRevisionsV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/feature-revisions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/feature-revisions`

Returns a paginated list of feature revisions across all features in the organization. Use the `featureId` query parameter to filter to a single feature. Revision `rules` is a flat array with per-rule scope.

<h3 id="list-revisions-across-all-features-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of items to return|
|offset|query|integer|false|How many items to skip (use in conjunction with limit for pagination)|
|skipPagination|query|string \| boolean|false|If true, return all matching items and ignore limit/offset.<br>Self-hosted only. Has no effect unless API_ALLOW_SKIP_PAGINATION is set to true or 1.|
|featureId|query|string|false|none|
|status|query|string \| [string]|false|Filter by revision status. Single value, comma-separated list, repeated params (?status=draft&status=approved), or `all-drafts` shorthand for all active-draft statuses (draft, pending-review, approved, changes-requested).|
|author|query|string|false|none|
|mine|query|string \| boolean|false|If true, return only revisions authored by or contributed to by the calling user.|
|archived|query|string \| boolean|false|Whether to include revisions for archived features. Defaults to `false` (non-archived features only). Pass `true` to include revisions for archived features alongside non-archived ones.|

## List revisions for a feature

<a id="opIdgetFeatureRevisionsV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/features/string/revisions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/features/{id}/revisions`

Returns a paginated list of revisions for this feature, sorted newest-first. Revision `rules` is a flat array with per-rule scope.

<h3 id="list-revisions-for-a-feature-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The id of the requested resource|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of items to return|
|offset|query|integer|false|How many items to skip (use in conjunction with limit for pagination)|
|skipPagination|query|string \| boolean|false|If true, return all matching items and ignore limit/offset.<br>Self-hosted only. Has no effect unless API_ALLOW_SKIP_PAGINATION is set to true or 1.|
|status|query|string \| [string]|false|Filter by revision status. Single value, comma-separated list, repeated params (?status=draft&status=approved), or `all-drafts` shorthand for all active-draft statuses (draft, pending-review, approved, changes-requested).|
|author|query|string|false|none|
|mine|query|string \| boolean|false|If true, return only revisions authored by or contributed to by the calling user. Needs a personal access token, or an organization API key that assumes a named member's role. Mutually exclusive with `author`.|

|offset|integer|true|none|none|
|count|integer|true|none|none|
|total|integer|true|none|none|
|hasMore|boolean|true|none|none|
|nextOffset|integer \| null|true|none|none|
|» *anyOf*|integer|false|none|none|
|» *anyOf*|null|false|none|none|

## Create a draft revision

<a id="opIdpostFeatureRevisionV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/features/string/revisions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "comment": "string",
    "title": "string",
    "ignoreWarnings": true
  }'
```

`POST /v2/features/{id}/revisions`

Creates a new draft revision branched from the current live revision.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comment": "string",
  "title": "string",
  "ignoreWarnings": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-draft-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|overrideDraftLimit|query|string \| boolean|false|If the organization caps concurrent drafts per feature (`maxConcurrentDrafts` setting), requests at or over the cap are rejected with a 409. Pass `true` to create the draft anyway. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» comment|body|string|false|Markdown. What changed and why, for reviewers.|
|» title|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`).|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Get the most recent active draft revision

<a id="opIdgetFeatureRevisionLatestV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/features/string/revisions/latest \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/features/{id}/revisions/latest`

Returns the most recently updated active draft revision for the feature. Returns 404 if no matching draft exists. Filter by status, author, or use `mine=true` to scope to the calling user's own drafts.

<h3 id="get-the-most-recent-active-draft-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|mine|query|string \| boolean|false|If true, return only the most recent active draft authored by or contributed to by the calling user.|
|status|query|string \| [string]|false|Filter by revision status. Single value, comma-separated list, repeated params (?status=draft&status=approved), or `all-drafts` shorthand for all active-draft statuses (draft, pending-review, approved, changes-requested).|
|author|query|string|false|Filter to drafts created by this user (userId).|

## Diff a revision against another revision

<a id="opIdgetFeatureRevisionDiffV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/features/string/revisions/0/diff \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/diff`

Returns a schema-keyed JSON diff between this revision and a baseline. The same shapes the in-app review surface produces under `Copy as → Minimal JSON` / `Full JSON`: `minimal` lists only what changed (with id-keyed arrays bucketed into added/removed/modified items and reorder detection), while `full` returns the complete before/after content of the revision. Lifecycle fields (version, status, comment, date, createdBy, publishedBy) are excluded from the diff body and echoed via `from` / `to` instead. Defaults to diffing against the revision's own `baseVersion`; pass `?base=live` to diff against the current live revision, or `?base=<version>` for an arbitrary historical one.

<h3 id="diff-a-revision-against-another-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|format|query|string|false|`minimal` (default) returns only what changed, with id-keyed arrays bucketed into added/removed/modified items. `full` returns the complete before/after content of the revision.|
|base|query|string \| integer|false|Compare against: `baseVersion` (default — the revision's own `baseVersion`, matches the in-app review view), `live` (the currently-live revision), or an integer version (an arbitrary historical revision).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|format|minimal|
|format|full|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "diff": {
    "name": "string",
    "type": "feature",
    "from": 0,
    "to": 0,
    "changes": [
      {
        "field": "string",
        "change": "added",
        "property1": null,
        "property2": null
      }
    ],
    "supplemental": [
      {
        "name": "string",
        "type": "string",
        "change": "added",
        "property1": null,
        "property2": null
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Set the default value in a draft revision

<a id="opIdputFeatureRevisionDefaultValueV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/features/string/revisions/0/default-value \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "defaultValue": "string",
    "defaultValueConfig": "string",
    "revisionTitle": "string",
    "revisionComment": "string",
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/default-value`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "defaultValue": "string",
  "defaultValueConfig": "string",
  "revisionTitle": "string",
  "revisionComment": "string",
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="set-the-default-value-in-a-draft-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer \| string|true|none|
|skipSchemaValidation|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `skipSchemaValidation` in the request body instead.|
|ignoreWarnings|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `ignoreWarnings` in the request body instead.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» defaultValue|body|string|true|New default value. In Config mode (feature has `baseConfig`), the default must be exactly a config with no overrides: send `"{}"` to use `baseConfig`, or set `defaultValueConfig` to point at a descendant.|
|» defaultValueConfig|body|string \| null|false|Key of a config within the feature's `baseConfig` family that the default value resolves to (the base itself or a descendant). The default is exactly that config with no overrides; pass `null` to use `baseConfig`. Do not embed `@config:` in `defaultValue` — use this field.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» revisionTitle|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`). Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» revisionComment|body|string|false|Markdown. What changed and why, for reviewers. Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Set feature-level prerequisites in a draft revision

<a id="opIdputFeatureRevisionPrerequisitesV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/features/string/revisions/0/prerequisites \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "prerequisites": [
      {
        "id": "string"
      }
    ],
    "revisionTitle": "string",
    "revisionComment": "string",
    "ignoreWarnings": true
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/prerequisites`

Sets the feature-level prerequisites for this revision. Each prerequisite must be a boolean feature flag; the gate is always 'prerequisite flag is on'. The condition is applied automatically — only the flag ID is required.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "prerequisites": [
    {
      "id": "string"
    }
  ],
  "revisionTitle": "string",
  "revisionComment": "string",
  "ignoreWarnings": true
}
```

<h3 id="set-feature-level-prerequisites-in-a-draft-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer \| string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» prerequisites|body|[object]|true|List of prerequisite boolean flags. When any prerequisite flag is off for a user, this flag returns its defaultValue for that user.|
|» » id|body|string|true|ID of a boolean feature flag|
|» revisionTitle|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`). Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» revisionComment|body|string|false|Markdown. What changed and why, for reviewers. Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

`POST /v2/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/rules`

Appends a new rule to the revision's rule list. Supply `allEnvironments: true` on the rule to target all environments, or `environments: [...]` to scope to specific ones.

**Scheduling:** For `force` and `rollout` rules, attach a schedule via `rampSchedule` (multi-step ramp) or `schedule` (simple start/end window) — these create standalone ramp actions and set `pendingRamp: "create"` on the rule. For `experiment-ref` and `safe-rollout` rules, only `schedule` is supported and is stored as legacy schedule fields on the rule itself (`rampSchedule` is not available for these rule types).

`PUT /v2/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/rules/{ruleId}`

Patches fields on an existing rule (identified by `ruleId`). The rule `type` cannot be changed. Scope can be updated via `allEnvironments` / `environments` patch fields.

**Scheduling:** For `force` and `rollout` rules, update the schedule via `rampSchedule` (multi-step ramp) or `schedule` (simple start/end window) — these manage standalone ramp actions and set `pendingRamp: "create"` on the rule. For `experiment-ref` and `safe-rollout` rules, only `schedule` is supported and updates legacy schedule fields on the rule itself (`rampSchedule` is not available for these rule types).

|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» allowUnscopedRules|body|boolean|false|When the organization requires rules to target specific environments or Projects, set to true to save a rule that applies to All Environments and All Projects. ## Delete a rule from a draft revision

<a id="opIddeleteFeatureRevisionRuleV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/features/string/revisions/0/rules/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "revisionTitle": "string",
    "revisionComment": "string",
    "ignoreWarnings": true
  }'
```

`DELETE /v2/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/rules/{ruleId}`

Removes the rule from the revision. Any pending ramp actions for this rule are also cleared.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "revisionTitle": "string",
  "revisionComment": "string",
  "ignoreWarnings": true
}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-rule-from-a-draft-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer \| string|true|none|
|ruleId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» revisionTitle|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`). Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» revisionComment|body|string|false|Markdown. What changed and why, for reviewers. Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

`POST /v2/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/rules/reorder`

bearerAuth, basicAuth

`PUT /v2/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/rules/{ruleId}/ramp-schedule`

Queues a revision-controlled ramp action for this rule. If the rule already has a live ramp schedule, this stores an `update` action applied on publish; otherwise it stores a `create` action. No live schedule config changes are applied immediately by this endpoint.

You can build the ramp from a template (`templateId`) and set the rollback anchor (`startState`) in the same request — e.g. pull in a template and pass `startState: { "coverage": 0 }` so a rollback returns the rule to 0%.

## Remove ramp schedule from a rule

<a id="opIddeleteFeatureRevisionRuleRampScheduleV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/features/string/revisions/0/rules/string/ramp-schedule \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "revisionTitle": "string",
    "revisionComment": "string",
    "ignoreWarnings": true
  }'
```

`DELETE /v2/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/rules/{ruleId}/ramp-schedule`

Clears any pending ramp action for this rule. If a live ramp schedule exists, queues a detach that removes it on publish — the rule will show `pendingRamp: "detach"`. If only a pending create exists, it is removed and `pendingRamp` is cleared.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "revisionTitle": "string",
  "revisionComment": "string",
  "ignoreWarnings": true
}
```

<h3 id="remove-ramp-schedule-from-a-rule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer \| string|true|none|
|ruleId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» revisionTitle|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`). Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» revisionComment|body|string|false|Markdown. What changed and why, for reviewers. Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Request review for a draft revision

<a id="opIdpostFeatureRevisionRequestReviewV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/features/string/revisions/0/request-review \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "comment": "string",
    "autoPublishOnApproval": true,
    "scheduledPublishAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "scheduledPublishLockEdits": true,
    "scheduledPublishLockOthers": true
  }'
```

`POST /v2/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/request-review`

Moves the draft into the `pending-review` state and notifies reviewers.

Set `autoPublishOnApproval` to `true` to publish the revision automatically the moment it is approved (GitHub auto-merge model). This requires the org to have auto-publish-on-approval enabled for the feature and the caller to have publish permission; the auto-publish then executes with the caller's authority.

Set `scheduledPublishAt` to a future ISO date-time to defer the auto-publish until that date (it still also requires approval when review is required). Use `scheduledPublishLockEdits` to freeze edits to this draft while the schedule is pending, and `scheduledPublishLockOthers` to block publishing other drafts of this feature in the meantime.

Neither can be set on a draft whose rules would take a draft experiment live, since an automatic publish doesn't start the experiment. Schedule the experiment's start instead; starting it publishes the draft.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comment": "string",
  "autoPublishOnApproval": true,
  "scheduledPublishAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "scheduledPublishLockEdits": true,
  "scheduledPublishLockOthers": true
}
```

<h3 id="request-review-for-a-draft-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» comment|body|string|false|Markdown. What changed and why, for reviewers. Replaces the draft's comment; leaving it out clears it.|
|» autoPublishOnApproval|body|boolean|false|none|
|» scheduledPublishAt|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» scheduledPublishLockEdits|body|boolean|false|none|
|» scheduledPublishLockOthers|body|boolean|false|none|

## Schedule (or cancel) a deferred publish for a draft revision

<a id="opIdpostFeatureRevisionSchedulePublishV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/features/string/revisions/0/schedule-publish \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "scheduledPublishAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true,
    "lockEdits": true,
    "lockOthers": true,
    "bypassApproval": true
  }'
```

`POST /v2/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/schedule-publish`

Schedules the draft to publish on or after `scheduledPublishAt`. When approval is required, publishing waits until the draft is also approved. Send `scheduledPublishAt: null` to cancel the schedule.

Set `lockEdits` to prevent content changes while the schedule is pending; rebasing remains allowed. Set `lockOthers` to prevent other drafts of this Feature Flag from being published until this schedule runs or is canceled. The caller needs Publish access, and that access is checked again when the schedule runs. A caller with Bypass draft approvals access can schedule an unapproved draft by sending `bypassApproval: true`. That schedule must be canceled and recreated before it can be changed, and a later edit that would reset an approval also drops the bypass.

A draft whose rules would take a draft experiment live can't be scheduled, since a scheduled publish doesn't start the experiment. Schedule the experiment's start instead; starting it publishes the draft.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "scheduledPublishAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true,
  "lockEdits": true,
  "lockOthers": true,
  "bypassApproval": true
}
```

<h3 id="schedule-or-cancel-a-deferred-publish-for-a-draft-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» scheduledPublishAt|body|string(date-time) \| null|true|When to publish, as an RFC3339 timestamp (e.g. `2026-01-31T09:00:00Z` or `2026-01-31T02:00:00-07:00`), or `null` to cancel a pending schedule.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» lockEdits|body|boolean|false|none|
|» lockOthers|body|boolean|false|none|
|» bypassApproval|body|boolean|false|none|

## Submit a review on a draft revision

<a id="opIdpostFeatureRevisionSubmitReviewV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/features/string/revisions/0/submit-review \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "comment": "string",
    "action": "approve",
    "skipAutoPublish": true
  }'
```

`POST /v2/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/submit-review`

Submits an `approve`, `request-changes`, or `comment` review on the draft. The verdict belongs to whoever the request acts as; see [Naming who asked](/api/introduction#naming-who-asked). No one can rule on a draft they created. Contributors cannot approve their own drafts when `blockSelfApproval` is enabled.

When `action` is `approve` and the revision has `autoPublishOnApproval` enabled, the revision is automatically published after approval. The response includes `autoPublished: true` when this happens. Pass `skipAutoPublish: true` to approve without triggering auto-publish.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comment": "string",
  "action": "approve",
  "skipAutoPublish": true
}
```

<h3 id="submit-a-review-on-a-draft-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» comment|body|string|false|Markdown. Why you approved, requested changes or commented.|
|» action|body|string|false|`approve`, `request-changes` or `comment`. Defaults to `comment`, which doesn't change whether the draft is approved.|
|» skipAutoPublish|body|boolean|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|approve|
|» action|request-changes|
|» action|comment|

## Recall a review request (revert to draft)

<a id="opIdpostFeatureRevisionRecallReviewV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/features/string/revisions/0/recall-review \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{}'
```

`POST /v2/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/recall-review`

Retracts the review request, returning the revision from `pending-review`, `changes-requested`, or `approved` back to `draft`. Allowed for any user with draft-management permission on the feature (the same permission required to request review), not only the original requester. Existing review log entries are preserved as audit history but any in-flight reviewer verdicts (Approved / Requested Changes) submitted during this review cycle no longer count — submitting a fresh `request-review` starts a new cycle.

> Body parameter

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="recall-a-review-request-revert-to-draft-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|

## Undo a reviewer's own review verdict

<a id="opIdpostFeatureRevisionUndoReviewV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/features/string/revisions/0/undo-review \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{}'
```

`POST /v2/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/undo-review`

Reviewer retracts their own verdict. The verdict belongs to whoever the request acts as; see [Naming who asked](/api/introduction#naming-who-asked). No one can rule on a draft they created. The revision status rewinds to the state implied by the remaining active verdicts from other reviewers: any outstanding `Requested Changes` → `changes-requested`, else any outstanding `Approved` → `approved`, else `pending-review`. Existing review comments are preserved. If the retraction resolves the revision to `approved` and auto-publish-on-approval is armed, the revision is published.

> Body parameter

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="undo-a-reviewers-own-review-verdict-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|

## Get merge status for a draft revision

<a id="opIdgetFeatureRevisionMergeStatusV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/features/string/revisions/0/merge-status \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/merge-status`

Runs the three-way merge between the draft and the current live version without applying it. Conflicts are granular: each conflicting field gets its own key, and rules conflict individually (`rules.<ruleId>`, plus `rules.order` for competing reorders). Pass the returned `liveVersion` as `expectedLiveVersion` when rebasing. Also reports `rebaseRequired` so callers can detect ahead of time whether the publish endpoint will block until the draft is rebased.

<h3 id="get-merge-status-for-a-draft-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "liveVersion": 0,
  "draftDateUpdated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "conflicts": [
    {
      "name": "string",
      "key": "string",
      "resolved": true,
      "base": "string",
      "live": "string",
      "revision": "string"
    }
  ],
  "result": {
    "defaultValue": "string",
    "rules": [
      null
    ],
    "environmentsEnabled": {
      "property1": true,
      "property2": true
    },
    "prerequisites": [
      {
        "id": "string",
        "condition": "string"
      }
    ],
    "archived": true,
    "metadata": {
      "releaseType": "string",
      "riskLevel": "string",
      "property1": null,
      "property2": null
    },
    "holdout": {
      "id": "string",
      "value": "string"
    }
  },
  "rebaseRequired": true
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response|Inline|

|rebaseRequired|boolean|true|none|Whether the draft must be rebased before it can be published. This is true when the merge has conflicts, or when the organization requires rebasing and the draft or its approval is out of date. If there are no conflicts, a caller with Bypass draft approvals access can send `ignoreWarnings: true` to force-publish instead.|

## Preview a rebase without applying it

<a id="opIdpostFeatureRevisionRebasePreviewV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/features/string/revisions/0/rebase/preview \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "conflictResolutions": {
      "property1": "overwrite",
      "property2": "overwrite"
    },
    "expectedLiveVersion": 0,
    "expectedDraftDateUpdated": "string",
    "ignoreWarnings": true
  }'
```

`POST /v2/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/rebase/preview`

Dry-run of the rebase: runs the same three-way merge with the supplied `conflictResolutions` and returns every conflict (resolved and unresolved) plus the merged result once all are resolved — without modifying the draft. Use it to iterate on resolutions before committing them via the rebase endpoint.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "conflictResolutions": {
    "property1": "overwrite",
    "property2": "overwrite"
  },
  "expectedLiveVersion": 0,
  "expectedDraftDateUpdated": "string",
  "ignoreWarnings": true
}
```

<h3 id="preview-a-rebase-without-applying-it-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» conflictResolutions|body|object|false|Map of conflict key → resolution. Keys come from the returned conflicts: `defaultValue`, `prerequisites`, `archived`, `holdout`, `environmentsEnabled.<env>`, `metadata.<field>`, `rules.<ruleId>`, and `rules.order`. `overwrite` keeps the draft's version of that item; `discard` keeps live's. The blanket `rules` key applies one strategy to all rule-level conflicts.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» expectedLiveVersion|body|integer|false|Optimistic-concurrency guard: the live version the resolutions were authored against (as returned by merge-status or rebase preview). If live has since moved, the request fails with `409` instead of applying resolutions to different conflicts.|
|» expectedDraftDateUpdated|body|string|false|Optimistic-concurrency guard for the draft side: the draft's `draftDateUpdated` timestamp as returned by merge-status or rebase preview. If the draft has been modified since (e.g. by a co-author), the request fails with `409` instead of applying resolutions against changed draft content.|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

|---|---|
|» » **additionalProperties**|overwrite|
|» » **additionalProperties**|discard|

## Rebase a draft revision onto the current live version

<a id="opIdpostFeatureRevisionRebaseV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/features/string/revisions/0/rebase \

    "expectedDraftDateUpdated": "string",

  }'
```

`POST /v2/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/rebase`

Updates the draft's base revision to match the currently-live revision, applying the draft's changes on top. Supply `conflictResolutions` to resolve conflicting items individually — including per-rule (`rules.<ruleId>`) and rule-order (`rules.order`) conflicts. Supply `expectedLiveVersion` and/or `expectedDraftDateUpdated` (both returned by merge-status and rebase preview) to fail fast with `409` if either side changes between conflict review and submission. Unresolved conflicts also respond with `409`.

> Body parameter

```json
{

    "property1": "overwrite",
    "property2": "overwrite"
  },
  "expectedLiveVersion": 0,
  "expectedDraftDateUpdated": "string",
  "ignoreWarnings": true
}
```

Keys come from the returned conflicts: `defaultValue`, `prerequisites`, `archived`, `holdout`, `environmentsEnabled.<env>`, `metadata.<field>`, `rules.<ruleId>`, and `rules.order`. `overwrite` keeps the draft's version of that item; `discard` keeps live's. The blanket `rules` key applies one strategy to all rule-level conflicts.|

|» expectedLiveVersion|body|integer|false|Optimistic-concurrency guard: the live version the resolutions were authored against (as returned by merge-status or rebase preview). If live has since moved, the request fails with `409` instead of applying resolutions to different conflicts.|
|» expectedDraftDateUpdated|body|string|false|Optimistic-concurrency guard for the draft side: the draft's `draftDateUpdated` timestamp as returned by merge-status or rebase preview. If the draft has been modified since (e.g. by a co-author), the request fails with `409` instead of applying resolutions against changed draft content.|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
