## Publish a draft revision

<a id="opIdpostFeatureRevisionPublishV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/features/string/revisions/0/publish \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "comment": "string",
    "bypassApproval": true,
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`POST /v2/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/publish`

Publishes the draft and makes its changes live. The caller needs Publish access for every affected environment. When approval is required, the draft must be approved unless the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. If the organization requires rebasing, an out-of-date draft must be rebased first; an authorized caller can instead send `ignoreWarnings: true` to force-publish it. Any pending ramp actions in `pendingRamp` are applied as part of the same operation. A 422 response lists every blocking gate and the available resolution.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comment": "string",
  "bypassApproval": true,
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="publish-a-draft-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|skipSchemaValidation|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `skipSchemaValidation` in the request body instead.|
|ignoreWarnings|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `ignoreWarnings` in the request body instead.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» comment|body|string|false|Note recorded in the audit log for this publish. Also becomes the draft's comment if the draft has none; otherwise the existing draft comment is kept.|
|» bypassApproval|body|boolean|false|Deprecated and ignored. Approval is bypassed automatically when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access for this resource or when the organization enables the REST API approval bypass. Otherwise, the revision must be approved before it can be published.|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Reopen a discarded revision as a draft

<a id="opIdpostFeatureRevisionReopenV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

  -X POST \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

  -d '{}'
```

`POST /v2/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/reopen`

Returns a `discarded` revision to `draft` status so it can be edited, reviewed, and published. Prior review state is not restored — the draft must go back through review if approvals are required.

```json
{}
```

## Revert the feature to a prior revision

<a id="opIdpostFeatureRevisionRevertV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v2/features/string/revisions/0/revert \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "strategy": "draft",
    "comment": "string",
    "title": "string",
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`POST /v2/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/revert`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "strategy": "draft",
  "comment": "string",
  "title": "string",
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="revert-the-feature-to-a-prior-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» strategy|body|string|false|none|
|» comment|body|string|false|Markdown. What changed and why, for reviewers.|
|» title|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`).|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» strategy|draft|
|» strategy|publish|

|202|Location|string||The confirmation to poll|
|202|Retry-After|integer||Seconds to wait before polling|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, basicAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="growthbook-rest-api-features">features</h1>

Control your feature flags programmatically.

**These are v1 endpoints.** New integrations should use the v2 Feature Flags endpoints, which expose a unified per-rule environment scope instead of per-environment rule arrays.

## Get all features

<a id="opIdlistFeatures"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/features \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/features`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated.** Use [GET /v2/features](#operation/listFeaturesV2) instead.

Returns features with pagination. The skipPagination query parameter is
honored only when API_ALLOW_SKIP_PAGINATION is set (self-hosted deployments).


<h3 id="get-all-features-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of items to return|
|offset|query|integer|false|How many items to skip (use in conjunction with limit for pagination)|
|projectId|query|string|false|Filter by project id|
|clientKey|query|string|false|Filter by a SDK connection's client key|
|skipPagination|query|string \| boolean|false|If true, return all matching items and ignore limit/offset.<br>Self-hosted only. Has no effect unless API_ALLOW_SKIP_PAGINATION is set to true or 1.|

<h3 id="create-a-single-feature-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» id|body|string|true|Unique, permanent key, shown as the Feature Flag's name in the UI and used in code. Keep it short. If `featureRegexValidator` in `GET /api/v1/settings` is set, follow it (`featureKeyExample` shows the format); otherwise use kebab-case (e.g. `checkout-express-pay`). Put context in `description`.|
|» archived|body|boolean|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|Markdown. What the Feature Flag gates and why, rollout plan, and links. Put context here, not in the key.|
|» owner|body|string|false|The userId or email address of the owner. If an email address is provided, it will be used to look up the userId of the matching organization member. If an ID is provided, it will be validated as existing in the organization. When omitted, it defaults to the requesting member: a personal access token's owner, or the member an organization API key assumes. An organization API key acting as itself must send it, or the request fails with a 400.|
|» project|body|string|false|An associated project ID|
|» targetingAllProjects|body|boolean|false|Make this feature discoverable in — and served to — every project, beyond its primary `project`. Requires the `targetFeatures` permission (FlagsTarget policy) unscoped to any project. Governance stays with `project`.|
|» targetingProjects|body|[string]|false|Secondary project IDs this feature is targeted in and served to, beyond its primary `project`. Adding a project requires the `targetFeatures` permission (FlagsTarget policy) in that project. Governance stays with `project`.|
|» valueType|body|string|true|The data type of the feature payload. Boolean by default.|
|» defaultValue|body|string|true|Default value when feature is enabled. Type must match `valueType`. In Config mode (`baseConfig` set) this is the JSON override patch merged on top of the config.|
|» baseConfig|body|string \| null|false|Key of the config backing this flag ("Config mode"). Requires `valueType: "json"` and a live config; `defaultValue` and rule values become override patches on top. null or omitted for a plain flag.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags for filtering and grouping. Use these instead of encoding groups in names.|
|» environments|body|object|false|Settings for each environment, keyed by environment ID. Any environment you leave out is enabled or disabled per that environment's "Default state for new features" setting.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|true|none|
|» » » rules|body|[object]|true|none|
|» » » » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » » » allProjects|body|boolean|false|When true (default), the rule applies to every project the feature is delivered to. When false, `projects` scopes it.|
|» » » » projects|body|[string]|false|Project IDs this rule is scoped to when `allProjects` is false. An empty array scopes the rule to no project.|
|» » » » rampScheduleId|body|object|false|Read-only; ignored on write. Accepted so a GET response can be posted back unchanged.|
|» » » » scheduleType|body|object|false|Read-only; ignored on write. Accepted so a GET response can be posted back unchanged.|
|» » » » description|body|string|false|Short note on why the rule exists (e.g. `Beta testers only`).|
|» » » » condition|body|string|false|Applied to everyone by default.|
|» » » » savedGroups|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » » » » match|body|string|true|none|
|» » » » » ids|body|[string]|true|none|
|» » » » savedGroupTargeting|body|[object]|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated — use `savedGroups`. Accepted so a GET response can be posted back unchanged; `savedGroups` takes precedence if both are sent.|
|» » » » » matchType|body|string|true|none|
|» » » » » savedGroups|body|[string]|true|none|
|» » » » prerequisites|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » » » » id|body|string|true|Feature ID|
|» » » » » condition|body|string|true|none|
|» » » » scheduleRules|body|[[ScheduleRule](#schemaschedulerule)]|false|none|

|» » » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Enabled by default|

|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Deletes a single feature

<a id="opIddeleteFeature"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/features/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v1/features/{id}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated.** Use [DELETE /v2/features/:id](#operation/deleteFeatureV2) instead.

Permanently deletes a Feature Flag and all of its revisions. The caller needs Archive & delete access. Deleting a live Feature Flag also requires Publish access for every environment where it is enabled and the organization setting "REST API always bypasses approval requirements". Otherwise, archive the Feature Flag before deleting it.

<h3 id="deletes-a-single-feature-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The id of the requested resource|

```json
  "deletedId": "feature-123"
}
```

```json
    },

}
```

## Toggle a feature in one or more environments

<a id="opIdtoggleFeature"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/features/string/toggle \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "reason": "string",
    "comment": "string",
    "environments": {
      "property1": true,
      "property2": true
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v1/features/{id}/toggle`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated.** Use [POST /v2/features/:id/toggle](#operation/toggleFeatureV2) instead.

Enables or disables a Feature Flag in one or more environments and immediately publishes the change. The caller needs Publish access for every environment in the request. When approval is required, use a draft revision instead, unless the caller can bypass draft approvals.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "reason": "string",
  "comment": "string",
  "environments": {
    "property1": true,
    "property2": true
  }
}
```

|body|body|object|true|none|
|» reason|body|string|false|none|
|» comment|body|string|false|Comment to record on the revision this toggle publishes, when it changes any environment. Defaults to "Created via REST API". (`reason` is recorded in the audit log only.)|

## Revert a feature to a specific revision

<a id="opIdrevertFeature"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/features/string/revert \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "revision": 0,
    "comment": "string",
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/features/{id}/revert`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated.** Use [POST /v2/features/:id/revert](#operation/revertFeatureV2) instead.

Restores a previously published revision and immediately publishes the result as a new revision. The caller needs Revert access for every affected environment. When approval is required, the request is allowed only if the caller holds the `FlagsBypassApprovals` policy, or the organization enables either "REST API always bypasses approval requirements" or "Allow reverts without approval".

If the restored values no longer match the Feature Flag's current value type or JSON schema, or restoring an archived state would archive a flag that live flags or experiments still depend on, the API returns 422 with `warnings`. Send `"ignoreWarnings": true` to acknowledge those warnings and continue.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "revision": 0,
  "comment": "string",
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="revert-a-feature-to-a-specific-revision-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The id of the requested resource|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» revision|body|number|true|none|
|» comment|body|string|false|none|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

<h1 id="growthbook-rest-api-feature-revisions">feature-revisions</h1>

Draft revisions for feature flags, including rules, scheduling, and approval workflows.

**These are v1 endpoints.** New integrations should use the v2 Feature Revisions endpoints.

## List feature revisions

<a id="opIdlistRevisions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/revisions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/revisions`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated.** Use [GET /v2/feature-revisions](#operation/listRevisionsV2) instead.

Returns a paginated list of feature revisions across all features in the organization. Optionally filtered by feature, status, author, and/or the calling user's involvement. Results are sorted newest-first.

<h3 id="list-feature-revisions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of items to return|
|offset|query|integer|false|How many items to skip (use in conjunction with limit for pagination)|
|skipPagination|query|string \| boolean|false|If true, return all matching items and ignore limit/offset.<br>Self-hosted only. Has no effect unless API_ALLOW_SKIP_PAGINATION is set to true or 1.|
|featureId|query|string|false|none|
|status|query|string \| [string]|false|Filter by revision status. Single value, comma-separated list, repeated params (?status=draft&status=approved), or `all-drafts` shorthand for all active-draft statuses (draft, pending-review, approved, changes-requested).|
|author|query|string|false|none|
|mine|query|string \| boolean|false|If true, return only revisions authored by or contributed to by the calling user. Needs a personal access token, or an organization API key that assumes a named member's role. Mutually exclusive with `author`.|

## Create a draft revision

<a id="opIdpostFeatureRevision"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/features/string/revisions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "comment": "string",
    "title": "string",
    "ignoreWarnings": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/features/{id}/revisions`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated.** Use [POST /v2/features/:id/revisions](#operation/postFeatureRevisionV2) instead.

Creates a new draft revision branched from the current live revision. A feature can have multiple concurrent drafts; use this to start an isolated line of edits.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comment": "string",
  "title": "string",
  "ignoreWarnings": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-draft-revision-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|overrideDraftLimit|query|string \| boolean|false|If the organization caps concurrent drafts per feature (`maxConcurrentDrafts` setting), requests at or over the cap are rejected with a 409. Pass `true` to create the draft anyway. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» comment|body|string|false|none|
|» title|body|string|false|none|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Get the most recent active draft revision

<a id="opIdgetFeatureRevisionLatest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/features/string/revisions/latest \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/features/{id}/revisions/latest`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated.** Use [GET /v2/features/:id/revisions/latest](#operation/getFeatureRevisionLatestV2) instead.

Returns the most recently updated draft revision for the feature. Returns 404 if there is no active draft. Pass `mine=true` to return the most recent draft authored by or contributed to by the calling user. Needs a personal access token, or an organization API key that assumes a named member's role.

<h3 id="get-the-most-recent-active-draft-revision-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|mine|query|string \| boolean|false|If true, return only the most recent active draft authored by or contributed to by the calling user. Needs a personal access token, or an organization API key that assumes a named member's role.|

`PUT /v1/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/metadata`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated.** Use [PUT /v2/features/:id/revisions/:version/metadata](#operation/putFeatureRevisionMetadataV2) instead.

Updates draft-level metadata (`comment`, `title`) and/or feature-level metadata (owner, project, tags, customFields, jsonSchema, etc.). Merge semantics: omitted fields are left unchanged; any provided field replaces the current value (pass an empty string/array/object to clear). Feature metadata changes are staged on the revision and applied to the feature on publish. Changing `project` requires publish permission on both the old and new project.

## Set the default value in a draft revision

<a id="opIdputFeatureRevisionDefaultValue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/features/string/revisions/0/default-value \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "defaultValue": "string",
    "revisionTitle": "string",
    "revisionComment": "string",
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/default-value`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated.** Use [PUT /v2/features/:id/revisions/:version/default-value](#operation/putFeatureRevisionDefaultValueV2) instead.

Replaces the feature's default value for this revision. The value must be a string representation matching the feature's value type (e.g. `"true"` for booleans, `42` for numbers, a JSON string for JSON features).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "defaultValue": "string",
  "revisionTitle": "string",
  "revisionComment": "string",
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="set-the-default-value-in-a-draft-revision-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer \| string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» defaultValue|body|string|true|none|
|» revisionTitle|body|string|false|none|
|» revisionComment|body|string|false|none|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Set feature-level prerequisites in a draft revision

<a id="opIdputFeatureRevisionPrerequisites"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/features/string/revisions/0/prerequisites \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "prerequisites": [
      {
        "id": "string",
        "condition": "string"
      }
    ],
    "revisionTitle": "string",
    "revisionComment": "string",
    "ignoreWarnings": true
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/prerequisites`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated.** Use [PUT /v2/features/:id/revisions/:version/prerequisites](#operation/putFeatureRevisionPrerequisitesV2) instead.

Replaces the feature's prerequisite list for this revision. Each prerequisite condition is evaluated against `{ value: <prereq-flag-value> }` at SDK eval time — use `value` as the condition key.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "prerequisites": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "condition": "string"
    }
  ],
  "revisionTitle": "string",
  "revisionComment": "string",
  "ignoreWarnings": true
}
```

<h3 id="set-feature-level-prerequisites-in-a-draft-revision-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer \| string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» prerequisites|body|[object]|true|none|
|» » id|body|string|true|none|
|» » condition|body|string|true|none|
|» revisionTitle|body|string|false|none|
|» revisionComment|body|string|false|none|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Set archived state in a draft revision

<a id="opIdputFeatureRevisionArchive"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/features/string/revisions/0/archive \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "archived": true,
    "revisionTitle": "string",
    "revisionComment": "string",
    "ignoreWarnings": true
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/archive`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated.** Use [PUT /v2/features/:id/revisions/:version/archive](#operation/putFeatureRevisionArchiveV2) instead.

Sets whether the feature is archived. Archived features are excluded from SDK payloads on publish.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "archived": true,
  "revisionTitle": "string",
  "revisionComment": "string",
  "ignoreWarnings": true
}
```

<h3 id="set-archived-state-in-a-draft-revision-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer \| string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» archived|body|boolean|true|none|
|» revisionTitle|body|string|false|none|
|» revisionComment|body|string|false|none|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

`POST /v1/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/rules`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated.** Use [POST /v2/features/:id/revisions/:version/rules](#operation/postFeatureRevisionRuleAddV2) instead, which accepts rules with unified `allEnvironments`/`environments` scope fields instead of a per-environment `environment` parameter.

Appends a new rule to the end of the rule list for the given environment. A `rule.type` of `force`, `rollout`, `experiment-ref`, or `safe-rollout` determines the accepted shape. Use `rampSchedule` for ramp configuration or `schedule` for a simple start/end window; if both are provided, `rampSchedule` wins.

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated.** Use [PUT /v2/features/:id/revisions/:version/rules/:ruleId](#operation/putFeatureRevisionRuleV2) instead, which locates rules by `ruleId` in the flat array without an `environment` parameter.

Patches fields on an existing rule. The rule `type` cannot be changed — to convert types, delete and re-add. Fields that don't apply to the current rule type are rejected.

## Delete a rule from a draft revision

<a id="opIddeleteFeatureRevisionRule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/features/string/revisions/0/rules/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "environment": "string",
    "revisionTitle": "string",
    "revisionComment": "string",
    "ignoreWarnings": true
  }'
```

`DELETE /v1/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/rules/{ruleId}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated.** Use [DELETE /v2/features/:id/revisions/:version/rules/:ruleId](#operation/deleteFeatureRevisionRuleV2) instead, which removes the rule from the flat array without an `environment` parameter.

Removes the rule from the specified environment. Any pending ramp actions on the draft for this rule are also cleared.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "environment": "string",
  "revisionTitle": "string",
  "revisionComment": "string",
  "ignoreWarnings": true
}
```

This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

<aside class="warning">

</aside>

## Remove ramp schedule from a rule

<a id="opIddeleteFeatureRevisionRuleRampSchedule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/features/string/revisions/0/rules/string/ramp-schedule \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "environment": "string",
    "revisionTitle": "string",
    "revisionComment": "string",
    "ignoreWarnings": true
  }'
```

`DELETE /v1/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/rules/{ruleId}/ramp-schedule`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated.** Use [DELETE /v2/features/:id/revisions/:version/rules/:ruleId/ramp-schedule](#operation/deleteFeatureRevisionRuleRampScheduleV2) instead.

Removes a pending ramp schedule attached by the draft. If the rule currently has a live ramp schedule, a detach action is queued and applied at publish time.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "environment": "string",
  "revisionTitle": "string",
  "revisionComment": "string",
  "ignoreWarnings": true
}
```

<h3 id="remove-ramp-schedule-from-a-rule-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer \| string|true|none|
|ruleId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» environment|body|string|false|**Deprecated.**|
|» revisionTitle|body|string|false|none|
|» revisionComment|body|string|false|none|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Submit a review on a draft revision

<a id="opIdpostFeatureRevisionSubmitReview"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/features/string/revisions/0/submit-review \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "comment": "string",
    "action": "approve",
    "skipAutoPublish": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/submit-review`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated.** Use [POST /v2/features/:id/revisions/:version/submit-review](#operation/postFeatureRevisionSubmitReviewV2) instead.

Submits an `approve`, `request-changes`, or `comment` review on the draft. The verdict belongs to whoever the request acts as; see [Naming who asked](/api/introduction#naming-who-asked). No one can rule on a draft they created. Contributors cannot approve their own drafts, but may submit comments or request changes.

When `action` is `approve` and the revision has `autoPublishOnApproval` enabled, the revision is automatically published after approval. Pass `skipAutoPublish: true` to approve without triggering auto-publish.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comment": "string",
  "action": "approve",
  "skipAutoPublish": true
}
```

<h3 id="submit-a-review-on-a-draft-revision-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» comment|body|string|false|none|
|» action|body|string|false|`approve`, `request-changes` or `comment`. Defaults to `comment`, which doesn't change whether the draft is approved.|
|» skipAutoPublish|body|boolean|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|approve|
|» action|request-changes|
|» action|comment|

## Rebase a draft revision onto the current live version

<a id="opIdpostFeatureRevisionRebase"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/features/string/revisions/0/rebase \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "conflictResolutions": {
      "property1": "overwrite",
      "property2": "overwrite"
    },
    "ignoreWarnings": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/rebase`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated.** Use [POST /v2/features/:id/revisions/:version/rebase](#operation/postFeatureRevisionRebaseV2) instead.

Updates the draft's base revision to match the currently-live revision, applying the draft's changes on top. Supply `conflictResolutions` to resolve any conflicting fields.

**Conflict key format changed for v1 clients.** The per-rule `envName.ruleId` keys used by older clients are no longer recognized. Valid keys: `defaultValue`, `prerequisites`, `archived`, `holdout`, `environmentsEnabled.<env>`, `metadata.<field>`, `rules.<ruleId>`, `rules.order`, and the blanket `rules` (applies one strategy to all rule-level conflicts). Unrecognized keys are ignored; unresolved conflicts respond with `409`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "conflictResolutions": {
    "property1": "overwrite",
    "property2": "overwrite"
  },
  "ignoreWarnings": true
}
```

<h3 id="rebase-a-draft-revision-onto-the-current-live-version-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» conflictResolutions|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » **additionalProperties**|overwrite|
|» » **additionalProperties**|discard|

## Publish a draft revision

<a id="opIdpostFeatureRevisionPublish"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/features/string/revisions/0/publish \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "comment": "string",
    "bypassApproval": true,
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/publish`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated.** Use [POST /v2/features/:id/revisions/:version/publish](#operation/postFeatureRevisionPublishV2) instead.

Publishes the draft and makes its changes live. The caller needs Publish access for every affected environment. When approval is required, the draft must be approved unless the caller has Bypass draft approvals access.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comment": "string",
  "bypassApproval": true,
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="publish-a-draft-revision-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» comment|body|string|false|none|
|» bypassApproval|body|boolean|false|Deprecated and ignored. Approval is bypassed automatically when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access for this resource or when the organization enables the REST API approval bypass. Otherwise, the revision must be approved before it can be published.|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Revert the feature to a prior revision

<a id="opIdpostFeatureRevisionRevert"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/features/string/revisions/0/revert \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "strategy": "draft",
    "comment": "string",
    "title": "string",
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/features/{id}/revisions/{version}/revert`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated.** Use [POST /v2/features/:id/revisions/:version/revert](#operation/postFeatureRevisionRevertV2) instead.

Creates a new draft (or immediately publishes) whose content matches the specified historical revision.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "strategy": "draft",
  "comment": "string",
  "title": "string",
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="revert-the-feature-to-a-prior-revision-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» strategy|body|string|false|none|
|» comment|body|string|false|none|
|» title|body|string|false|none|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» strategy|draft|
|» strategy|publish|

<h1 id="growthbook-rest-api-ramp-schedules">ramp-schedules</h1>

Multi-step rollout schedules that gradually increase feature rule traffic over time, with optional real-time monitoring. Each step supports interval timers, approval gates, and hold conditions. Monitored steps are backed by a live analysis experiment that can automatically hold, roll back, or advance the ramp based on guardrail and signal metric health.

## Get all rampSchedules

<a id="opIdlistRampSchedules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/ramp-schedules \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/ramp-schedules`

Returns all ramp schedules for the organization, with optional filters.


<h3 id="get-all-rampschedules-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of items to return|
|offset|query|integer|false|How many items to skip (use in conjunction with limit for pagination)|
|featureId|query|string|false|none|
|status|query|string|false|Filter by schedule status|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|pending|
|status|ready|
|status|running|
|status|paused|
|status|completed|
|status|rolled-back|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, basicAuth
</aside>

`POST /v1/ramp-schedules`

Creates a ramp schedule, optionally attached to a published feature rule by passing `featureId` and `ruleId` together (the target is then injected into every action). Attaching on creation skips the revision review flow, so when the organization requires review anywhere it is limited to credentials that may bypass approval. The reviewed way to attach a plan is `PUT /features/{id}/revisions/{version}/rules/{ruleId}/ramp-schedule` followed by a publish. Without a target the schedule is a free-standing skeleton in `pending` status. Requires a Pro plan or above.

## Start a ramp schedule

<a id="opIdstartRampSchedule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/ramp-schedules/string/actions/start \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v1/ramp-schedules/{id}/actions/start`

Transitions the schedule from `ready` to `running`. The schedule must have
at least one target rule attached — a schedule created without targets starts
in `pending` and moves to `ready` automatically when the first target is
attached via `/actions/add-target`.

The first step is processed immediately: interval-free steps advance right
away; interval-based steps arm a timer. Once started, use `/actions/pause`
to halt, `/actions/advance` to skip steps, or `/actions/rollback` to revert.


<h3 id="start-a-ramp-schedule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|

## Pause a ramp schedule

<a id="opIdpauseRampSchedule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/ramp-schedules/string/actions/pause \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v1/ramp-schedules/{id}/actions/pause`

Pauses a `running` schedule. Traffic percentages are frozen at their current
values; no step advancement happens while paused. Records `pausedAt` so that
interval timing can be correctly offset when the schedule resumes.

Use `/actions/resume` to continue from the same step, or `/actions/rollback`
to revert all rule effects entirely.

## Resume a paused ramp schedule

<a id="opIdresumeRampSchedule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/ramp-schedules/string/actions/resume \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v1/ramp-schedules/{id}/actions/resume`

Resumes a `paused` schedule without moving the current step. Timing anchors
(`phaseStartedAt`, `startedAt`) are shifted forward by the pause duration so
that interval-based steps continue from where they left off rather than
restarting their clock.

Does **not** advance to the next step — use `/actions/advance` if you also
want to skip the remainder of the current step.


<h3 id="resume-a-paused-ramp-schedule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

## Roll back a ramp schedule

<a id="opIdrollbackRampSchedule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/ramp-schedules/string/actions/rollback \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "reason": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/ramp-schedules/{id}/actions/rollback`

Rewinds all ramp effects (rule coverage, targeting, etc.) to the starting
position and lands in terminal `rolled-back` status. The reason is persisted
as `lastRollbackReason` (prefixed with `Manual: `) and surfaced in the UI.

This is also the correct response to a monitoring alert — when the
`/status` endpoint returns `decision: "rollback"` or signals include
`guardrail-failing`, call this endpoint with a descriptive `reason`.

From this terminal state the schedule can be brought back to `ready` via
`/actions/restart`, after which `/actions/start` will run it again.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "reason": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="roll-back-a-ramp-schedule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» reason|body|string|false|none|

## Restart a terminal ramp schedule

<a id="opIdrestartRampSchedule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/ramp-schedules/string/actions/restart \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v1/ramp-schedules/{id}/actions/restart`

Brings a `rolled-back` (or `completed`) schedule back into `running` in a
single call. Any prior start-on-date delays are cleared (`startedAt`,
`phaseStartedAt`, etc. are reset), `currentStepIndex` is normalised to
`-1`, then the same logic as `/actions/start` runs to apply start actions
and advance through immediately-eligible steps.

The rollback that preceded this already rewound rule effects to the
starting position; this endpoint does **not** re-execute that rewind for
`rolled-back` schedules. `completed` schedules are defensively rewound
first.


<h3 id="restart-a-terminal-ramp-schedule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|

## Jump to a specific step

<a id="opIdjumpRampSchedule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/ramp-schedules/string/actions/jump \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "targetStepIndex": -1
  }'
```

`POST /v1/ramp-schedules/{id}/actions/jump`

Teleports the schedule to `targetStepIndex` (forward or backward) and leaves
it `paused`. Resets timing anchors so the destination step's interval starts
fresh when the schedule is next resumed or started.

Pass `-1` to return to the pre-start position without applying rollback rule
patches — useful for resetting a non-started schedule. For a full traffic
revert, use `/actions/rollback` instead.

Accepts any non-terminal schedule status.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "targetStepIndex": -1
}
```

<h3 id="jump-to-a-specific-step-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» targetStepIndex|body|integer|true|Zero-based index of the step to jump to; -1 = pre-start|

## Complete a ramp schedule immediately

<a id="opIdcompleteRampSchedule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/ramp-schedules/string/actions/complete \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "disableRule": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/ramp-schedules/{id}/actions/complete`

Immediately applies the schedule's end-state rule patches (the equivalent
of what would happen after the last step advances normally) and marks the
schedule as `completed`, skipping any remaining steps.

Pass `disableRule: true` to also disable the linked rule (equivalent to
the cutoff-date-driven completion).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "disableRule": true
}
```

<h3 id="complete-a-ramp-schedule-immediately-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» disableRule|body|boolean|false|none|

## Approve the pending approval gate

<a id="opIdapproveStepRampSchedule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/ramp-schedules/string/actions/approve-step \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v1/ramp-schedules/{id}/actions/approve-step`

Clears whichever approval gate is currently pending on the schedule:

- **Start gate** — a schedule created with `requiresStartApproval` sits in `ready` at step -1 with its rule disabled (zero traffic). Approving starts the ramp (or, if a future `startDate` is set, arms it to start on that date).
- **Step gate** — the `holdConditions.requiresApproval` gate on the current step of a `running` schedule.

For a step gate, approval is the **final** gate: it can only be granted once every other hold has cleared. This endpoint rejects the request (`400`) if the step is not yet ready — while the interval timer is still counting down, or (for monitored steps) before fresh analysis is available or while a guardrail/health signal is failing. Poll `/status` and call this once it reports awaiting approval.

**Non-monitored steps**: once the interval has elapsed, approving clears the last hold and advances immediately, chaining through subsequent instant steps.

**Monitored steps**: approving clears the last hold and the agenda advances on its next tick (re-checking analysis first).

Different from `/actions/advance`: `approve-step` works within the normal evaluation flow and refuses to skip ahead of the interval or any other unmet gate. Use `/actions/advance` to bypass all remaining holds.

Requires update + publish (start gate) or review (step gate) permissions for the associated feature.


<h3 id="approve-the-pending-approval-gate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|

## Add a target rule to a ramp schedule

<a id="opIdaddTargetRampSchedule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/ramp-schedules/string/actions/add-target \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "featureId": "string",
    "ruleId": "string",
    "environment": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/ramp-schedules/{id}/actions/add-target`

Attaches an additional feature rule to this ramp schedule. The `ruleId`
must identify a rule that is already published and must not already be
controlled by another schedule. `environment` is accepted for backward
compatibility with pre-v2 ramps but is deprecated and no longer required.

This skips the revision review flow, so when the organization requires review
anywhere it is limited to credentials that may bypass approval. The reviewed way
to attach a plan is `PUT /features/{id}/revisions/{version}/rules/{ruleId}/ramp-schedule`
followed by a publish.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "featureId": "string",
  "ruleId": "string",
  "environment": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-target-rule-to-a-ramp-schedule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» featureId|body|string|true|none|
|» ruleId|body|string|true|none|
|» environment|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated pre-v2 disambiguator; ignored on v2 rules where `rule.id` is uniquely sufficient.|

## Remove a target rule from a ramp schedule

<a id="opIdejectTargetRampSchedule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "targetId": "string",
    "ruleId": "string",
    "environment": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/ramp-schedules/{id}/actions/eject-target`

Detaches a target rule from this ramp schedule. Identify the target either
by its `targetId` or by the `[ruleId, environment]` pair.

If this is the last target on the schedule, the schedule is deleted entirely
and the response contains `deleted: true` instead of `rampSchedule`.

```json
  "targetId": "string",
  "ruleId": "string",
  "environment": "string"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» targetId|body|string|false|Target ID (from the targets array)|
|» ruleId|body|string|false|Rule ID — use as an alternative to targetId|
|» environment|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated pre-v2 disambiguator. Optional when used with ruleId; omit on v2 ramps.|

## Advance to the next step, overriding any holds

<a id="opIdapiAdvanceRampSchedule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/ramp-schedules/string/actions/advance \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "reason": "string",
    "force": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/ramp-schedules/{id}/actions/advance`

Moves the schedule to the next step, bypassing **all** hold conditions —
interval, min sample size, and monitoring signal holds. Accepts `running`
or `paused` status; if paused, the schedule is implicitly resumed (timing
anchors recalculated) before the step moves.

**Approval gate**: if the current step has an unsatisfied
`holdConditions.requiresApproval` gate, this endpoint returns **409** by
default. Either call `/actions/approve-step` first (recommended), or pass
`force: true` to override the approval gate. `force: true` requires
`FlagsBypassApprovals` permission and is logged in the audit trail.

**Two common uses:**
- **Post-interval monitoring hold** (`decision: "hold"`, interval elapsed): the
  step timer has completed but a signal or guardrail is flagging concern. Use
  this after reviewing the `/status` health summary and deciding to accept the
  risk and proceed.
- **Hard override**: skip a step regardless of where it is in its interval or
  hold conditions (CI gate, external deployment pipeline).

When to use other actions instead:
- **`/actions/resume`** — restores a paused schedule without moving the step.
- **`/actions/approve-step`** — clears only the approval gate; other conditions
  still resolve naturally.
- **`/actions/rollback`** — preferred response when `decision: "rollback"` or
  signals include `guardrail-failing`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "reason": "string",
  "force": true
}
```

<h3 id="advance-to-the-next-step-overriding-any-holds-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» reason|body|string|false|Reason for advancing|
|» force|body|boolean|false|Bypass a pending approval gate on the current step. Requires admin-level (`FlagsBypassApprovals`) permission. When omitted or `false`, a 409 is returned if the step has an unsatisfied `holdConditions.requiresApproval` gate. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Get ramp schedule status summary

<a id="opIdgetRampScheduleStatus"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/ramp-schedules/string/status \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/ramp-schedules/{id}/status`

Returns a real-time status summary for a ramp schedule: current step, overall health decision, traffic quality, and per-metric effect sizes. Designed for CI pipeline integrations and monitoring dashboards that need a single call to determine whether it is safe to advance.

## Set ramp monitoring mode

<a id="opIdsetMonitoringModeRampSchedule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/ramp-schedules/string/actions/set-monitoring-mode \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "monitoringMode": "auto"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/ramp-schedules/{id}/actions/set-monitoring-mode`

Sets the user preference for ramp monitoring updates. In `manual` mode, automatic snapshot scheduling is disabled and operators must click Update manually. In `auto` mode, snapshots run automatically when the current step is monitored and the ramp is running.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "monitoringMode": "auto"
}
```

<h3 id="set-ramp-monitoring-mode-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» monitoringMode|body|string|true|`auto` schedules snapshots automatically while allowed by ramp state. `manual` disables agenda updates and relies on manual Update clicks.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» monitoringMode|auto|
|» monitoringMode|manual|

## Toggle automatic monitoring updates

<a id="opIdsetAutoUpdateRampSchedule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/ramp-schedules/string/actions/set-auto-update \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "enabled": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/ramp-schedules/{id}/actions/set-auto-update`

Deprecated alias for setting monitoring mode. Prefer `/actions/set-monitoring-mode`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enabled": true
}
```

<h3 id="toggle-automatic-monitoring-updates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» enabled|body|boolean|true|Legacy alias for monitoring mode (`true` => auto, `false` => manual).|

## Update ramp monitoring configuration

<a id="opIdupdateRampScheduleMonitoring"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/ramp-schedules/string/monitoring \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "datasourceId": "string",
    "guardrailMetricIds": [
      "string"
    ],
    "signalMetricIds": [
      "string"
    ],
    "updateScheduleMinutes": 10,
    "monitoringMode": "auto",
    "autoUpdate": true,
    "srmAction": "rollback",
    "noTrafficAction": "rollback",
    "noTrafficGracePeriodHours": 0.1,
    "multipleExposureAction": "rollback",
    "exposureQuery": {
      "id": "string",
      "identifierType": "string"
    },
    "exposureQueryId": "string"
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/ramp-schedules/{id}/monitoring`

Replaces the monitoring configuration. Health-action thresholds (`srmAction`, `noTrafficAction`, etc.) can be updated at any time.

Once a linked SafeRollout has started, `datasourceId`, `exposureQueryId`, the metric IDs and the snapshot cadence are all locked — stop and recreate the schedule to change the data source.

Changes to guardrail or signal metric IDs take effect on the next analysis run.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "datasourceId": "string",
  "guardrailMetricIds": [
    "string"
  ],
  "signalMetricIds": [
    "string"
  ],
  "updateScheduleMinutes": 10,
  "monitoringMode": "auto",
  "autoUpdate": true,
  "srmAction": "rollback",
  "noTrafficAction": "rollback",
  "noTrafficGracePeriodHours": 0.1,
  "multipleExposureAction": "rollback",
  "exposureQuery": {
    "id": "string",
    "identifierType": "string"
  },
  "exposureQueryId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-ramp-monitoring-configuration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» datasourceId|body|string|true|none|
|» guardrailMetricIds|body|[string]|true|none|
|» signalMetricIds|body|[string]|false|none|
|» updateScheduleMinutes|body|number \| null|false|none|

|» noTrafficAction|body|string|false|none|

|» » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» multipleExposureAction|body|string|false|none|
|» exposureQuery|body|object|false|The assignment query, grouping its ID with the identifier type analyzed on. Mutually exclusive with the deprecated `exposureQueryId`.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of one of the data source's assignment queries.|
|» » identifierType|body|string \| null|false|The identifier type to analyze on, which the query must declare. Required when selecting a different assignment query that declares several. Otherwise defaults to the current identifier type, or the query's only one. Null is treated as omitted, so a response's value can be sent back.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|

|» exposureQueryId|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: use `exposureQuery`. Rejected when selecting a different assignment query that declares several identifier types; set `exposureQuery.identifierType` instead.|

## Update ramp lockdown configuration

<a id="opIdupdateRampScheduleLockdown"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/ramp-schedules/string/lockdown \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "mode": "none"
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/ramp-schedules/{id}/lockdown`

Sets the lockdown mode. `locked` prevents other users from publishing unrelated changes to the parent feature while the ramp is running — useful when you want to ensure no external edits interfere with a live rollout. It does **not** affect the ramp's own auto-advancement or monitoring behavior; use `actions/pause` to halt the ramp itself. `none` removes the publishing restriction.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "mode": "none"
}
```

<h3 id="update-ramp-lockdown-configuration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» mode|body|string|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» mode|none|
|» mode|locked|

## Update ramp schedule steps

<a id="opIdupdateRampScheduleSteps"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/ramp-schedules/string/steps \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "steps": [
      {
        "actions": null,
        "interval": 0.1,
        "monitored": true,
        "holdConditions": {
          "minSampleSize": 1,
          "requiresApproval": true
        },
        "approvalNotes": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/ramp-schedules/{id}/steps`

Fully replaces the steps array for a ramp schedule. Only allowed when the schedule is in a non-running, non-terminal state (`ready`, `pending`, or `paused`). Pause a running schedule first; restart a terminal schedule first.

On a schedule attached to a rule this skips the revision review flow, so when the organization requires review anywhere it is limited to credentials that may bypass approval.

**Step actions** (coverage/targeting patches) are not accepted here — they change the SDK payload and must go through a feature revision draft. Existing step actions are preserved for each position. Use `PUT /v2/features/:id/revisions/:version/rules/:ruleId/ramp-schedule` to modify coverage/targeting.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "steps": [
    {
      "actions": null,
      "interval": 0.1,
      "monitored": true,
      "holdConditions": {
        "minSampleSize": 1,
        "requiresApproval": true
      },
      "approvalNotes": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-ramp-schedule-steps-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» steps|body|[object]|true|Full replacement of the steps array. Step-level coverage patches (`actions`) are intentionally excluded — those require a revision publish because they change the SDK payload. Use the revision flow to modify coverage/targeting; use this endpoint to update monitoring flags and hold conditions.|
|» » actions|body|object|false|Read-only; ignored on write. Accepted so a GET response can be posted back unchanged.|
|» » interval|body|number \| null|true|Hold duration in seconds before this step's gates are evaluated. `null` means no time gate.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» » monitored|body|boolean|false|When true, this step runs A/B traffic analysis while active. Applies only to future steps — cannot be changed on the currently executing step.|
|» » holdConditions|body|object|false|Additional gates that must clear before the step advances: `minSampleSize` and/or `requiresApproval`.|
|» » » minSampleSize|body|integer|false|none|
|» » » requiresApproval|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » approvalNotes|body|string \| null|false|Optional notes shown to approvers when the step is awaiting approval.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

## Trigger a manual monitoring update

<a id="opIdrefreshMonitoringRampSchedule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/ramp-schedules/string/actions/refresh-monitoring \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v1/ramp-schedules/{id}/actions/refresh-monitoring`

Queues a new analysis snapshot for the schedule's monitoring experiment.
The snapshot runs asynchronously — poll `GET /ramp-schedules/:id/status`
until `snapshotAt` advances to confirm results are ready.

Only available when the schedule is within its monitored step window:
- Not in a terminal state (`completed` or `rolled-back`).
- Has at least one step with `monitored: true`.
- `currentStepIndex` is within `[firstMonitoredStepIndex, lastMonitoredStepIndex]`.

Violating any condition returns **409 Conflict** with a descriptive message.

Requires the `runQueries` permission on the configured datasource (enforced via `canRunExperimentQueries`).


<h3 id="trigger-a-manual-monitoring-update-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|

## Roll back matching ramp schedules

<a id="opIdrollbackMatchingRampSchedules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/ramp-schedules/actions/rollback \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "reason": "string",
    "property1": null,
    "property2": null
  }'
```

`POST /v1/ramp-schedules/actions/rollback`

Rolls back every `running` or `paused` ramp schedule that matches the query
filters. Built for an alerting tool's webhook, such as a Datadog monitor.

Each filter takes comma-separated values and matches any of them; different
filters must all match. At least one filter is required.

Returns each matched schedule and whether the rollback was applied or skipped,
for example because the API key can't publish its Feature Flag. Unknown body
fields are ignored, so a tool can send its own payload.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "reason": "string",
  "property1": null,
  "property2": null
}
```

<h3 id="roll-back-matching-ramp-schedules-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|environment|query|[string]|false|Comma-separated environments. Matches ramps whose rules run in any of them.|
|project|query|[string]|false|Comma-separated Project ids. Matches ramps on Feature Flags in any of them.|
|tag|query|[string]|false|Comma-separated tags. Matches ramps on Feature Flags with any of them.|
|feature|query|[string]|false|Comma-separated Feature Flag ids.|
|customFields|query|object|false|Custom field values, as `customFields[<key>]=<value>`. Comma-separate several values for one key.|
|reason|query|string|false|Used when the body has no `reason`, for tools whose payload can't be changed.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» reason|body|string|false|Recorded on each ramp, prefixed with `Alert: `. Use the alert title and link.|
|» **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "rampSchedules": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "featureId": "string",
      "result": "applied",
      "message": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 202 Response

```json

  "confirmation": {
    "id": "string",
    "status": "pending",

        "action": "feature.create",

          "string"
        ]
      }
    ],

    "expiresAt": "string",
    "response": {
      "status": 0,
      "body": null
    },
    "note": "string"
  },
  "message": "string"
}
```

## Pause matching ramp schedules

<a id="opIdpauseMatchingRampSchedules"></a>

```bash
  -X POST \

  -d '{
    "reason": "string",

  }'
```

`POST /v1/ramp-schedules/actions/pause`

Pauses every `running` ramp schedule that matches the query filters. Built
for an alerting tool's webhook, such as a Datadog monitor. Each schedule stays
paused until someone calls `/actions/resume` on it.

Each filter takes comma-separated values and matches any of them; different
filters must all match. With no filters, every running schedule is paused,
for example during a site-wide outage.

Returns each matched schedule and whether the pause was applied or skipped,
for example because the API key can't publish its Feature Flag. Unknown body
fields are ignored, so a tool can send its own payload.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "reason": "string",
  "property1": null,
  "property2": null
}
```

|project|query|[string]|false|Comma-separated Project ids. Matches ramps on Feature Flags in any of them.|
|tag|query|[string]|false|Comma-separated tags. Matches ramps on Feature Flags with any of them.|
|feature|query|[string]|false|Comma-separated Feature Flag ids.|
|customFields|query|object|false|Custom field values, as `customFields[<key>]=<value>`. Comma-separate several values for one key.|
|reason|query|string|false|Used when the body has no `reason`, for tools whose payload can't be changed.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» reason|body|string|false|Recorded on each ramp, prefixed with `Alert: `. Use the alert title and link.|
