`PUT /v1/ramp-schedules/{id}`

Updates the name, steps, endActions, startDate, or cutoffDate of a ramp schedule.

Only allowed when the schedule is in `pending`, `ready`, or `paused` status.

Changing `steps`, `startActions`, `endActions`, `startDate`, or `cutoffDate` on a
schedule that is attached to a rule skips the revision review flow, so when the
organization requires review anywhere it is limited to credentials that may
bypass approval. Otherwise stage a new plan on a draft revision and publish it.

**targetId shorthand**: When providing `steps` or `endActions`, you may omit `targetId`
(or pass `"t1"`) in each action. If the schedule has exactly one active target, the server
will resolve it automatically. For schedules with multiple targets, provide the explicit
target UUID from `targets[].id`.

**Coverage on monitored steps**: See the create endpoint description for details
on how `coverage` is interpreted for monitored steps (total enrollment, not
variation-1 exposure).

|» » interval|body|number \| null|true|Hold duration in seconds before this step's gates are evaluated. null = no time gate (advance as soon as holdConditions clear).|

|» » » » coverage|body|number \| null|false|Traffic fraction (0–1). For monitored steps the rollout rule is promoted to an experiment: treatment = [0, coverage), control = [0.5, 0.5+coverage). Both arms are equal-sized and non-adjacent, so a step-up only adds new users to each arm — no existing user changes group. The REST API enforces coverage ≤ 0.5 on monitored steps so control end never exceeds 1.0. The SDK uses explicit hash ranges on bucketingV2 clients to keep bucketing stable across monitored/unmonitored transitions.|
|» » » » » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » » » » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» » » » condition|body|string \| null|false|none|

|» » » » savedGroups|body|[object] \| null|false|none|
|» » » » » *anyOf*|body|[object]|false|none|

## Delete a single rampSchedule

<a id="opIddeleteRampSchedule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/ramp-schedules/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v1/ramp-schedules/{id}`

Permanently deletes a ramp schedule. This does not undo any rule patches that
were already applied by completed steps.


<h3 id="delete-a-single-rampschedule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

<h1 id="growthbook-rest-api-data-sources">data-sources</h1>

## Get a Data Source's Information Schema

`GET /v1/data-sources/{dataSourceId}/information-schema`

Returns cached database schema metadata for a data source, including databases, schemas, and tables. The information schema is automatically created when a SQL-based data source is added. Not all data source types support information schemas.

<h3 id="get-a-data-sources-information-schema-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Short display name. Put details in `description`.|
|» description|body|string|false|Markdown. Put context here, not in the name.|
|» owner|body|string|false|The userId or email address of the owner. If an email address is provided, it will be used to look up the userId of the matching organization member. If an ID is provided, it will be validated as existing in the organization.|
|» projects|body|[string]|false|List of associated project ids|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|List of associated tags|
|» datasource|body|string|true|The datasource id|
|» userIdTypes|body|[string]|true|List of identifier columns in this table. For example, "id" or "anonymous_id"|
|» userIdColumns|body|object|false|Maps an identifier type to the column holding it, for SQL that does not alias its columns to the identifier type names, e.g. `{"user_id": "userId"}`. May also be a single-level field path into a JSON column (`properties.userId`). Unmapped types use the identifier type name as the column name.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» aggregatedFactTableSettings|body|object|false|Settings for maintaining shared daily aggregated tables (a subset of userIdTypes plus the daily update time and restate lookback window) used to speed up CUPED. Requires the data pipeline (pipeline-mode) feature.|
|» » idTypes|body|[string]|true|none|
|» » updateTime|body|object|true|none|

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The id of the requested resource|
|body|body|object|true|none|

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response|Inline|

<h3 id="get-a-single-aggregated-table-run-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|run|[AggregatedTableRun](#schemaaggregatedtablerun)|true|none|none|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, basicAuth

`POST /v1/bulk-import/facts`

Creates or updates Fact Tables, Fact Table filters, and Fact Metrics. Resources upsert by `id`. Pass `dryRun: true` to validate with zero writes. Not transactional: a live mid-loop failure returns HTTP 400 (403 for a permission failure) with write counts and `errors`.

<h3 id="bulk-import-fact-tables-filters-and-metrics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» defaultManagedBy|body|string|false|Fallback `managedBy` for Fact Tables and Fact Metrics that omit the field. Defaults to `"api"`; the dbt sync sends `"dbt"`. Filters inherit `"api"` only when the parent Fact Table is api-managed.|
|» dryRun|body|boolean|false|Validate with zero writes.|
|» factTables|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » id|body|string|true|none|
|» » data|body|object|true|none|
|» » » name|body|string|true|Short display name. Put details in `description`.|
|» » » description|body|string|false|Markdown. Put context here, not in the name.|
|» » » owner|body|string|false|The userId or email address of the owner. If an email address is provided, it will be used to look up the userId of the matching organization member. If an ID is provided, it will be validated as existing in the organization.|
|» » » projects|body|[string]|false|List of associated project ids|
|» » » tags|body|[string]|false|List of associated tags|
|» » » datasource|body|string|true|The datasource id|
|» » » userIdTypes|body|[string]|true|List of identifier columns in this table. For example, "id" or "anonymous_id"|
|» » » userIdColumns|body|object|false|Maps an identifier type to the column holding it, for SQL that does not alias its columns to the identifier type names, e.g. `{"user_id": "userId"}`. May also be a single-level field path into a JSON column (`properties.userId`). Unmapped types use the identifier type name as the column name.|
|» » » » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » » aggregatedFactTableSettings|body|object|false|Settings for maintaining shared daily aggregated tables (a subset of userIdTypes plus the daily update time and restate lookback window) used to speed up CUPED. Requires the data pipeline (pipeline-mode) feature.|
|» » » » idTypes|body|[string]|true|none|
|» » » » updateTime|body|object|true|none|
|» » » » » time|body|string|true|none|
|» » » » » timezone|body|string|true|none|
|» » » » lookbackWindow|body|integer|true|none|
|» » » » restateChunkDays|body|integer|false|none|
|» » » sql|body|string|true|The SQL query for this fact table|
|» » » timestampColumn|body|string|false|The column holding the event timestamp. Must be a date column on this fact table. Defaults to "timestamp" when unset.|
|» » » eventName|body|string|false|The event name used in SQL template variables|
|» » » columns|body|[[FactTableColumnInput](#schemafacttablecolumninput)]|false|Optional array of column definitions for this fact table. On create, columns are stored as-is. On update, columns upsert by `column`: existing columns are patched, new columns are created, and columns not included are left unchanged. Omit `datatype` to leave an existing column's type untouched; send "" to reset it for auto-detection; new columns are auto-detected when `datatype` is omitted or "". Datatype-dependent properties (e.g. `alwaysInlineFilter`) are validated once the datatype is known. Slice-related properties require an enterprise license.|
|» » » managedBy|body|string|false|Set this to "api" (or "dbt" for resources synced from dbt) to disable editing in the GrowthBook UI|

|» » » » type|body|string|true|none|
|» » » » value|body|number|false|When type is absolute, this is a finite lower bound, including zero or negative values. When type is percentile, this must be strictly between 0 and 1. Required when enabling capping or changing type; omitted values are preserved only for same-type updates.|
|» » » » ignoreZeros|body|boolean|false|If true and capping is `percentile`, zeros will be ignored when calculating the percentile.|
|» » » » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» » » windowSettings|body|object|false|Controls the conversion window for the metric|
|» » » » type|body|string|true|none|
|» » » » delayHours|body|number|false|**Deprecated.** Wait this many hours after experiment exposure before counting conversions. Ignored if delayValue is set.|
|» » » » delayValue|body|number|false|Wait this long after experiment exposure before counting conversions.|
|» » » » delayUnit|body|string|false|Default `hours`.|
|» » » » windowValue|body|number|false|none|
|» » » » windowUnit|body|string|false|Default `hours`.|
|» » » priorSettings|body|object|false|Controls the bayesian prior for the metric. If omitted, organization defaults will be used.|
|» » » » override|body|boolean|true|If false, the organization default settings will be used instead of the other settings in this object|
|» » » » proper|body|boolean|true|If true, the `mean` and `stddev` will be used, otherwise we will use an improper flat prior.|
|» » » » mean|body|number|true|The mean of the prior distribution of relative effects in proportion terms (e.g. 0.01 is 1%)|
|» » » » stddev|body|number|true|Must be > 0. The standard deviation of the prior distribution of relative effects in proportion terms.|
|» » » regressionAdjustmentSettings|body|object|false|Controls the regression adjustment (CUPED) settings for the metric|
|» » » » override|body|boolean|true|If false, the organization default settings will be used|
|» » » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Controls whether or not regression adjustment is applied to the metric|
|» » » » days|body|number|false|Number of pre-exposure days to use for the regression adjustment|
|» » » riskThresholdSuccess|body|number|false|**Deprecated.** No longer used. Accepted and ignored.|
|» » » riskThresholdDanger|body|number|false|**Deprecated.** No longer used. Accepted and ignored.|
|» » » displayAsPercentage|body|boolean|false|If true and the metric is a ratio or dailyParticipation metric, variation means will be displayed as a percentage. Defaults to true for dailyParticipation metrics and false for ratio metrics.|
|» » » minPercentChange|body|number|false|Minimum percent change to consider uplift significant, as a proportion (e.g. put 0.005 for 0.5%)|
|» » » maxPercentChange|body|number|false|Maximum percent change to consider uplift significant, as a proportion (e.g. put 0.5 for 50%)|
|» » » minSampleSize|body|number|false|none|
|» » » targetMDE|body|number|false|The percentage change that you want to reliably detect before ending an experiment, as a proportion (e.g. put 0.1 for 10%). This is used to estimate the "Days Left" for running experiments.|
|» » » managedBy|body|string|false|Set this to "api" (or "dbt" for resources synced from dbt) to disable editing in the GrowthBook UI|
|» » » metricAutoSlices|body|[string]|false|Array of slice column names that will be automatically included in metric analysis. This is an enterprise feature.|
|» » » replaces|body|[string]|false|Ids of older metrics (legacy or fact) that this metric supersedes, for example the legacy metric it was migrated from. Cannot include this metric's own id. Informational only - GrowthBook uses it to link the old and new definitions in the UI and to keep showing results from a snapshot that was created before an experiment switched to this metric. This field can only be set through the API.|
|» » » archived|body|boolean|false|Set to true to archive the metric. Archived metrics are hidden by default in the UI and excluded from new experiments.|

<h1 id="growthbook-rest-api-fact-metrics">fact-metrics</h1>

Fact Metrics are metrics built on top of Fact Table definitions

## Get all fact metrics

<a id="opIdlistFactMetrics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/fact-metrics \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/fact-metrics`

<h3 id="get-all-fact-metrics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of items to return|
|offset|query|integer|false|How many items to skip (use in conjunction with limit for pagination)|
|datasourceId|query|string|false|Filter by Data Source|
|projectId|query|string|false|Filter by project id|
|factTableId|query|string|false|Filter by Fact Table Id (for ratio metrics, only the numerator is considered)|

<h3 id="create-a-single-fact-metric-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Short display name (e.g. `Purchases per user`). Put the definition in `description`.|
|» description|body|string|false|Markdown. Put context here, not in the name.|
|» owner|body|string|false|The userId or email address of the owner. If an email address is provided, it will be used to look up the userId of the matching organization member. If an ID is provided, it will be validated as existing in the organization.|
|» projects|body|[string]|false|none|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags for filtering and grouping. Use these instead of encoding groups in names.|
|» metricType|body|string|true|none|
|» numerator|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » factTableId|body|string|true|none|
|» » column|body|string|false|Must be empty for proportion metrics and dailyParticipation metrics. Otherwise, the column name or one of the special values: '$$distinctUsers' or '$$count' (or '$$distinctDates' if metricType is 'mean' or 'ratio' or 'quantile' and quantileSettings.type is 'unit')|
|» » aggregation|body|string|false|User aggregation of selected column. Either sum or max for numeric columns; count distinct for string columns; hll merge / kll merge for pre-built sketch columns (requires data-source support); ignored for special columns. Default: sum. If you specify a string column you must explicitly specify count distinct. Not used for proportion metrics; for event quantile metrics only kll merge is applicable.|
|» » filters|body|[string]|false|**Deprecated.** Array of Fact Table Filter Ids. Deprecated, use rowFilters instead.|

|» maxPercentChange|body|number|false|Maximum percent change to consider uplift significant, as a proportion (e.g. put 0.5 for 50%)|
|» minSampleSize|body|number|false|none|
|» targetMDE|body|number|false|The percentage change that you want to reliably detect before ending an experiment, as a proportion (e.g. put 0.1 for 10%). This is used to estimate the "Days Left" for running experiments.|

This field can only be set through the API.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Resource deleted|Inline|
|202|Accepted|Held until a person confirms it in GrowthBook. Poll the Location until the confirmation completes.|[ConfirmationHeld](#schemaconfirmationheld)|

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|deletedId|string|true|none|The ID of the deleted fact metric|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Location|string||The confirmation to poll|
|202|Retry-After|integer||Seconds to wait before polling|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

</aside>

## Create a fact metric analysis

<a id="opIdpostFactMetricAnalysis"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/fact-metrics/string/analysis \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "userIdType": "string",
    "lookbackDays": 1,
    "populationType": "factTable",
    "populationId": "string",
    "additionalNumeratorFilters": [
      "string"
    ],
    "additionalDenominatorFilters": [
      "string"
    ],
    "useCache": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/fact-metrics/{id}/analysis`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "userIdType": "string",
  "lookbackDays": 1,
  "populationType": "factTable",
  "populationId": "string",
  "additionalNumeratorFilters": [
    "string"
  ],
  "additionalDenominatorFilters": [
    "string"
  ],
  "useCache": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-fact-metric-analysis-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The fact metric id to analyze|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» userIdType|body|string|false|The identifier type to use for the analysis. If not provided, defaults to the first available identifier type in the fact table.|
|» lookbackDays|body|number|false|Number of days to look back for the analysis. Defaults to 30.|
|» populationType|body|string|false|The type of population to analyze. Defaults to 'factTable', meaning the analysis will return the metric value for all units found in the fact table.|
|» populationId|body|string \| null|false|The ID of the population (e.g., segment ID) when populationType is not 'factTable'. Defaults to null.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» additionalNumeratorFilters|body|[string]|false|We support passing in adhoc filters for an analysis that don't live on the metric itself. These are in addition to the metric's filters. To use this, you can pass in an array of Fact Table Filter Ids.|
|» additionalDenominatorFilters|body|[string]|false|We support passing in adhoc filters for an analysis that don't live on the metric itself. These are in addition to the metric's filters. To use this, you can pass in an array of Fact Table Filter Ids.|
|» useCache|body|boolean|false|Whether to use a cached query if one exists. Defaults to true.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» populationType|factTable|
|» populationType|segment|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "metricAnalysis": {
    "id": "string",
    "status": "string",
    "settings": {
      "property1": null,
      "property2": null
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-fact-metric-analysis-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Resource created|Inline|

<h3 id="create-a-fact-metric-analysis-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|metricAnalysis|[MetricAnalysis](#schemametricanalysis)|true|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, basicAuth

<h3 id="create-a-single-metric-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» datasourceId|body|string|true|ID for the [DataSource](#tag/DataSource_model)|
|» managedBy|body|string|false|Where this metric must be managed from. If not set (empty string), it can be managed from anywhere. If set to "api", it can be managed via the API only.|
|» owner|body|string|false|The userId or email address of the owner. If an email address is provided, it will be used to look up the userId of the matching organization member. If an ID is provided, it will be validated as existing in the organization.|
|» name|body|string|true|Short display name (e.g. `Purchases per user`). Put the definition in `description`.|
|» description|body|string|false|Markdown. Put context here, not in the name.|
|» type|body|string|true|Type of metric. See [Metrics documentation](/app/metrics/legacy)|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags for filtering and grouping. Use these instead of encoding groups in names.|
|» projects|body|[string]|false|List of project IDs for projects that can access this metric|
|» archived|body|boolean|false|none|
|» behavior|body|object|false|none|
|» » goal|body|string|false|none|
|» » cappingSettings|body|object|false|Controls how outliers are handled|
|» » » type|body|string \| null|true|none|
|» » » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» » » value|body|number|false|When type is absolute, this is the absolute value. When type is percentile, this is the percentile value (from 0.0 to 1.0).|
|» » » ignoreZeros|body|boolean|false|If true and capping is `percentile`, zeros will be ignored when calculating the percentile.|
|» » cap|body|number|false|**Deprecated.** (deprecated, use cappingSettings instead) This should be non-negative|
|» » capping|body|string \| null|false|**Deprecated.** (deprecated, use cappingSettings instead) Used in conjunction with `capValue` to set the capping (winsorization). Do not specify or set to null for no capping. "absolute" will cap user values at the `capValue` if it is greater than 0. "percentile" will cap user values at the percentile of user values in an experiment using the `capValue` for the percentile, if greater than 0. <br/>  If `behavior.capping` is non-null, you must specify `behavior.capValue`.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» » capValue|body|number|false|**Deprecated.** (deprecated, use cappingSettings instead) This should be non-negative. <br/> Must specify `behavior.capping` when setting `behavior.capValue`.|
|» » windowSettings|body|object|false|Controls the conversion window for the metric|
|» » » type|body|string|true|none|
|» » » delayHours|body|number|false|**Deprecated.** Wait this many hours after experiment exposure before counting conversions. Ignored if delayValue is set.|
|» » » delayValue|body|number|false|Wait this long after experiment exposure before counting conversions.|
|» » » delayUnit|body|string|false|Default `hours`.|
|» » » windowValue|body|number|false|none|
|» » » windowUnit|body|string|false|none|
|» » conversionWindowStart|body|number|false|**Deprecated.** The start of a Conversion Window relative to the exposure date, in hours. This is equivalent to the [Conversion Delay](/app/metrics/legacy/#conversion-delay). <br/> Must specify both `behavior.conversionWindowStart` and `behavior.conversionWindowEnd` or neither.|
|» » conversionWindowEnd|body|number|false|**Deprecated.** The end of a [Conversion Window](/app/metrics/legacy/#conversion-window) relative to the exposure date, in hours. This is equivalent to the [Conversion Delay](/app/metrics/legacy/#conversion-delay) + Conversion Window Hours settings in the UI. In other words, if you want a 48 hour window starting after 24 hours, you would set conversionWindowStart to 24 and conversionWindowEnd to 72 (24+48). <br/> Must specify both `behavior.conversionWindowStart` and `behavior.conversionWindowEnd` or neither.|
|» » priorSettings|body|object|false|Controls the bayesian prior for the metric. If omitted, organization defaults will be used.|
|» » » override|body|boolean|true|If false, the organization default settings will be used instead of the other settings in this object|
|» » » proper|body|boolean|true|If true, the `mean` and `stddev` will be used, otherwise we will use an improper flat prior.|
|» » » mean|body|number|true|The mean of the prior distribution of relative effects in proportion terms (e.g. 0.01 is 1%)|
|» » » stddev|body|number|true|Must be > 0. The standard deviation of the prior distribution of relative effects in proportion terms.|
|» » riskThresholdSuccess|body|number|false|**Deprecated.** No longer used. Accepted and ignored.|
|» » riskThresholdDanger|body|number|false|**Deprecated.** No longer used. Accepted and ignored.|
|» » minPercentChange|body|number|false|Minimum percent change to consider uplift significant, as a proportion (e.g. put 0.005 for 0.5%)|
|» » maxPercentChange|body|number|false|Maximum percent change to consider uplift significant, as a proportion (e.g. put 0.5 for 50%)|
|» » minSampleSize|body|number|false|none|
|» » targetMDE|body|number|false|The percentage change that you want to reliably detect before ending an experiment, as a proportion (e.g. put 0.1 for 10%). This is used to estimate the "Days Left" for running experiments.|
|» sql|body|object|false|Preferred way to define SQL. Only one of `sql`, `sqlBuilder` or `mixpanel` allowed, and at least one must be specified.|
|» » identifierTypes|body|[string]|true|none|
|» » conversionSQL|body|string|true|none|
|» » userAggregationSQL|body|string|false|Custom user level aggregation for your metric (default: `SUM(value)`)|
|» » denominatorMetricId|body|string|false|The metric ID for a [denominator metric for funnel and ratio metrics](/app/metrics/legacy/#denominator-ratio--funnel-metrics)|
|» sqlBuilder|body|object|false|An alternative way to specify a SQL metric, rather than a full query. Using `sql` is preferred to `sqlBuilder`. Only one of `sql`, `sqlBuilder` or `mixpanel` allowed, and at least one must be specified.|
|» » identifierTypeColumns|body|[object]|true|none|

Your existing Legacy Metrics with this value will continue to work, but we suggest migrating to Fact Metrics instead.|

|» » » ignoreZeros|body|boolean|false|If true and capping is `percentile`, zeros will be ignored when calculating the percentile.|
|» » cap|body|number|false|**Deprecated.** (deprecated, use cappingSettings instead) This should be non-negative|
|» » capping|body|string \| null|false|**Deprecated.** (deprecated, use cappingSettings instead) Used in conjunction with `capValue` to set the capping (winsorization). Do not specify or set to null for no capping. "absolute" will cap user values at the `capValue` if it is greater than 0. "percentile" will cap user values at the percentile of user values in an experiment using the `capValue` for the percentile, if greater than 0. <br/>  If `behavior.capping` is non-null, you must specify `behavior.capValue`.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|

|» » » delayUnit|body|string|false|Default `hours`.|

|» » conversionWindowStart|body|number|false|**Deprecated.** The start of a Conversion Window relative to the exposure date, in hours. This is equivalent to the [Conversion Delay](/app/metrics/legacy/#conversion-delay). <br/> Must specify both `behavior.conversionWindowStart` and `behavior.conversionWindowEnd` or neither.|
|» » conversionWindowEnd|body|number|false|**Deprecated.** The end of a [Conversion Window](/app/metrics/legacy/#conversion-window) relative to the exposure date, in hours. This is equivalent to the [Conversion Delay](/app/metrics/legacy/#conversion-delay) + Conversion Window Hours settings in the UI. In other words, if you want a 48 hour window starting after 24 hours, you would set conversionWindowStart to 24 and conversionWindowEnd to 72 (24+48). <br/> Must specify both `behavior.conversionWindowStart` and `behavior.conversionWindowEnd` or neither.|
|» » priorSettings|body|object|false|Controls the bayesian prior for the metric. If omitted, organization defaults will be used.|

## Get results for all experiments that use a metric

<a id="opIdlistMetricExperiments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/metrics/string/experiments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/metrics/{id}/experiments`

Returns, for each experiment that uses the given metric (directly or via a metric group), the per-variation results for that metric from the latest snapshot. Supports the same filtering as the experiment list views via a raw search string or structured query params. Note: at most the 1000 most recent experiments using the metric are considered; filters and pagination are applied within that set, so results may be incomplete for metrics used by more than 1000 experiments.

<h3 id="get-results-for-all-experiments-that-use-a-metric-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The id of the requested resource|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of items to return|
|offset|query|integer|false|How many items to skip (use in conjunction with limit for pagination)|
|q|query|string|false|Raw experiment search/filter string (same syntax as the app's experiment list filters, e.g. `status:running tag:checkout`). Negation (`!`) and operators (`~`, `^`, `>`, `<`, `=`) are not supported and return a 400|
|projectId|query|string|false|Filter by comma-separated project ids or names|
|owner|query|string|false|Filter by comma-separated owner ids, names, or emails|
|status|query|string|false|Filter by comma-separated statuses (draft, running, stopped)|
|result|query|string|false|Filter by comma-separated results (won, lost, inconclusive, dnf)|
|tag|query|string|false|Filter by comma-separated tags|
|type|query|string|false|Filter by comma-separated experiment types (feature, visualChange, redirect)|
|bandits|query|string|false|When true, return only multi-armed bandits; when false, exclude them|
|startDate|query|string|false|Only include experiments that have a phase which ended on or after this date|
|endDate|query|string|false|Only include experiments that have a phase which ended on or before this date|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|bandits|true|
|bandits|false|

```json
    {
      "experimentId": "string",

      "status": "string",

          ],

        }
      ]
    }
  ],

  "hasMore": true,
  "nextOffset": 0
}
```

<h1 id="growthbook-rest-api-experiments">experiments</h1>

Experiments (A/B Tests)

## Get all experiments

<a id="opIdlistExperiments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/experiments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/experiments`

<h3 id="get-all-experiments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of items to return|
|offset|query|integer|false|How many items to skip (use in conjunction with limit for pagination)|
|projectId|query|string|false|Filter by project id|
|datasourceId|query|string|false|Filter by Data Source|
|trackingKey|query|string|false|Filter by experiment tracking key|
|experimentId|query|string|false|Filter the returned list by the experiment tracking key (not the internal experiment ID). Note, this was deprecated to help reduce confusion, consider using `trackingKey` instead, which is functionally identical. You cannot use both params at the same time.|
|status|query|string|false|none|
|q|query|string|false|Raw experiment search/filter string (same syntax as the app's experiment list filters, e.g. `status:running tag:checkout`). Negation (`!`) and operators (`~`, `^`, `>`, `<`, `=`) are not supported and return a 400|
|owner|query|string|false|Filter by comma-separated owner ids, names, or emails|
|result|query|[string]|false|Filter by comma-separated results (won, lost, inconclusive, dnf). Matches the experiment's recorded result — set when an experiment is stopped and retained if it's later restarted, so running experiments can match too|
|tag|query|string|false|Filter by comma-separated tags|
|implementationType|query|[string]|false|Filter by comma-separated implementation types (feature, visualChange, redirect) — the kinds of changes linked to the experiment. To filter standard experiments vs bandits, use `bandits` instead|
|metricId|query|string|false|Filter by comma-separated metric ids. Matches experiments that use a metric as a goal, secondary, or guardrail metric|
|bandits|query|string|false|When true, return only multi-armed bandits; when false, exclude them|
|archived|query|string \| boolean|false|Filter by archived status. Set to `true` to return only archived experiments, `false` to exclude them. If omitted, both archived and non-archived experiments are returned.|
|sortBy|query|string|false|Field to sort the results by|
|sortOrder|query|string|false|Sort direction (used with `sortBy`)|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|draft|
|status|running|
|status|stopped|
|result|dnf|
|result|won|
|result|lost|
|result|inconclusive|
|implementationType|feature|
|implementationType|visualChange|
|implementationType|redirect|
|bandits|true|
|bandits|false|
|sortBy|dateCreated|
|sortBy|dateUpdated|
|sortBy|name|
|sortOrder|asc|
|sortOrder|desc|

`POST /v1/experiments`

Creates a new experiment.

### Naming for human review

Keep `name` short; put reasoning in `hypothesis` and context in `description`. `trackingKey` is sent with exposure events, so keep it short and stable.

<h3 id="create-a-single-experiment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» datasourceId|body|string|false|ID for the [DataSource](#tag/DataSource_model). Can only be set if a templateId is not provided.|
|» assignmentQuery|body|object|false|The assignment query, grouping its ID with the identifier type analyzed on. Mutually exclusive with the deprecated `assignmentQueryId`. Can only be set if a templateId is not provided.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of one of the data source's assignment queries.|
|» » identifierType|body|string \| null|false|The identifier type to analyze on, which the query must declare. Required when selecting a different assignment query that declares several. Otherwise defaults to the current identifier type, or the query's only one. Null is treated as omitted, so a response's value can be sent back.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» assignmentQueryId|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: use `assignmentQuery`. Rejected when selecting a different assignment query that declares several identifier types; set `assignmentQuery.identifierType` instead. Can only be set if a templateId is not provided.|
|» trackingKey|body|string|true|Key sent with exposure events. Keep it short, in kebab-case (usually the Feature Flag key). If your organization requires a tracking key format, a key that doesn't match is rejected with `invalid_tracking_key`. Changing it after launch splits exposures across two keys.|
|» bypassDuplicateKeyCheck|body|boolean|false|If true, allow creating an experiment even if another experiment with the same tracking key already exists. This is ignored if the organization requires unique tracking keys as a rule. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» name|body|string|true|Short display name (e.g. `Express checkout button`). Put reasoning in `hypothesis` and context in `description`.|
|» type|body|string|false|none|
|» project|body|string|false|Project ID which the experiment belongs to|
|» templateId|body|string|false|ID of the [ExperimentTemplate](#tag/ExperimentTemplate_model) this experiment was created from. Template fields are applied by default and overridden by explicitly provided payload fields.|
|» hypothesis|body|string|false|Markdown. If we change X, metric Y will move because Z.|
|» description|body|string|false|Markdown. Put context here, not in the name.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags for filtering and grouping. Use these instead of encoding groups in names.|
|» metrics|body|[string]|false|none|
|» secondaryMetrics|body|[string]|false|none|
|» guardrailMetrics|body|[string]|false|none|
|» activationMetric|body|string|false|Users must convert on this metric before being included|
|» segmentId|body|string|false|Only users in this segment will be included|
|» queryFilter|body|string|false|WHERE clause to add to the default experiment query|
|» owner|body|string|false|The userId or email address of the owner. If an email address is provided, it will be used to look up the userId of the matching organization member. If an ID is provided, it will be validated as existing in the organization. When omitted, it defaults to the requesting member: a personal access token's owner, or the member an organization API key assumes. An organization API key acting as itself leaves it empty.|
|» archived|body|boolean|false|none|
|» status|body|string|false|none|
|» autoRefresh|body|boolean|false|none|
|» hashAttribute|body|string|false|none|
|» fallbackAttribute|body|string|false|none|
|» attributeScopeAllProjects|body|boolean|false|Picker preference: show attributes from all projects in this experiment's targeting UI instead of only those in scope for its project and linked features. Does not loosen enforcement — when the organization requires registered attributes with project scoping, out-of-scope attributes are still rejected.|
|» hashVersion|body|number|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» disableStickyBucketing|body|boolean|false|When true, disables Sticky Bucketing for this experiment. If omitted, defaults to your organization's Sticky Bucketing setting for new experiments. Sticky Bucketing only takes effect when it is also enabled at the organization level.|
|» bucketVersion|body|integer|false|none|
|» minBucketVersion|body|integer|false|none|
|» releasedVariationId|body|string|false|none|
|» excludeFromPayload|body|boolean|false|none|
|» inProgressConversions|body|string|false|none|
|» attributionModel|body|string|false|Setting attribution model to `"experimentDuration"` is the same as selecting "Ignore Conversion Windows" for the Conversion Window Override. Setting it to `"lookbackOverride"` requires a `lookbackOverride` object to be provided.|
|» lookbackOverride|body|object|false|Controls the lookback override for the experiment. For type "window", value must be a non-negative number and valueUnit is required.|
|» » type|body|string|true|none|
|» » value|body|number \| string(date-time)|true|For "window" type - non-negative numeric value (e.g. 7 for 7 days). For "date" type a date string.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|number|false|For "window" type - non-negative numeric value (e.g. 7 for 7 days). For "date" type a date string.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string(date-time)|false|For "window" type - non-negative numeric value (e.g. 7 for 7 days). For "date" type a date string.|
|» » valueUnit|body|string|false|Used when type is "window". Defaults to "days".|
|» statsEngine|body|string|false|none|
|» variations|body|[object]|true|none|
|» » id|body|string|false|Stable variation id. On update, an omitted id is filled from the stored variation with the same key, or the same position, when the number of variations is unchanged.|
|» » variationId|body|string|false|Alias for `id`. Mirrors the GET response. `id` takes precedence.|
|» » key|body|string|true|Key sent with exposure events (e.g. `0`, `1`). Changing it after launch splits exposures.|
|» » name|body|string|true|Short label shown in results (e.g. `Control`).|
|» » description|body|string|false|What this variation changes.|
|» » screenshots|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » » path|body|string|true|none|
|» » » width|body|number|false|none|
|» » » height|body|number|false|none|
|» » » description|body|string|false|none|
|» phases|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » name|body|string|true|Short phase label (e.g. `Main`).|
|» » dateStarted|body|string(date-time)|true|none|
|» » dateEnded|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» » reasonForStopping|body|string|false|none|
|» » seed|body|string|false|none|
|» » coverage|body|number|false|none|
|» » namespace|body|object|false|none|
|» » » namespaceId|body|string|true|none|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » range|body|[number]|false|none|
|» » » ranges|body|[[number, number]]|false|none|
|» » prerequisites|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » » id|body|string|true|Feature ID|
|» » » condition|body|string|true|none|
|» » reason|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: use `reasonForStopping`. Takes precedence if set.|
|» » condition|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: use `targetingCondition`. Takes precedence if set.|
|» » targetingCondition|body|string|false|Targeting condition as a JSON string. Mirrors the GET response.|
|» » savedGroups|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » » match|body|string|true|none|
|» » » ids|body|[string]|true|none|
|» » savedGroupTargeting|body|[object]|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated — use `savedGroups`. Accepted so a GET response can be posted back unchanged; `savedGroups` takes precedence if both are sent.|

## Get latest results for many experiments

<a id="opIdlistExperimentResults"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/experiments/results \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/experiments/results`

Returns the latest non-dimension snapshot for each experiment matching the filters. Use this to scan results across a portfolio in one call.

Pagination semantics:
- `total` is the count of experiments matching the filters.
- `count` is the length of the returned `experimentResults` array.
- Experiments without a completed snapshot are omitted from `experimentResults`, so `count` may be less than the page slice and a page may legitimately return `count: 0` while `hasMore: true`.
- `hasMore` and `nextOffset` advance over experiments matching the filters, not over returned results.

Use the per-experiment `GET /experiments/{id}/results` endpoint to inspect specific phases or dimensions.

<h3 id="get-latest-results-for-many-experiments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of items to return|
|offset|query|integer|false|How many items to skip (use in conjunction with limit for pagination)|
|projectId|query|string|false|Filter by project id|
|datasourceId|query|string|false|Filter by Data Source|
|trackingKey|query|string|false|Filter by experiment tracking key|
|status|query|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|draft|
|status|running|
|status|stopped|

`POST /v1/experiments/{id}`

Setting `status` from draft to running starts the experiment as `POST /experiments/{id}/start` does, judged on the experiment as this update leaves it, with `skipChecklist` in this body. Changing `archived` archives or unarchives it as `POST /experiments/{id}/archive` and `/unarchive` do.

<h3 id="update-a-single-experiment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The id of the requested resource|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» datasourceId|body|string|false|Changing it needs an `assignmentQueryId` from the new one, and drops the metrics, segment and unit dimensions that aren't from it.|
|» assignmentQuery|body|object|false|The assignment query, grouping its ID with the identifier type analyzed on. Mutually exclusive with the deprecated `assignmentQueryId`.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of one of the data source's assignment queries.|
|» » identifierType|body|string \| null|false|The identifier type to analyze on, which the query must declare. Required when selecting a different assignment query that declares several. Otherwise defaults to the current identifier type, or the query's only one. Null is treated as omitted, so a response's value can be sent back.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» assignmentQueryId|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: use `assignmentQuery`. Rejected when selecting a different assignment query that declares several identifier types; set `assignmentQuery.identifierType` instead.|
|» trackingKey|body|string|false|Key sent with exposure events. Keep it short, in kebab-case (usually the Feature Flag key). If your organization requires a tracking key format, a key that doesn't match is rejected with `invalid_tracking_key`. Changing it after launch splits exposures across two keys.|
|» bypassDuplicateKeyCheck|body|boolean|false|If true, allow updating the tracking key even if another experiment with the same tracking key already exist. This is ignored if the organization requires unique tracking keys as a rule. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» name|body|string|false|Short display name (e.g. `Express checkout button`). Put reasoning in `hypothesis` and context in `description`.|
|» type|body|string|false|none|
|» bypassApproval|body|boolean|false|Deprecated and ignored. Approval is bypassed automatically when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access for this resource or when the organization enables the REST API approval bypass. Otherwise, the revision must be approved before it can be published.|
|» project|body|string|false|Project ID which the experiment belongs to|
|» hypothesis|body|string|false|Markdown. If we change X, metric Y will move because Z.|
|» description|body|string|false|Markdown. Put context here, not in the name.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags for filtering and grouping. Use these instead of encoding groups in names.|
|» metrics|body|[string]|false|none|
|» secondaryMetrics|body|[string]|false|none|
|» guardrailMetrics|body|[string]|false|none|
|» activationMetric|body|string|false|Users must convert on this metric before being included|
|» segmentId|body|string|false|Only users in this segment will be included|
|» queryFilter|body|string|false|WHERE clause to add to the default experiment query|
|» owner|body|string|false|The userId or email address of the owner. If an email address is provided, it will be used to look up the userId of the matching organization member. If an ID is provided, it will be validated as existing in the organization.|
|» archived|body|boolean|false|none|
|» linkedChanges|body|string|false|Required while the experiment still serves through linked changes. "materialize" keeps a stopped experiment's released variation as a permanent force rule on each linked Feature Flag; "remove" acknowledges that the linked changes stop serving.|
|» status|body|string|false|none|
|» autoRefresh|body|boolean|false|none|
|» hashAttribute|body|string|false|none|
|» fallbackAttribute|body|string|false|none|
|» attributeScopeAllProjects|body|boolean|false|Picker preference: show attributes from all projects in this experiment's targeting UI instead of only those in scope for its project and linked features. Does not loosen enforcement — when the organization requires registered attributes with project scoping, out-of-scope attributes are still rejected.|
|» hashVersion|body|number|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» disableStickyBucketing|body|boolean|false|none|
|» bucketVersion|body|integer|false|none|
|» minBucketVersion|body|integer|false|none|
|» results|body|string|false|The result status of the experiment. Maps to resultSummary.status in the GET response.|
|» winner|body|number|false|The index of the winning variation (0-indexed). Maps to resultSummary.winner (variation ID) in the GET response.|
|» analysis|body|string|false|Analysis summary or conclusions for the experiment. Maps to resultSummary.conclusions in the GET response.|
|» releasedVariationId|body|string|false|The ID of the released variation. Maps to resultSummary.releasedVariationId in the GET response.|
|» excludeFromPayload|body|boolean|false|If true, the experiment is excluded from the SDK payload. Maps to resultSummary.excludeFromPayload in the GET response.|
|» inProgressConversions|body|string|false|none|
|» attributionModel|body|string|false|Setting attribution model to `"experimentDuration"` is the same as selecting "Ignore Conversion Windows" for the Conversion Window Override. Setting it to `"lookbackOverride"` requires a `lookbackOverride` object to be provided.|
|» lookbackOverride|body|object|false|Controls the lookback override for the experiment. For type "window", value must be a non-negative number and valueUnit is required.|
|» » type|body|string|true|none|
|» » value|body|number \| string(date-time)|true|For "window" type - non-negative numeric value (e.g. 7 for 7 days). For "date" type a date string.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|number|false|For "window" type - non-negative numeric value (e.g. 7 for 7 days). For "date" type a date string.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string(date-time)|false|For "window" type - non-negative numeric value (e.g. 7 for 7 days). For "date" type a date string.|
|» » valueUnit|body|string|false|Used when type is "window". Defaults to "days".|
|» statsEngine|body|string|false|none|
|» variations|body|[object]|false|none|

|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|Scheduled start/end. Set to `null` to remove. Provide any of `startAt`, `stopAt`, or `stopAfter` (a deferred relative end resolved at start). End-of-experiment automation is set via the nested `scheduledStopPlan`, which is required whenever a `stopAt` or `stopAfter` is set.|
|» » startAt|body|string(date-time)|false|ISO datetime when the experiment should start. Must be in the future. Setting or clearing this field invalidates any existing staged start (`nextScheduledStatusUpdate`); call POST /experiments/{id}/start to stage the new schedule.|

|» » » value|body|integer|true|none|
|» » » unit|body|string|true|none|
|» » scheduledStopPlan|body|[ScheduledStopPlan](#schemascheduledstopplan)|false|End-of-experiment automation applied at the scheduled end. Required whenever a `stopAt` or `stopAfter` is set (any mode, including `notify`).|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» precomputedUnitDimensionIds|body|[string]|false|none|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipChecklist|body|boolean|false|When `status` starts a draft: start past its incomplete launch checklist items, as `POST /experiments/{id}/start` does. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Resource created|Inline|
|202|Accepted|Held until a person confirms it in GrowthBook. Poll the Location until the confirmation completes.|[ConfirmationHeld](#schemaconfirmationheld)|
|409|Conflict|Conflict|Inline|

<h3 id="update-a-single-experiment-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|experiment|[Experiment](#schemaexperiment)|true|none|none|
|bypassedGates|[object]|false|none|Gates this start skipped or bypassed. Present only when there were some.|
|» key|string|true|none|The checklist item, or `rampLocked:<featureId>` for a linked Feature Flag a ramp locks.|
|» type|string|true|none|Gate kind: "checklist-item", "approval-required", "merge-conflict", "unrelated-draft-changes", "permission-denied" or "ramp-locked".|
|» outcome|string|true|none|none|
|» via|string|true|none|How it was passed: `skipChecklist`, the caller's permission (`bypassApprovalPermission`), or the organization's REST API approval bypass (`restApiBypassesReviews`).|
|publishedFeatureDrafts|[[publishedFeatureDrafts](#schemapublishedfeaturedrafts)]|false|none|The linked Feature Flag drafts the start published. Present only when it published some.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|» via|skipSchemaValidation|
|» via|skipHooks|
|» via|bypassApprovalPermission|
|» via|restApiBypassesReviews|
|» via|revertsBypassApproval|
|» via|skipChecklist|

Status Code **409**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|message|string|true|none|none|
|code|string|true|none|none|
|details|[ApiErrorChecklistIncompleteDetails](#schemaapierrorchecklistincompletedetails)|true|none|none|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|One or more linked feature drafts could not be published|
|message|string|true|none|none|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|code|pending_draft_publish_failed|

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Location|string||The confirmation to poll|

## Delete an experiment

<a id="opIddeleteExperiment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/experiments/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v1/experiments/{id}`

Archive first: a live experiment can only be deleted when the organization allows the REST API to bypass approval requirements. Linked Feature Flags lose their experiment rule unless `linkedChanges` is "materialize".

<h3 id="delete-an-experiment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The id of the requested resource|
|linkedChanges|query|string|false|Required while the experiment still serves through linked changes. "materialize" keeps a stopped experiment's released variation as a permanent force rule on each linked Feature Flag; "remove" acknowledges that the linked changes stop serving.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|linkedChanges|materialize|
|linkedChanges|remove|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "deletedId": "string"
}
```

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "confirmation": {
    "id": "string",
    "status": "pending",
    "actions": [
      {
        "action": "feature.create",
        "environments": [
          "string"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "summary": "string",
    "url": "string",
    "expiresAt": "string",
    "response": {
      "status": 0,
      "body": null
    },
    "note": "string"
  },
  "message": "string"
}
```

|200|OK|Resource deleted|Inline|
|202|Accepted|Held until a person confirms it in GrowthBook. Poll the Location until the confirmation completes.|[ConfirmationHeld](#schemaconfirmationheld)|

<h3 id="delete-an-experiment-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

### Response Headers

|202|Retry-After|integer||Seconds to wait before polling|

## Archive an experiment

<a id="opIdpostExperimentArchive"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/experiments/string/archive \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "linkedChanges": "materialize"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/experiments/{id}/archive`

An archived experiment leaves the SDK payload. Refused while a running experiment or a temporary rollout still serves through linked changes unless `linkedChanges` says what happens to them.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "linkedChanges": "materialize"
}
```

<h3 id="archive-an-experiment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The id of the requested resource|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» linkedChanges|body|string|false|Required while the experiment still serves through linked changes. "materialize" keeps a stopped experiment's released variation as a permanent force rule on each linked Feature Flag; "remove" acknowledges that the linked changes stop serving.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» linkedChanges|materialize|
|» linkedChanges|remove|

## Start/Stage an experiment

<a id="opIdpostExperimentStart"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/experiments/string/start \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "skipChecklist": true,
    "bypassApproval": true,
    "ignoreWarnings": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/experiments/{id}/start`

Starts an experiment or stages it for a future start if a `statusUpdateSchedule` is set on the experiment. Both check the launch checklist that `GET /experiments/{id}/start-checklist` returns, as gates. An incomplete item refuses the start with `checklist_incomplete` unless `skipChecklist` is set; a linked Feature Flag blocker refuses it either way. The refusal lists each blocking gate in `gates`, with the flag or permission that gets past it and a route that resolves it. A linked Feature Flag draft that still needs approval, or a flag locked by a ramp, is bypassed automatically when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access for that flag or the organization enables the REST API approval bypass. A start reports what it got past in `bypassedGates` and the drafts it published in `publishedFeatureDrafts`; if a draft can't publish, for example because it needs a rebase, the start fails with `pending_draft_publish_failed` before any is published. A staged start carries the caller's Bypass draft approvals access to when it runs, for the drafts as they were when it was staged: if one has changed since, or the caller has lost that access, it needs approval like any other. The organization's REST API approval bypass doesn't carry to a staged start.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "skipChecklist": true,
  "bypassApproval": true,
  "ignoreWarnings": true
}
```

<h3 id="startstage-an-experiment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The id of the requested resource|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» skipChecklist|body|boolean|false|If true, skips validating the experiment satisfies all pre-launch checklist items. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» bypassApproval|body|boolean|false|Deprecated and ignored. Approval is bypassed automatically when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access for this resource or when the organization enables the REST API approval bypass. Otherwise, the revision must be approved before it can be published.|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

Otherwise, defaults to the test variation when results is 'won' and to the baseline variation for other results.|
|» analysis|body|string|false|Optional markdown summary displayed on the experiment results page.|
|» reason|body|string|false|Optional reason for ending the phase stored on the latest phase metadata.|
|» dateEnded|body|string|false|Optional ISO datetime for ending the latest phase. Defaults to the current date and time.|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Set an experiment's schedule and shipping automation

<a id="opIdputExperimentSchedule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/experiments/string/schedule \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "startAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "stopAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "stopAfter": {
      "value": 1,
      "unit": "hours"
    },
    "scheduledStopPlan": {
      "mode": "notify",
      "tiebreakerMetricId": "string",
      "fallback": "notify",
      "fallbackVariationId": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/experiments/{id}/schedule`

Full-replace of the experiment's scheduled start/end and end-of-experiment shipping automation. The body is the complete desired state: any omitted field is cleared (omit `startAt` to remove a scheduled start; send an empty body to clear the whole schedule). Provide either `stopAt` or `stopAfter`, not both; a relative `stopAfter` resolves to a concrete stop when the experiment starts. Setting a scheduled end (`stopAt` or `stopAfter`) requires a `scheduledStopPlan` (any mode, including `notify`). The scheduled end must be in the future: a `stopAt` (or a `stopAfter` that resolves) in the past is rejected — including one whose end date has already passed and been acted on, so changing the plan after a soft end requires committing to a new end date. Auto-ship shipping requires the Decision Framework.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "startAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "stopAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "stopAfter": {
    "value": 1,
    "unit": "hours"
  },
  "scheduledStopPlan": {
    "mode": "notify",
    "tiebreakerMetricId": "string",
    "fallback": "notify",
    "fallbackVariationId": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="set-an-experiments-schedule-and-shipping-automation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The id of the requested resource|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» startAt|body|string(date-time)|false|ISO datetime when the experiment should start; must be in the future. Omit to clear a scheduled start. Staging still happens via POST /experiments/{id}/start.|
|» stopAt|body|string(date-time)|false|Absolute ISO datetime to stop the experiment.|
|» stopAfter|body|object|false|Deferred relative end, resolved to a concrete stop at the experiment's actual start (or now, if already running).|
|» » value|body|integer|true|none|
|» » unit|body|string|true|none|
|» scheduledStopPlan|body|[ScheduledStopPlan](#schemascheduledstopplan)|false|End-of-experiment automation. Required whenever a `stopAt` or `stopAfter` is set (any mode, including `notify`).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » unit|hours|
|» » unit|days|

## Modify temporary rollout status for a stopped experiment

<a id="opIdpostExperimentModifyTemporaryRollout"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/experiments/string/modify-temporary-rollout \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "enableTemporaryRollout": true,
    "releasedVariationId": "string",
    "ignoreWarnings": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/experiments/{id}/modify-temporary-rollout`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enableTemporaryRollout": true,
  "releasedVariationId": "string",
  "ignoreWarnings": true
}
```

<h3 id="modify-temporary-rollout-status-for-a-stopped-experiment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The id of the requested resource|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» enableTemporaryRollout|body|boolean|true|If true, keep the stopped experiment in SDK payload and force traffic to the winner variation. If false, end temporary rollout and remove from SDK payload.|
|» releasedVariationId|body|string|false|Variation ID (e.g. var_abc123) to release to 100% of traffic eligible for this experiment. Required if enableTemporaryRollout is true.|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Create Experiment Snapshot

<a id="opIdpostExperimentSnapshot"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/experiments/string/snapshot \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "triggeredBy": "manual",
    "dimension": "string",
    "phase": 0
  }'
```

`POST /v1/experiments/{id}/snapshot`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "triggeredBy": "manual",
  "dimension": "string",
  "phase": 0
}
```

<h3 id="create-experiment-snapshot-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The experiment id of the experiment to update|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» triggeredBy|body|string|false|Set to "schedule" if you want this request to trigger notifications and other events as if it were a scheduled update. Defaults to manual.|
|» dimension|body|string|false|Dimension to break results down by. For Unit Dimensions, use the dimension id (e.g. "dim_abc123"). For Experiment Dimensions, use "exp:<dimensionName>" (e.g. "exp:country"). Built-in pre-exposure dimensions include "pre:date" and, when configured, "pre:activation". Use "cutoff:<ISO datetime>" (e.g. "cutoff:2026-01-15T00:12:00.000Z") to split units by whether they were first exposed before or after the cutoff; it must fall within the phase dates. Use "combo:<dimA>::<dimB>" (e.g. "combo:exp:country::dim_abc123") to break down by the intersection of two dimensions, each an Experiment Dimension or Unit Dimension id; values beyond the top 20 combined slices are merged into "(other)". Omit this field to create a standard snapshot.|
|» phase|body|integer|false|Zero-based phase index to snapshot, where 0 is the first experiment phase. Defaults to the latest phase.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» triggeredBy|manual|
|» triggeredBy|schedule|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "snapshot": {
    "id": "string",
    "experiment": "string",
    "status": "string"
  }
}
```

> 409 Response

```json

  "message": "string",
  "code": "requires_full_refresh",
  "details": {
    "reason": "string"
  }
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|200|OK|Resource created|Inline|
|409|Conflict|Conflict|Inline|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|details|[ApiErrorRequiresFullRefreshDetails](#schemaapierrorrequiresfullrefreshdetails)|true|none|none|

|message|string|true|none|none|

<h1 id="growthbook-rest-api-namespaces">namespaces</h1>

Namespaces partition your user population into buckets so that experiments using the same hash attribute do not overlap unintentionally. Each namespace defines a 0–1 range and individual experiments claim sub-ranges within it.

## Get all namespaces

<a id="opIdlistNamespaces"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/namespaces \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/namespaces`

<h3 id="get-all-namespaces-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of items to return|
|offset|query|integer|false|How many items to skip (use in conjunction with limit for pagination)|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "namespaces": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "displayName": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "status": "active",
      "format": "legacy",
      "hashAttribute": "string",
      "seed": "string"
    }
  ],
  "limit": 0,
  "offset": 0,
  "count": 0,
  "total": 0,
  "hasMore": true,
  "nextOffset": 0
}
```

## Rotate namespace seed

<a id="opIdpostNamespaceRotateSeed"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/namespaces/string/rotateSeed \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "seed": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/namespaces/{id}/rotateSeed`

⚠️ Dangerous: sets a new seed for a multiRange namespace. Every user's bucket position within the namespace is re-computed immediately, which re-randomizes traffic eligibility for **all** experiments currently using this namespace. Only do this if you intentionally want to reshuffle all allocations across experiments. This could be useful when re-using a namespace for a new set of experiments.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "seed": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="rotate-namespace-seed-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The unique id of the namespace|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» seed|body|string|false|A specific value to use as the new seed. If omitted, a random value is generated.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "namespace": {
    "id": "string",
    "displayName": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "status": "active",
    "format": "legacy",
    "hashAttribute": "string",
    "seed": "string"
  }
}
```

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "confirmation": {
    "id": "string",
    "status": "pending",
    "actions": [
      {
        "action": "feature.create",
        "environments": [
          "string"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "summary": "string",
    "url": "string",
    "expiresAt": "string",
    "response": {
      "status": 0,
      "body": null
    },
    "note": "string"
  },
  "message": "string"
}
```

```json
  ],
```

```bash
  "query": "string",
```
```json
  "factTableId": "string",

    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-single-segment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Short display name. Put details in `description`.|
|» owner|body|string|false|The userId or email address of the owner. If an email address is provided, it will be used to look up the userId of the matching organization member. If an ID is provided, it will be validated as existing in the organization.|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of the segment|
|» datasourceId|body|string|true|ID of the datasource this segment belongs to|
|» identifierType|body|string|true|Type of identifier (user, anonymous, etc.)|
|» projects|body|[string]|false|List of project IDs for projects that can access this segment|
|» managedBy|body|string|false|Where this Segment must be managed from. If not set (empty string), it can be managed from anywhere.|
|» type|body|string|true|GrowthBook supports two types of Segments, SQL and FACT. SQL segments are defined by a SQL query, and FACT segments are defined by a fact table and filters.|
|» query|body|string|false|SQL query that defines the Segment. This is required for SQL segments.|
|» factTableId|body|string|false|ID of the fact table this segment belongs to. This is required for FACT segments.|
|» filters|body|[string]|false|Optional array of fact table filter ids that can further define the Fact Table based Segment.|

|---|---|
|» managedBy|""|
|» managedBy|api|
|» type|SQL|
|» type|FACT|

<h1 id="growthbook-rest-api-reports">reports</h1>

Custom analysis reports built on top of experiment snapshots. Reports let you re-run analysis with different metrics, date ranges, stats engines, and other settings without modifying the underlying experiment.

If an ID is provided, it will be validated as existing in the organization. When omitted, it defaults to the requesting member: a personal access token's owner, or the member an organization API key assumes. An organization API key acting as itself leaves it empty.|
|» statsEngine|body|string|false|Stats engine override|
|» goalMetrics|body|[string]|false|Goal metric IDs (defaults to experiment's goal metrics)|
|» secondaryMetrics|body|[string]|false|Secondary metric IDs (defaults to experiment's secondary metrics)|
|» guardrailMetrics|body|[string]|false|Guardrail metric IDs (defaults to experiment's guardrail metrics)|
|» activationMetric|body|string|false|Activation metric ID|
|» dimension|body|string|false|Dimension to cut results by|
|» dateStarted|body|string(date-time)|false|Analysis start date (ISO 8601)|
|» dateEnded|body|string(date-time)|false|Analysis end date (ISO 8601)|
|» regressionAdjustmentEnabled|body|boolean|false|Enable CUPED regression adjustment|
|» sequentialTestingEnabled|body|boolean|false|Enable sequential testing|
|» sequentialTestingTuningParameter|body|number|false|Tuning parameter for sequential testing (frequentist only)|
|» differenceType|body|string|false|How lifts are expressed in results. Defaults to experiment setting.|
|» attributionModel|body|string|false|Metric conversion window attribution model. Defaults to experiment setting.|
|» lookbackOverride|body|object|false|Lookback window when `attributionModel` is `lookbackOverride`|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » type|body|string|true|none|
|» » value|body|object|true|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » type|body|string|true|none|
|» » value|body|number|true|none|
|» » valueUnit|body|string|true|none|
|» metricOverrides|body|[object]|false|Per-metric window, prior, and regression-adjustment overrides|
|» » id|body|string|true|none|
|» » windowType|body|string|false|none|
|» » windowHours|body|number|false|none|

|» » loseRisk|body|number|false|**Deprecated.** No longer used. Accepted and ignored.|
|» customMetricSlices|body|[object]|false|Custom metric slice definitions|
|» » slices|body|[object]|true|none|
|» » » column|body|string|true|none|
|» » » levels|body|[string]|true|none|
|» segment|body|string|false|Segment ID to filter users by. Defaults to experiment setting.|
|» queryFilter|body|string|false|Raw SQL WHERE clause added to the exposure query. Defaults to experiment setting.|
|» skipPartialData|body|boolean|false|When true, exclude users who have not completed the full conversion window.|
|» shareLevel|body|string|false|Visibility of the created report. Defaults to `private`. Set to `public` to receive a shareable `shareUrl` in the response.|

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Update report metadata (title, description, visibility)

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/reports/string/metadata \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "title": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "status": "published",
    "shareLevel": "public",
    "editLevel": "organization"
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/reports/{id}/metadata`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "status": "published",
  "shareLevel": "public",
  "editLevel": "organization"
}
```

<h3 id="update-report-metadata-title-description-visibility-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The id of the requested resource|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» title|body|string|false|Report title|
|» description|body|string|false|Report description|
|» status|body|string|false|UI lifecycle marker for the report|
|» shareLevel|body|string|false|Visibility of the report. Setting to `public` enables a shareable `shareUrl`; setting back to `organization` or `private` revokes public access (the share token is preserved, so re-publishing exposes the same URL).|
|» editLevel|body|string|false|Who can edit the report in the GrowthBook UI. `organization` allows any org member with the `createAnalyses` permission; `private` restricts editing to the report owner.|

|» status|private|

## Partially update a single saved group

<a id="opIdupdateSavedGroup"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/saved-groups/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "condition": "string",
    "values": [
      "string"
    ],
    "owner": "string",
    "projects": [
      "string"
    ],
    "currentUploadVersion": 1,
    "bypassApproval": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/saved-groups/{id}`

Applies the change immediately and records it as a published revision, so it appears in history and fires revision webhooks. When the organization requires approvals, open a draft instead or pass `bypassApproval` with the bypass permission.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "condition": "string",
  "values": [
    "string"
  ],
  "owner": "string",
  "projects": [
    "string"
  ],
  "currentUploadVersion": 1,
  "bypassApproval": true
}
```

<h3 id="partially-update-a-single-saved-group-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The id of the requested resource|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|Short display name (e.g. `Internal employees`). Put details in `description`.|
|» description|body|string|false|Short note (max 100 characters) on who is in the Saved Group and why.|
|» condition|body|string|false|When type = 'condition', this is the JSON-encoded condition for the group|
|» values|body|[string]|false|When type = 'list', this is the list of values for the attribute key|
|» owner|body|string|false|The userId or email address of the owner. If an email address is provided, it will be used to look up the userId of the matching organization member. If an ID is provided, it will be validated as existing in the organization.|
|» projects|body|[string]|false|none|
|» currentUploadVersion|body|integer|false|When type = 'remote', the upload whose IDs the group uses. Must be a valid upload of this group.|
|» bypassApproval|body|boolean|false|Set to true to update the live Saved Group without approval. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access in every current and destination Project. This field has no effect when approval is not required.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "savedGroup": {
    "id": "string",

    "dateCreated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "dateUpdated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",

    }
  },
```
