## Archive a single saved group

<a id="opIdarchiveSavedGroup"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/saved-groups/string/archive \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ignoreWarnings": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/saved-groups/{id}/archive`

Archives a Saved Group. If it is still referenced by a Feature Flag, experiment, or another Saved Group, the API returns 422 with the affected references. Send `"ignoreWarnings": true` to acknowledge those references and continue. When approval is required, create and publish an archive revision instead, or use a caller with Bypass draft approvals access. A successful response lists any skipped gates in `bypassedGates`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ignoreWarnings": true
}
```

<h3 id="archive-a-single-saved-group-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The id of the requested resource|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "savedGroup": {
    "id": "string",
    "type": "condition",
    "dateCreated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "dateUpdated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "name": "string",
    "owner": "string",
    "ownerEmail": "string",
    "condition": "string",
    "attributeKey": "string",
    "values": [
      "string"
    ],
    "description": "string",
    "projects": [
      "string"
    ],
    "archived": true,
    "useEmptyListGroup": true,
    "currentUploadVersion": 0,
    "currentUpload": {
      "version": 0,
      "dateCreated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "numeric": true
    }
  },
  "bypassedGates": [
    {
      "type": "string",
      "outcome": "bypassed",
      "via": "ignoreWarnings"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "confirmation": {
    "id": "string",
    "status": "pending",
    "actions": [
      {
        "action": "feature.create",
        "environments": [
          "string"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "summary": "string",
    "url": "string",
    "expiresAt": "string",
    "response": {
      "status": 0,
      "body": null
    },
    "note": "string"
  },

## Upload a new version of a remote saved group's IDs

<a id="opIdpostSavedGroupUpload"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/saved-groups/string/uploads \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "fileKey": "string",
    "fileName": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/saved-groups/{id}/uploads`

Records the next version of the group's IDs. The start and end of the file are checked for one ID per line, then the whole file in the background; loaders trim and deduplicate the IDs. Poll `GET /saved-groups/{id}/uploads/{version}` until it's valid, then set the group's `currentUploadVersion` with `PUT /saved-groups-revisions/{id}/{version}/upload-version` to use it. Loaders pick up the group's version from `currentUpload` and download it from `GET /saved-groups/{id}/uploads/{version}/file`, which redirects to a short-lived signed storage URL.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "fileKey": "string",
  "fileName": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="upload-a-new-version-of-a-remote-saved-groups-ids-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The id of the requested resource|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» fileKey|body|string|true|The `fileKey` from the upload URL endpoint|
|» fileName|body|string|false|The file's original name, used when downloading it|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "upload": {
    "savedGroupId": "string",
    "version": 0,
    "fileName": "string",
    "size": 0,
    "sha256": "string",
    "dateCreated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "createdBy": "string",
    "status": {
      "type": "pending"
    },
    "loads": [
      {
        "storeId": "string",
        "status": {
          "type": "loading"
        },
        "dateUpdated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "confirmation": {
    "id": "string",
    "status": "pending",
    "actions": [
      {
        "action": "feature.create",
        "environments": [
          "string"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "summary": "string",
    "url": "string",
    "expiresAt": "string",
    "response": {
      "status": 0,
      "body": null
    },
    "note": "string"
  },
  "message": "string"
}
```

## Delete an upload of a remote saved group

<a id="opIddeleteSavedGroupUpload"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/saved-groups/string/uploads/1 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v1/saved-groups/{id}/uploads/{version}`

Deletes the upload and its file. The version the group uses, or one an open draft uses, can't be deleted. Version numbers aren't reused. Needs permission to publish the saved group.

<h3 id="delete-an-upload-of-a-remote-saved-group-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The id of the remote saved group|
|version|path|integer|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "deletedVersion": 0
}
```

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "confirmation": {
    "id": "string",
    "status": "pending",
    "actions": [
      {
        "action": "feature.create",
        "environments": [
          "string"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "summary": "string",
    "url": "string",
    "expiresAt": "string",
    "response": {
      "status": 0,
      "body": null
    },
    "note": "string"
  },
  "message": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-an-upload-of-a-remote-saved-group-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Resource deleted|Inline|
|202|Accepted|Held until a person confirms it in GrowthBook. Poll the Location until the confirmation completes.|[ConfirmationHeld](#schemaconfirmationheld)|

<h3 id="delete-an-upload-of-a-remote-saved-group-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|deletedVersion|integer|true|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Location|string||The confirmation to poll|
|202|Retry-After|integer||Seconds to wait before polling|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, basicAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="growthbook-rest-api-saved-group-revisions">saved-group-revisions</h1>

Draft revisions for saved groups, including pending changes, approvals, and lifecycle (publish, discard, revert).

Most callers can interact with these endpoints via shorthand actions (`/items/add`, `/items/remove`, single-field PUTs) instead of authoring JSON Patch ops directly. Pass `version: "new"` on edit endpoints to auto-create a draft.

## List saved-group revisions across the organization

<a id="opIdlistSavedGroupRevisions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/saved-groups-revisions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/saved-groups-revisions`

Returns a paginated list of revisions across all saved groups in the organization, sorted newest-first. Optionally filtered by saved group, status, author, or the calling user's involvement.

<h3 id="list-saved-group-revisions-across-the-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of items to return|
|offset|query|integer|false|How many items to skip (use in conjunction with limit for pagination)|
|skipPagination|query|string \| boolean|false|If true, return all matching items and ignore limit/offset.<br>Self-hosted only. Has no effect unless API_ALLOW_SKIP_PAGINATION is set to true or 1.|
|savedGroupId|query|string|false|Restrict results to revisions for a single saved group. When omitted, returns revisions across every saved group the caller can read.|
|status|query|string|false|Filter by revision status. Accepts a comma-separated list, or the literal `open` for non-merged/non-discarded revisions.|
|author|query|string|false|none|
|mine|query|string \| boolean|false|If true, return only revisions authored by the calling user. Needs a personal access token, or an organization API key that assumes a named member's role. Mutually exclusive with `author`.|

## Create a draft revision

<a id="opIdpostSavedGroupRevision"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/saved-groups-revisions/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "title": "string",
    "comment": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/saved-groups-revisions/{savedGroupId}`

Creates a new draft revision branched from the current live saved group. A saved group can have multiple concurrent drafts; use this to start an isolated line of edits.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "string",
  "comment": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-draft-revision-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|savedGroupId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» title|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`).|
|» comment|body|string|false|Markdown. What changed and why, for reviewers.|

## Get the most recent active draft revision

<a id="opIdgetSavedGroupRevisionLatest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/saved-groups-revisions/string/latest \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/saved-groups-revisions/{savedGroupId}/latest`

Returns the most recently updated open (non-merged, non-discarded) revision for the saved group. Returns 404 if there is no active draft. Pass `mine=true` to restrict to drafts authored by the calling user. Needs a personal access token, or an organization API key that assumes a named member's role.

<h3 id="get-the-most-recent-active-draft-revision-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|savedGroupId|path|string|true|none|
|mine|query|string \| boolean|false|If true, return only the most recent active draft authored by the calling user. Needs a personal access token, or an organization API key that assumes a named member's role.|

## Update saved group metadata in a draft revision

<a id="opIdputSavedGroupRevisionMetadata"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/saved-groups-revisions/string/0/metadata \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "revisionTitle": "string",
    "revisionComment": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "owner": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "projects": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/saved-groups-revisions/{savedGroupId}/{version}/metadata`

Stages metadata changes (name, owner, description, projects) on the draft. Pass `version: "new"` to auto-create a draft. The change is only applied to the live saved group when the revision is merged.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "revisionTitle": "string",
  "revisionComment": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "owner": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "projects": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-saved-group-metadata-in-a-draft-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|savedGroupId|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer \| string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» revisionTitle|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`). Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» revisionComment|body|string|false|Markdown. What changed and why, for reviewers. Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» name|body|string|false|Short display name (e.g. `Internal employees`). Put details in `description`.|
|» owner|body|string|false|The userId or email address of the owner. If an email address is provided, it will be used to look up the userId of the matching organization member. If an ID is provided, it will be validated as existing in the organization.|
|» description|body|string|false|Short note (max 100 characters) on who is in the Saved Group and why.|
|» projects|body|[string]|false|none|

## Replace the values list in a list saved group draft revision

<a id="opIdputSavedGroupRevisionValues"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/saved-groups-revisions/string/0/values \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "revisionTitle": "string",
    "revisionComment": "string",
    "values": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/saved-groups-revisions/{savedGroupId}/{version}/values`

Replaces the entire `values` array atomically. Only valid for `list` saved groups. For safe concurrent updates against a draft, prefer `POST .../items/add` and `POST .../items/remove`. Pass `version: "new"` to auto-create a draft.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "revisionTitle": "string",
  "revisionComment": "string",
  "values": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="replace-the-values-list-in-a-list-saved-group-draft-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|savedGroupId|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer \| string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» revisionTitle|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`). Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» revisionComment|body|string|false|Markdown. What changed and why, for reviewers. Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» values|body|[string]|true|none|

## Set the upload a remote saved group draft revision uses

<a id="opIdputSavedGroupRevisionUploadVersion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/saved-groups-revisions/string/0/upload-version \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "revisionTitle": "string",
    "revisionComment": "string",
    "currentUploadVersion": 1
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/saved-groups-revisions/{savedGroupId}/{version}/upload-version`

Stages which upload the group uses. Only valid for `remote` saved groups, and the upload must be valid. Pass `version: "new"` to auto-create a draft.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "revisionTitle": "string",
  "revisionComment": "string",
  "currentUploadVersion": 1
}
```

|body|body|object|true|none|
|» revisionTitle|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`). Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» revisionComment|body|string|false|Markdown. What changed and why, for reviewers. Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|

## Stage an archive/unarchive in a draft revision

<a id="opIdputSavedGroupRevisionArchive"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/saved-groups-revisions/string/0/archive \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "revisionTitle": "string",
    "revisionComment": "string",
    "archived": true,
    "ignoreWarnings": true
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/saved-groups-revisions/{savedGroupId}/{version}/archive`

Stages an archive or unarchive on the draft. Pass `version: "new"` to auto-create a draft. Archived saved groups can be permanently deleted via `DELETE /saved-groups/{id}` once the archive is published.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "revisionTitle": "string",
  "revisionComment": "string",
  "archived": true,
  "ignoreWarnings": true
}
```

<h3 id="stage-an-archiveunarchive-in-a-draft-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|savedGroupId|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer \| string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» revisionTitle|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`). Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» revisionComment|body|string|false|Markdown. What changed and why, for reviewers. Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» archived|body|boolean|true|none|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Append items to a list saved group draft revision

<a id="opIdpostSavedGroupRevisionItemsAdd"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/saved-groups-revisions/string/0/items/add \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "revisionTitle": "string",
    "revisionComment": "string",
    "items": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v1/saved-groups-revisions/{savedGroupId}/{version}/items/add`

Appends the provided items (deduplicated) to the draft's `values` array. Only valid for `list` saved groups. Pass `version: "new"` to auto-create a draft. Duplicate items are merged on top of any existing draft, so multiple successive add/remove calls accumulate.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "revisionTitle": "string",
  "revisionComment": "string",
  "items": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="append-items-to-a-list-saved-group-draft-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|savedGroupId|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer \| string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» revisionTitle|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`). Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» revisionComment|body|string|false|Markdown. What changed and why, for reviewers. Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» items|body|[string]|true|none|

## Request review for a draft revision

<a id="opIdpostSavedGroupRevisionRequestReview"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/saved-groups-revisions/string/0/request-review \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "autoPublishOnApproval": true,
    "ignoreWarnings": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/saved-groups-revisions/{savedGroupId}/{version}/request-review`

Moves the draft from `draft` into `pending-review`. Notifies reviewers per the org's approval-flow settings.

Set `autoPublishOnApproval` to `true` to publish the revision automatically the moment it is approved (GitHub auto-merge model). This requires the org to have auto-publish-on-approval enabled and the caller to have publish permission on the saved group; the auto-publish then executes with the caller's authority.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "autoPublishOnApproval": true,
  "ignoreWarnings": true
}
```

<h3 id="request-review-for-a-draft-revision-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|savedGroupId|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» autoPublishOnApproval|body|boolean|false|none|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Submit a review on a draft revision

<a id="opIdpostSavedGroupRevisionSubmitReview"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/saved-groups-revisions/string/0/submit-review \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "decision": "approve",
    "comment": "string",
    "skipAutoPublish": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/saved-groups-revisions/{savedGroupId}/{version}/submit-review`

Submits an `approve`, `request-changes`, or `comment` review on the revision. The verdict belongs to whoever the request acts as; see [Naming who asked](/api/introduction#naming-who-asked). No one can rule on a draft they created. Submitting `approve` or `request-changes` needs Review access. A `comment` is participation rather than a verdict, so it is also open to the Comments permission or draft authority on the entity. Authors and contributors cannot submit `approve` reviews on their own drafts when the org has `blockSelfApproval` enabled.

When `decision` is `approve` and the revision has `autoPublishOnApproval` enabled, the revision is automatically published after approval. The response includes `autoPublished: true` when this happens. Pass `skipAutoPublish: true` to approve without triggering auto-publish.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "decision": "approve",
  "comment": "string",
  "skipAutoPublish": true
}
```

<h3 id="submit-a-review-on-a-draft-revision-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|savedGroupId|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» decision|body|string|true|none|
|» comment|body|string|false|Markdown. Why you approved, requested changes or commented.|
|» skipAutoPublish|body|boolean|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» decision|approve|
|» decision|request-changes|
|» decision|comment|

## Schedule (or cancel) a deferred publish

<a id="opIdpostSavedGroupRevisionSchedulePublish"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/saved-groups-revisions/string/0/schedule-publish \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "scheduledPublishAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "lockEdits": true,
    "lockOthers": true,
    "bypassApproval": true,
    "ignoreWarnings": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/saved-groups-revisions/{savedGroupId}/{version}/schedule-publish`

Arms a revision to publish automatically at a future time. Pass `scheduledPublishAt` as an RFC3339 timestamp in the future to arm, or `null` to cancel a pending schedule. Requires the `scheduled-revisions` commercial feature and publish permission on the Saved Group. A draft that still requires approval must request review first (or be armed with `bypassApproval` by a caller who can bypass).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "scheduledPublishAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "lockEdits": true,
  "lockOthers": true,
  "bypassApproval": true,
  "ignoreWarnings": true
}
```

<h3 id="schedule-or-cancel-a-deferred-publish-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|savedGroupId|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» scheduledPublishAt|body|string(date-time) \| null|true|When to publish, as an RFC3339 timestamp (e.g. `2026-01-31T09:00:00Z` or `2026-01-31T02:00:00-07:00`), or `null` to cancel a pending schedule.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» lockEdits|body|boolean|false|none|
|» lockOthers|body|boolean|false|none|
|» bypassApproval|body|boolean|false|none|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Retract your own review verdict

<a id="opIdpostSavedGroupRevisionUndoReview"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/saved-groups-revisions/string/0/undo-review \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{}'
```

`POST /v1/saved-groups-revisions/{savedGroupId}/{version}/undo-review`

Retracts the calling user's own active `approve` or `request-changes` verdict, returning the revision to `pending-review`. Review comments stay in the log. Retracting a `request-changes` can leave the revision approved by someone else, in which case an armed auto-publish fires. The verdict belongs to whoever the request acts as; see [Naming who asked](/api/introduction#naming-who-asked). No one can rule on a draft they created.

> Body parameter

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="retract-your-own-review-verdict-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|savedGroupId|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|

## Get merge status for a draft revision

<a id="opIdgetSavedGroupRevisionMergeStatus"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/saved-groups-revisions/string/0/merge-status \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/saved-groups-revisions/{savedGroupId}/{version}/merge-status`

Runs a dry-run merge of the draft against the current live saved group and returns any conflicts. Use this before publishing to preview changes and detect conflicting edits.

    {
      "field": "string",
      "baseValue": null,
      "liveValue": null,
      "proposedValue": null
    }
  ],
  "canAutoMerge": true

## Rebase a draft revision onto the current live saved group

<a id="opIdpostSavedGroupRevisionRebase"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/saved-groups-revisions/string/0/rebase \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "conflictResolutions": {
      "property1": "overwrite",
      "property2": "overwrite"
    },
    "customValues": {
      "property1": [
        null
      ],
      "property2": [
        null
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v1/saved-groups-revisions/{savedGroupId}/{version}/rebase`

Updates the draft's base snapshot to the current live state, applying the draft's changes on top. Supply `conflictResolutions` to resolve any conflicting fields. Strategies are `overwrite` (use the draft's value), `discard` (keep the live value), or `union` (merge arrays — use only on `values`). Optimistic locking is not enforced by this endpoint; callers who need strict locking should call `merge-status` before and after.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "conflictResolutions": {
    "property1": "overwrite",
    "property2": "overwrite"
  },
  "customValues": {
    "property1": [
      null
    ],
    "property2": [
      null
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="rebase-a-draft-revision-onto-the-current-live-saved-group-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|savedGroupId|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» conflictResolutions|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» customValues|body|object|false|Custom values to use for `union` strategy fields. Keyed by field name.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[object]|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » **additionalProperties**|overwrite|
|» » **additionalProperties**|discard|
|» » **additionalProperties**|union|

## Publish a draft revision

<a id="opIdpostSavedGroupRevisionPublish"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/saved-groups-revisions/string/0/publish \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "bypassApproval": true,
    "ignoreWarnings": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/saved-groups-revisions/{savedGroupId}/{version}/publish`

Publishes the draft and applies its changes to the live Saved Group. The caller needs Publish access in every assigned Project. When approval is required, the draft must be approved unless the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. If the organization requires rebasing, an out-of-date draft must be rebased first; an authorized caller can instead send `ignoreWarnings: true` to force-publish it. A 422 response lists every blocking gate and the available resolution.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "bypassApproval": true,
  "ignoreWarnings": true
}
```

<h3 id="publish-a-draft-revision-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|savedGroupId|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» bypassApproval|body|boolean|false|Deprecated and ignored. Approval is bypassed automatically when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access for this resource or when the organization enables the REST API approval bypass. Otherwise, the revision must be approved before it can be published.|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Revert the saved group to a prior revision

<a id="opIdpostSavedGroupRevisionRevert"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/saved-groups-revisions/string/0/revert \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "strategy": "draft",
    "title": "string",
    "comment": "string",
    "ignoreWarnings": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/saved-groups-revisions/{savedGroupId}/{version}/revert`

Creates a new draft (or immediately publishes) whose content matches the specified historical revision. Defaults to creating a draft; when the org enables 'reverts bypass approval' it defaults to publishing immediately. Pass `strategy` to override.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "strategy": "draft",
  "title": "string",
  "comment": "string",
  "ignoreWarnings": true
}
```

<h3 id="revert-the-saved-group-to-a-prior-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|savedGroupId|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» strategy|body|string|false|Whether to stage the revert as a draft or publish it immediately. Defaults to `draft`, or to `publish` when the org enables 'reverts bypass approval'.|
|» title|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`).|
|» comment|body|string|false|Currently ignored. Use `title` to describe the revert.|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» strategy|draft|
|» strategy|publish|

<h1 id="growthbook-rest-api-constants">constants</h1>

**Beta** — these endpoints are new and may change in backwards-incompatible ways.

Reusable named values referenced from feature flag values as `@const:key` and resolved into the SDK payload at build time. String constants are interpolated via `{{ @const:key }}`; JSON (object) constants are composed via an `$extends` array. A constant's own keys **replace** what its `$extends` bases provide, wholesale — constants are atomic building blocks. (Config and feature values compose as deep, targeted patches instead.)

## Create a single constant

<a id="opIdpostConstant"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/constants \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

    "key": "string",
    "name": "string",

    "value": "string",

      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "description": "string",
    "project": "string",
    "owner": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/constants`

> Body parameter

{
  "key": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "type": "string",
  "value": "string",
  "environmentValues": {
    "property1": "string",

}

<h3 id="create-a-single-constant-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» key|body|string|true|Stable reference handle (lowercase slug, unique per org), referenced as `@const:key`|
|» name|body|string|true|The display name of the constant|
|» type|body|string|true|`string` (interpolated as `{{ @const:key }}`) or `json` (substituted as a whole value)|
|» value|body|string|false|none|
|» environmentValues|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|Markdown. Put context here, not in the name.|
|» project|body|string|false|none|
|» owner|body|string|false|The userId or email address of the owner. If an email address is provided, it will be used to look up the userId of the matching organization member. If an ID is provided, it will be validated as existing in the organization. When omitted, it defaults to the requesting member: a personal access token's owner, or the member an organization API key assumes. An organization API key acting as itself leaves it empty.|

## Partially update a single constant

<a id="opIdupdateConstant"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/constants/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "value": "string",
    "environmentValues": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "description": "string",
    "project": "string",
    "owner": "string",
    "bypassApproval": true,
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/constants/{key}`

Applies the change immediately and records it as a published revision, so it appears in history and fires revision webhooks. When the organization requires approvals, open a draft instead or pass `bypassApproval` with the bypass permission.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "value": "string",
  "environmentValues": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "description": "string",
  "project": "string",
  "owner": "string",
  "bypassApproval": true,
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="partially-update-a-single-constant-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|The key of the constant|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|Short display name. Put details in `description`.|
|» value|body|string|false|none|
|» environmentValues|body|object|false|Per-environment value overrides (environment id → value). When provided, this REPLACES the entire override map — send the complete set, not just the environments you want to change (omit the field to leave overrides unchanged).|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|Markdown. Put context here, not in the name.|
|» project|body|string|false|none|
|» owner|body|string|false|The userId or email address of the owner. If an email address is provided, it will be used to look up the userId of the matching organization member. If an ID is provided, it will be validated as existing in the organization.|
|» bypassApproval|body|boolean|false|Set to true to write directly to the live Constant without approval. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access in the Constant's Project, unless the organization enables the REST API approval bypass. This field has no effect when approval is not required.|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "constant": {
    "id": "string",
    "key": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "type": "string",
    "owner": "string",
    "ownerEmail": "string",
    "value": "string",
    "environmentValues": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "description": "string",
    "project": "string",
    "archived": true,
    "dateCreated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "dateUpdated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  },
  "bypassedGates": [
    {
      "type": "string",
      "outcome": "bypassed",
      "via": "ignoreWarnings"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "confirmation": {
    "id": "string",
    "status": "pending",
    "actions": [
      {
        "action": "feature.create",
        "environments": [
          "string"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "summary": "string",
    "url": "string",
    "expiresAt": "string",
    "response": {
      "status": 0,
      "body": null
    },
    "note": "string"
  },
  "message": "string"
}
```

## Unarchive a single constant

<a id="opIdunarchiveConstant"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/constants/string/unarchive \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/constants/{key}/unarchive`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="unarchive-a-single-constant-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|The key of the constant|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "constant": {
    "id": "string",
    "key": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "type": "string",
    "owner": "string",
    "ownerEmail": "string",
    "value": "string",
    "environmentValues": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "description": "string",
    "project": "string",
    "archived": true,
    "dateCreated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "dateUpdated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  },
  "bypassedGates": [
    {
      "type": "string",
      "outcome": "bypassed",
      "via": "ignoreWarnings"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h1 id="growthbook-rest-api-constant-revisions">constant-revisions</h1>

**Beta** — these endpoints are new and may change in backwards-incompatible ways.

Draft revisions for constants, including pending changes, approvals, and lifecycle (publish, discard, revert). Pass `version: "new"` on edit endpoints to auto-create a draft.

## List constant revisions across the organization

<a id="opIdlistConstantRevisions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/constants-revisions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/constants-revisions`

Returns a paginated list of revisions across all constants in the organization, sorted newest-first. Optionally filtered by constant, status, author, or the calling user's involvement.

<h3 id="list-constant-revisions-across-the-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of items to return|
|offset|query|integer|false|How many items to skip (use in conjunction with limit for pagination)|
|skipPagination|query|string \| boolean|false|If true, return all matching items and ignore limit/offset.<br>Self-hosted only. Has no effect unless API_ALLOW_SKIP_PAGINATION is set to true or 1.|
|key|query|string|false|Restrict results to revisions for a single constant (by its key). When omitted, returns revisions across every constant the caller can read.|
|status|query|string|false|Filter by revision status. Accepts a comma-separated list, or the literal `open` for non-merged/non-discarded revisions.|
|author|query|string|false|none|
|mine|query|string \| boolean|false|If true, return only revisions authored by the calling user. Needs a personal access token, or an organization API key that assumes a named member's role. Mutually exclusive with `author`.|

## Create a draft revision

<a id="opIdpostConstantRevision"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/constants-revisions/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "title": "string",
    "comment": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/constants-revisions/{key}`

Creates a new draft revision branched from the current live constant. A constant can have multiple concurrent drafts; use this to start an isolated line of edits.

  "comment": "string"
}

## Get the most recent active draft revision

<a id="opIdgetConstantRevisionLatest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/constants-revisions/string/latest \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/constants-revisions/{key}/latest`

Returns the most recently updated open (non-merged, non-discarded) revision for the constant. Returns 404 if there is no active draft. Pass `mine=true` to restrict to drafts authored by the calling user. Needs a personal access token, or an organization API key that assumes a named member's role.

|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|mine|query|string \| boolean|false|If true, return only the most recent active draft authored by the calling user. Needs a personal access token, or an organization API key that assumes a named member's role.|

## Update constant metadata in a draft revision

<a id="opIdputConstantRevisionMetadata"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/constants-revisions/string/0/metadata \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "revisionTitle": "string",
    "revisionComment": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "owner": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "project": "string"
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/constants-revisions/{key}/{version}/metadata`

Stages metadata changes (name, owner, description, project) on the draft. Pass `version: "new"` to auto-create a draft. The change is only applied to the live constant when the revision is merged.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "revisionTitle": "string",
  "revisionComment": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "owner": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "project": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-constant-metadata-in-a-draft-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer \| string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» revisionTitle|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`). Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» revisionComment|body|string|false|Markdown. What changed and why, for reviewers. Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» name|body|string|false|Short display name. Put details in `description`.|
|» owner|body|string|false|The userId or email address of the owner. If an email address is provided, it will be used to look up the userId of the matching organization member. If an ID is provided, it will be validated as existing in the organization.|
|» description|body|string|false|Markdown. Put context here, not in the name.|
|» project|body|string|false|none|

## Update the value of a constant draft revision

<a id="opIdputConstantRevisionValue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/constants-revisions/string/0/value \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "revisionTitle": "string",
    "revisionComment": "string",
    "value": "string",
    "environmentValues": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/constants-revisions/{key}/{version}/value`

Stages a new default `value` and/or per-environment `environmentValues` on the draft. At least one must be supplied. Pass `version: "new"` to auto-create a draft. The value must match the constant's type (valid JSON for `json` constants).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "revisionTitle": "string",
  "revisionComment": "string",
  "value": "string",
  "environmentValues": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-value-of-a-constant-draft-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer \| string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» revisionTitle|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`). Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» revisionComment|body|string|false|Markdown. What changed and why, for reviewers. Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» value|body|string|false|The default value (raw string for `string` constants, JSON-encoded for `json` constants)|
|» environmentValues|body|object|false|Per-environment value overrides (environment id → value)|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

## Stage an archive/unarchive in a draft revision

<a id="opIdputConstantRevisionArchive"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/constants-revisions/string/0/archive \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "revisionTitle": "string",
    "revisionComment": "string",
    "archived": true,
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/constants-revisions/{key}/{version}/archive`

Stages an archive or unarchive on the draft. Pass `version: "new"` to auto-create a draft. Archived constants can be permanently deleted via `DELETE /constants/{key}` once the archive is published.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "revisionTitle": "string",
  "revisionComment": "string",
  "archived": true,
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="stage-an-archiveunarchive-in-a-draft-revision-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer \| string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» revisionTitle|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`). Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» revisionComment|body|string|false|Markdown. What changed and why, for reviewers. Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» archived|body|boolean|true|none|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Request review for a draft revision

<a id="opIdpostConstantRevisionRequestReview"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/constants-revisions/string/0/request-review \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "autoPublishOnApproval": true,
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/constants-revisions/{key}/{version}/request-review`

Moves the draft from `draft` into `pending-review`. Notifies reviewers per the org's approval-flow settings.

Set `autoPublishOnApproval` to `true` to publish the revision automatically the moment it is approved. This requires the org to have auto-publish-on-approval enabled and the caller to have publish permission on the constant.

> Body parameter

  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}

The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. ## Submit a review on a draft revision

<a id="opIdpostConstantRevisionSubmitReview"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/constants-revisions/string/0/submit-review \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "decision": "approve",
    "comment": "string",
    "skipAutoPublish": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/constants-revisions/{key}/{version}/submit-review`

Submits an `approve`, `request-changes`, or `comment` review on the revision. The verdict belongs to whoever the request acts as; see [Naming who asked](/api/introduction#naming-who-asked). No one can rule on a draft they created. Submitting `approve` or `request-changes` needs Review access. A `comment` is participation rather than a verdict, so it is also open to the Comments permission or draft authority on the entity. Authors and contributors cannot submit `approve` reviews on their own drafts when the org has `blockSelfApproval` enabled.

When `decision` is `approve` and the revision has `autoPublishOnApproval` enabled, the revision is automatically published after approval. The response includes `autoPublished: true` when this happens. Pass `skipAutoPublish: true` to approve without triggering auto-publish.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "decision": "approve",
  "comment": "string",
  "skipAutoPublish": true
}
```

<h3 id="submit-a-review-on-a-draft-revision-3-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» decision|body|string|true|none|
|» comment|body|string|false|Markdown. Why you approved, requested changes or commented.|
|» skipAutoPublish|body|boolean|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» decision|approve|
|» decision|request-changes|
|» decision|comment|

> 200 Response

```json

    ],

## Schedule (or cancel) a deferred publish

<a id="opIdpostConstantRevisionSchedulePublish"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/constants-revisions/string/0/schedule-publish \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "scheduledPublishAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "lockEdits": true,
    "lockOthers": true,
    "bypassApproval": true,
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/constants-revisions/{key}/{version}/schedule-publish`

Arms a revision to publish automatically at a future time. Pass `scheduledPublishAt` as an RFC3339 timestamp in the future to arm, or `null` to cancel a pending schedule. Requires the `scheduled-revisions` commercial feature and publish permission on the Constant. A draft that still requires approval must request review first (or be armed with `bypassApproval` by a caller who can bypass).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "scheduledPublishAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "lockEdits": true,
  "lockOthers": true,
  "bypassApproval": true,
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="schedule-or-cancel-a-deferred-publish-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» scheduledPublishAt|body|string(date-time) \| null|true|When to publish, as an RFC3339 timestamp (e.g. `2026-01-31T09:00:00Z` or `2026-01-31T02:00:00-07:00`), or `null` to cancel a pending schedule.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» lockEdits|body|boolean|false|none|
|» lockOthers|body|boolean|false|none|
|» bypassApproval|body|boolean|false|none|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Retract your own review verdict

<a id="opIdpostConstantRevisionUndoReview"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/constants-revisions/string/0/undo-review \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{}'
```

`POST /v1/constants-revisions/{key}/{version}/undo-review`

Retracts the calling user's own active `approve` or `request-changes` verdict, returning the revision to `pending-review`. Review comments stay in the log. Retracting a `request-changes` can leave the revision approved by someone else, in which case an armed auto-publish fires. The verdict belongs to whoever the request acts as; see [Naming who asked](/api/introduction#naming-who-asked). No one can rule on a draft they created.

> Body parameter

```json
{}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|

`GET /v1/constants-revisions/{key}/{version}/merge-status`

## Rebase a draft revision onto the current live constant

<a id="opIdpostConstantRevisionRebase"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/constants-revisions/string/0/rebase \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "conflictResolutions": {
      "property1": "overwrite",
      "property2": "overwrite"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v1/constants-revisions/{key}/{version}/rebase`

Updates the draft's base snapshot to the current live state, applying the draft's changes on top. Supply `conflictResolutions` to resolve any conflicting fields. Strategies are `overwrite` (use the draft's value) or `discard` (keep the live value).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "conflictResolutions": {
    "property1": "overwrite",
    "property2": "overwrite"
  }
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» conflictResolutions|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » **additionalProperties**|overwrite|
|» » **additionalProperties**|discard|

## Publish a draft revision

<a id="opIdpostConstantRevisionPublish"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/constants-revisions/string/0/publish \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "bypassApproval": true,
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/constants-revisions/{key}/{version}/publish`

Publishes the draft and makes its changes live. The caller needs Publish access for the affected environments. When approval is required, the draft must be approved unless the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. If the organization requires rebasing, an out-of-date draft must be rebased first; an authorized caller can instead send `ignoreWarnings: true` to force-publish it. A 422 response lists every blocking gate and the available resolution.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "bypassApproval": true,
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="publish-a-draft-revision-3-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» bypassApproval|body|boolean|false|Deprecated and ignored. Approval is bypassed automatically when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access for this resource or when the organization enables the REST API approval bypass. Otherwise, the revision must be approved before it can be published.|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

> Example responses

## Revert the constant to a prior revision

<a id="opIdpostConstantRevisionRevert"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/constants-revisions/string/0/revert \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "strategy": "draft",
    "title": "string",
    "comment": "string",
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/constants-revisions/{key}/{version}/revert`

Creates a new draft (or immediately publishes) whose content matches the specified historical revision. Defaults to creating a draft; when the org enables 'reverts bypass approval' it defaults to publishing immediately. Pass `strategy` to override.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "strategy": "draft",
  "title": "string",
  "comment": "string",
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="revert-the-constant-to-a-prior-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» strategy|body|string|false|Whether to stage the revert as a draft or publish it immediately. Defaults to `draft`, or to `publish` when the org enables 'reverts bypass approval'.|
|» title|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`).|
|» comment|body|string|false|Currently ignored. Use `title` to describe the revert.|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» strategy|draft|
|» strategy|publish|

<h1 id="growthbook-rest-api-configs">configs</h1>

**Beta** — these endpoints are new and may change in backwards-incompatible ways.

Reusable, typed, inheritable JSON objects referenced from feature flag values as `@config:key`. A config carries a field `schema` (with TypeScript/JSON Schema import-export) and a lineage `parent`. Inheritance is expressed via `parent`, never an in-value `@config:` entry. Values layer as a **deep, targeted patch**: a child (or a config-backed feature value) restates only the leaves it changes and inherits the rest — unlike a constant's `$extends`, whose own keys replace wholesale. Schema fields colliding with a published ancestor's key follow 'base wins': identical re-declarations are stripped with a warning, differing ones are rejected.

    }

<h3 id="create-a-single-config-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|skipSchemaValidation|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `skipSchemaValidation` in the request body instead.|
|ignoreWarnings|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `ignoreWarnings` in the request body instead.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» key|body|string|true|Stable reference handle (lowercase slug, unique per org), referenced as `@config:key`|
|» name|body|string|true|The display name of the config|
|» parent|body|string|false|The `key` of the config to inherit from (the primary lineage spine). Express inheritance via `parent`/`extends`, NEVER via a `@config:` entry in `value` (which is rejected).|
|» extends|body|[string]|false|Additional composition bases (config `key`s) layered on top of `parent`, in precedence order (later overrides earlier; all override `parent`; own keys win last). Set inheritance here, never via a `@config:` entry in `value`.|
|» value|body|object|false|This config's base value as a JSON object. Per-environment/project variants are expressed via `scopedOverrides`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» scopedOverrides|body|[object]|false|Ordered, first-match-wins environment/project-scoped variant selection. Each entry points at a flavor config (a child config, by `key`) whose value is deep-merged onto this config's resolved value when the (environment, project) scope matches — resolved at build time, per layer. This is how you create an environment-scoped override (as opposed to a plain child config): make a child config for the override value, then add it here with its scope. Send the complete list to replace it; an empty array clears all overrides. Entries must reference existing configs, may not reference this config itself, and may not be unreachable (fully subsumed by an earlier entry).|
|» » config|body|string|true|The `key` of the flavor config (a child config) whose value patches this config when the scope matches.|
|» » environments|body|[string]|false|Environment ids this entry applies to. Empty/omitted = any environment.|
|» » projects|body|[string]|false|Project ids this entry applies to. Empty/omitted = any project.|
|» description|body|string|false|Markdown. Put context here, not in the name.|
|» project|body|string|false|none|
|» owner|body|string|false|The userId or email address of the owner. If an email address is provided, it will be used to look up the userId of the matching organization member. If an ID is provided, it will be validated as existing in the organization. When omitted, it defaults to the requesting member: a personal access token's owner, or the member an organization API key assumes. An organization API key acting as itself leaves it empty.|
|» schema|body|[ConfigSchemaSource](#schemaconfigschemasource)|false|Field definitions for this config, as a JSON Schema document (`{ type: "json-schema", value }`) or typed-code source (`{ type: "typescript" \| "protobuf" \| "python" \| "go" \| "rust", value }`) — converted server-side in one call. Fields whose key an ancestor (via `parent`/`extends`) already owns follow "base wins": an identical re-declaration is stripped with a `redundant-declaration` warning; one with a differing definition is rejected. A field owned by two sibling bases is a conflict and is rejected. Omit to leave the config schema-less. Conversion warnings are returned in `warnings`.|
|» source|body|string|false|Optional identifier of the consuming codebase/service. When a typed-code schema (`typescript`/`protobuf`/`python`/`go`/`rust`) is supplied, its named-type structure is captured under this source so `GET /configs/:key/schema?source=<id>&format=<lang>` can reproduce those names.|
|» extensible|body|boolean|false|none|
|» experimentGuard|body|boolean|false|Enable the experiment guard on this config: publishing a change served to a running experiment soft-blocks unless overridden. Omit to inherit the org default.|
|» invariants|body|[object]|false|Cross-field validation rules. Each rule's expression is a mongo condition (mongrule). Stored on the config schema and enforced at publish.|
|» » name|body|string|true|none|
|» » rule|body|object|true|The rule expression, as a mongo condition (mongrule) — the same condition syntax as feature targeting, extended with `{ "$ref": "otherField" }` to compare against another field, e.g. `{ "min_replicas": { "$lte": { "$ref": "max_replicas" } } }`.|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » message|body|string|false|Shown to editors when the rule is violated. Optional — defaults to a generic message naming the rule.|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

  -X POST \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{

      "type": "json-schema",
      "value": {
        "property1": null,
        "property2": null
      }
    }
  }'
```

      "property2": null

      }

    {
      "key": "string",

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|format|go|
|format|rust|
