`POST /v1/configs/{key}`

Applies the change immediately and records it as a published revision, so it appears in history and fires revision webhooks. When the organization requires approvals, open a draft instead or pass `bypassApproval` with the bypass permission.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "parent": "string",
  "extends": [
    "string"
  ],
  "value": {
    "property1": null,
    "property2": null
  },
  "scopedOverrides": [
    {
      "config": "string",
      "environments": [
        "string"
      ],
      "projects": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "description": "string",
  "project": "string",
  "owner": "string",
  "schema": {
    "type": "json-schema",
    "value": {
      "property1": null,
      "property2": null
    }
  },
  "source": "string",
  "extensible": true,
  "experimentGuard": true,
  "invariants": [
    {
      "name": "string",
      "rule": {
        "property1": null,
        "property2": null
      },
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "bypassApproval": true,
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="partially-update-a-single-config-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|The key of the config|
|skipSchemaValidation|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `skipSchemaValidation` in the request body instead.|
|ignoreWarnings|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `ignoreWarnings` in the request body instead.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|Short display name. Put details in `description`.|
|» parent|body|string|false|Change the lineage parent (the `key` of the config to inherit from). Set to an empty string to detach from the parent and make this a root config.|
|» extends|body|[string]|false|Replace the composition bases (mixins) layered on top of `parent`, in precedence order (later overrides earlier; all override `parent`; own keys win last). Send the complete set; an empty array clears all mixins. Set inheritance here, never via a `@config:` entry in `value`.|
|» value|body|object|false|This config's base value as a JSON object. Per-environment/project variants are expressed via `scopedOverrides`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» scopedOverrides|body|[object]|false|Replace the ordered, first-match-wins environment/project-scoped variant selection. Each entry points at a flavor config (a child config, by `key`) whose value is deep-merged onto this config's resolved value when the (environment, project) scope matches. Send the complete list; an empty array clears all overrides; omit to leave unchanged. Entries must reference existing configs, may not reference this config itself, and may not be unreachable.|
|» » config|body|string|true|The `key` of the flavor config (a child config) whose value patches this config when the scope matches.|
|» » environments|body|[string]|false|Environment ids this entry applies to. Empty/omitted = any environment.|
|» » projects|body|[string]|false|Project ids this entry applies to. Empty/omitted = any project.|
|» description|body|string|false|Markdown. Put context here, not in the name.|
|» project|body|string|false|none|
|» owner|body|string|false|The userId or email address of the owner. If an email address is provided, it will be used to look up the userId of the matching organization member. If an ID is provided, it will be validated as existing in the organization.|
|» schema|body|[ConfigSchemaSource](#schemaconfigschemasource)|false|Replace this config's field definitions, as a JSON Schema document (`{ type: "json-schema", value }`) or typed-code source (`{ type: "typescript" \| "protobuf" \| "python" \| "go" \| "rust", value }`). Fields whose key a published ancestor already owns follow "base wins": an identical re-declaration is stripped with a `redundant-declaration` warning; one with a differing definition is rejected. A schema change cascades the 'base wins' normalization to descendants when published; a change that removes or retypes fields descendants still use soft-blocks with a 422 unless the request body sets `ignoreWarnings: true`. Conversion warnings are returned in `warnings`.|
|» source|body|string|false|Optional identifier of the consuming codebase/service. When a `typescript` or `protobuf` schema is supplied, its named-type structure is captured under this source for reproduction on export.|
|» extensible|body|boolean|false|none|
|» experimentGuard|body|boolean|false|Enable or disable the experiment guard for this Config. Disabling it requires Bypass draft approvals access.|
|» invariants|body|[object]|false|Replace the config's cross-field validation rules. Each rule's expression is a mongo condition (mongrule). Send the complete set; an empty array clears all rules. Omit to leave them unchanged.|
|» » name|body|string|true|none|
|» » rule|body|object|true|The rule expression, as a mongo condition (mongrule) — the same condition syntax as feature targeting, extended with `{ "$ref": "otherField" }` to compare against another field, e.g. `{ "min_replicas": { "$lte": { "$ref": "max_replicas" } } }`.|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » message|body|string|false|Shown to editors when the rule is violated. Optional — defaults to a generic message naming the rule.|
|» bypassApproval|body|boolean|false|Set to true to write directly to the live Config without approval. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access in the Config's Project, unless the organization enables the REST API approval bypass. This field has no effect when approval is not required.|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Archive a single config

<a id="opIdarchiveConfig"></a>

```bash
  }'
```

`POST /v1/configs/{key}/archive`

Archives a config. A child config (including an environment/project override) is archived outright when its live value is an empty patch or nothing serves it. When archiving would strip a value that live features or other configs still consume, the request returns a 422 listing the blocking gates — re-submit with `"ignoreWarnings": true` in the request body to acknowledge and proceed. A locked config, or one whose org requires approval, returns its own gate (unlock or route the change through a draft revision).

> Body parameter

```json

  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Lock a config at its current published revision

<a id="opIdlockConfig"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/configs/string/lock \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "reason": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/configs/{key}/lock`

Locks the Config to its current published revision. Drafts can still be created and edited, but direct updates, publishes, scheduled publishes, reverts, and archives are blocked. The response returns the pinned revision in `lockedRevision`. Unlocking requires Bypass draft approvals access.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "reason": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="lock-a-config-at-its-current-published-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|The key of the config|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» reason|body|string|false|Optional note explaining why the config was locked.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "config": {
    "id": "string",
    "key": "string",
```

<h1 id="growthbook-rest-api-config-revisions">config-revisions</h1>

**Beta** — these endpoints are new and may change in backwards-incompatible ways.

Draft revisions for configs, including value and schema edits, schema import (JSON Schema / TypeScript / inferred), approvals, and lifecycle (publish, discard, revert). Publishing a schema change cascades the "base wins" normalization to descendant configs; a publish that removes or retypes fields descendants still use soft-blocks with a 422 unless the request body sets `ignoreWarnings: true`. Pass `version: "new"` on edit endpoints to auto-create a draft.

## List config revisions across the organization

<a id="opIdlistConfigRevisions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/configs-revisions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/configs-revisions`

Returns a paginated list of revisions across all configs in the organization, sorted newest-first. Optionally filtered by config, status, author, or the calling user's involvement.

<h3 id="list-config-revisions-across-the-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of items to return|
|offset|query|integer|false|How many items to skip (use in conjunction with limit for pagination)|
|skipPagination|query|string \| boolean|false|If true, return all matching items and ignore limit/offset.<br>Self-hosted only. Has no effect unless API_ALLOW_SKIP_PAGINATION is set to true or 1.|
|key|query|string|false|Restrict results to revisions for a single config (by its key). When omitted, returns revisions across every config the caller can read.|
|status|query|string|false|Filter by revision status. Accepts a comma-separated list, or the literal `open` for non-merged/non-discarded revisions.|
|author|query|string|false|none|
|mine|query|string \| boolean|false|If true, return only revisions authored by the calling user. Needs a personal access token, or an organization API key that assumes a named member's role. Mutually exclusive with `author`.|

## Create a draft revision

<a id="opIdpostConfigRevision"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/configs-revisions/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "title": "string",
    "comment": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/configs-revisions/{key}`

Creates a new draft revision branched from the current live config. A config can have multiple concurrent drafts; use this to start an isolated line of edits.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "string",
  "comment": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-draft-revision-4-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» title|body|string|false|none|
|» comment|body|string|false|none|

## Get the most recent active draft revision

<a id="opIdgetConfigRevisionLatest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/configs-revisions/string/latest \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/configs-revisions/{key}/latest`

Returns the most recently updated open (non-merged, non-discarded) revision for the config. Returns 404 if there is no active draft. Pass `mine=true` to restrict to drafts authored by the calling user. Needs a personal access token, or an organization API key that assumes a named member's role.

<h3 id="get-the-most-recent-active-draft-revision-4-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|mine|query|string \| boolean|false|If true, return only the most recent active draft authored by the calling user. Needs a personal access token, or an organization API key that assumes a named member's role.|

## Update config metadata in a draft revision

<a id="opIdputConfigRevisionMetadata"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/configs-revisions/string/0/metadata \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "revisionTitle": "string",
    "revisionComment": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "owner": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "project": "string",
    "parent": "string",
    "extends": [
      "string"
    ],
    "extensible": true,
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/configs-revisions/{key}/{version}/metadata`

Stages metadata changes (name, owner, description, project, lineage parent, extensibility) on the draft. Pass `version: "new"` to auto-create a draft. The change is only applied to the live config when the revision is merged.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "revisionTitle": "string",
  "revisionComment": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "owner": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "project": "string",
  "parent": "string",
  "extends": [
    "string"
  ],
  "extensible": true,
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-config-metadata-in-a-draft-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer \| string|true|none|
|skipSchemaValidation|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `skipSchemaValidation` in the request body instead.|
|ignoreWarnings|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `ignoreWarnings` in the request body instead.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» revisionTitle|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`). Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» revisionComment|body|string|false|Markdown. What changed and why, for reviewers. Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» name|body|string|false|Short display name. Put details in `description`.|
|» owner|body|string|false|The userId or email address of the owner. If an email address is provided, it will be used to look up the userId of the matching organization member. If an ID is provided, it will be validated as existing in the organization.|
|» description|body|string|false|Markdown. Put context here, not in the name.|
|» project|body|string|false|none|
|» parent|body|string|false|Change the lineage parent (the `key` to inherit from). Empty string detaches from the parent.|
|» extends|body|[string]|false|Replace the composition mixins layered on top of `parent`, in precedence order (later overrides earlier; all override `parent`; own keys win last). Send the complete set; an empty array clears all mixins.|
|» extensible|body|boolean|false|none|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Update the value of a config draft revision

<a id="opIdputConfigRevisionValue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/configs-revisions/string/0/value \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "revisionTitle": "string",
    "revisionComment": "string",
    "value": {
      "property1": null,
      "property2": null
    },
    "inferSchemaIfMissing": true,
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/configs-revisions/{key}/{version}/value`

Stages a new `value` (this config's own JSON object) on the draft. Pass `version: "new"` to auto-create a draft. A `@config:` inheritance entry in the value is rejected — express lineage via the `parent`/`extends` metadata fields instead. Configs are environment-agnostic: there is no per-environment override (use a Constant for that).

Inheritance is a deep (targeted) patch: this value is merged onto the resolved parent recursively, key by key — restate only the leaves you want to change and the rest are inherited. Arrays and scalars replace wholesale, `null` is a value (it does not delete a key), and a value composed from a constant via `$extends` is applied whole.

Set `inferSchemaIfMissing: true` to derive and stage a field schema from the value when the config has none yet.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "revisionTitle": "string",
  "revisionComment": "string",
  "value": {
    "property1": null,
    "property2": null
  },
  "inferSchemaIfMissing": true,
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-value-of-a-config-draft-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer \| string|true|none|
|skipSchemaValidation|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `skipSchemaValidation` in the request body instead.|
|ignoreWarnings|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `ignoreWarnings` in the request body instead.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» revisionTitle|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`). Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» revisionComment|body|string|false|Markdown. What changed and why, for reviewers. Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» value|body|object|false|This config's own value as a JSON object — a targeted patch deep-merged onto the resolved parent value.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» inferSchemaIfMissing|body|boolean|false|When the config has no schema yet, infer one from the supplied `value` and stage it on the same draft.|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/configs-revisions/string/0/property \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "revisionTitle": "string",
    "revisionComment": "string",
    "property": "string",
    "value": null,
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/configs-revisions/{key}/{version}/property`

Stages a single property of this config's own value on the draft, leaving every other property untouched. Prefer this over `PUT .../value` when changing one field: a whole-value write from a stale read silently drops properties someone else added in the meantime.

`null` is a value (it does not remove the property) — use `DELETE .../property` to remove one. Pass `version: "new"` to auto-create a draft.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "revisionTitle": "string",
  "revisionComment": "string",
  "property": "string",
  "value": null,
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="set-one-property-of-a-config-draft-revisions-value-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer \| string|true|none|
|skipSchemaValidation|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `skipSchemaValidation` in the request body instead.|
|ignoreWarnings|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `ignoreWarnings` in the request body instead.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» revisionTitle|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`). Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» revisionComment|body|string|false|Markdown. What changed and why, for reviewers. Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» property|body|string|true|Name of the property to set in this config's own value.|
|» value|body|object|true|The property's new value. `null` sets it to null.|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Remove one property from a config draft revision's value

<a id="opIddeleteConfigRevisionProperty"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/configs-revisions/string/0/property?property=string' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v1/configs-revisions/{key}/{version}/property`

## Update or import the schema of a config draft revision

<a id="opIdputConfigRevisionSchema"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/configs-revisions/string/0/schema \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "revisionTitle": "string",
    "revisionComment": "string",
    "schema": {
      "type": "json-schema",
      "value": {
        "property1": null,
        "property2": null
      }
    },
    "infer": true,
    "additionalProperties": true,
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/configs-revisions/{key}/{version}/schema`

Stages this config's field schema on the draft. Provide exactly ONE source:
- `schema`: a schema document — `{ type: "json-schema", value }` (a JSON Schema object) or `{ type: "typescript", value }` (TypeScript source). **JSON Schema is the recommended ("happy path") format** — it is the canonical pivot, preserves nested objects/arrays, and resolves local `$ref`/`$defs` (so generator output with referenced types works). `typescript` is a best-effort convenience parser. All conversions are lossy-by-design and degrade exotic constructs to permissive types WITH warnings (returned in `warnings`).
- `infer: true`: derive the schema from the draft's value.

Fields whose key a published ancestor already owns follow "base wins": an identical re-declaration is stripped with a `redundant-declaration` warning; one with a differing definition is rejected. Pass `version: "new"` to auto-create a draft.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "revisionTitle": "string",
  "revisionComment": "string",
  "schema": {
    "type": "json-schema",
    "value": {
      "property1": null,
      "property2": null
    }
  },
  "infer": true,
  "additionalProperties": true,
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-or-import-the-schema-of-a-config-draft-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer \| string|true|none|
|skipSchemaValidation|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `skipSchemaValidation` in the request body instead.|
|ignoreWarnings|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `ignoreWarnings` in the request body instead.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» revisionTitle|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`). Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» revisionComment|body|string|false|Markdown. What changed and why, for reviewers. Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» schema|body|[ConfigSchemaSource](#schemaconfigschemasource)|false|none|
|» infer|body|boolean|false|Derive the schema from the draft's value instead.|
|» additionalProperties|body|boolean|false|Whether the resulting object schema permits extra keys (family extensibility).|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

> 200 Response

```json
    "id": "string",

    "author": {
```

## Set (or update) a config's per-source render projection on a draft

<a id="opIdputConfigRevisionProjection"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/configs-revisions/string/0/projection \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "revisionTitle": "string",
    "revisionComment": "string",
    "source": "string",
    "schema": {
      "type": "json-schema",
      "value": {
        "property1": null,
        "property2": null
      }
    },
    "additionalProperties": true,
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/configs-revisions/{key}/{version}/projection`

Stages a per-source render projection on the draft, AND the schema it implies. Provide a named `schema` source (`{ type: "typescript" | "protobuf" | "python" | "go" | "rust" | "json-schema", value }`) for the consuming codebase identified by `source`: GrowthBook derives the config's canonical schema from it (so the change projects into the Config) and captures that source's named-type structure under `renderProjections[source]`. Both are staged on the draft and published through the normal flow. Pass `version: "new"` to auto-create a draft. Lossy conversions degrade with `warnings`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "revisionTitle": "string",
  "revisionComment": "string",
  "source": "string",
  "schema": {
    "type": "json-schema",
    "value": {
      "property1": null,
      "property2": null
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": true,
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="set-or-update-a-configs-per-source-render-projection-on-a-draft-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer \| string|true|none|
|skipSchemaValidation|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `skipSchemaValidation` in the request body instead.|
|ignoreWarnings|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `ignoreWarnings` in the request body instead.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» revisionTitle|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`). Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» revisionComment|body|string|false|Markdown. What changed and why, for reviewers. Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» source|body|string|true|Identifier of the consuming codebase/service this projection belongs to.|
|» schema|body|[ConfigSchemaSource](#schemaconfigschemasource)|true|The named schema source for this projection. Its type names are captured; its structure derives the config's canonical schema.|
|» additionalProperties|body|boolean|false|Whether the resulting object schema permits extra keys (family extensibility).|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Remove a config's per-source render projection on a draft

<a id="opIddeleteConfigRevisionProjection"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/configs-revisions/string/0/projection?source=string' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v1/configs-revisions/{key}/{version}/projection`

Stages removal of the `source` projection from `renderProjections` on the draft (the canonical schema is unchanged). Published through the normal flow. Pass `version: "new"` to auto-create a draft.

<h3 id="remove-a-configs-per-source-render-projection-on-a-draft-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer \| string|true|none|
|source|query|string|true|Identifier of the projection (source) to remove.|

## Stage an archive/unarchive in a draft revision

<a id="opIdputConfigRevisionArchive"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/configs-revisions/string/0/archive \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "revisionTitle": "string",
    "revisionComment": "string",
    "archived": true,
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/configs-revisions/{key}/{version}/archive`

Stages an archive or unarchive on the draft. Pass `version: "new"` to auto-create a draft. Archived configs can be permanently deleted via `DELETE /configs/{key}` once the archive is published.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "revisionTitle": "string",
  "revisionComment": "string",
  "archived": true,
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="stage-an-archiveunarchive-in-a-draft-revision-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer \| string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» revisionTitle|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`). Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» revisionComment|body|string|false|Markdown. What changed and why, for reviewers. Only used when `version` is "new"; ignored for existing drafts.|
|» archived|body|boolean|true|none|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Request review for a draft revision

<a id="opIdpostConfigRevisionRequestReview"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/configs-revisions/string/0/request-review \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "autoPublishOnApproval": true,
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/configs-revisions/{key}/{version}/request-review`

Moves the draft from `draft` into `pending-review`. Notifies reviewers per the org's approval-flow settings.

Set `autoPublishOnApproval` to `true` to publish the revision automatically the moment it is approved. This requires the org to have auto-publish-on-approval enabled and the caller to have publish permission on the config.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "autoPublishOnApproval": true,
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="request-review-for-a-draft-revision-4-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» autoPublishOnApproval|body|boolean|false|none|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Submit a review on a draft revision

<a id="opIdpostConfigRevisionSubmitReview"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/configs-revisions/string/0/submit-review \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "decision": "approve",
    "comment": "string",
    "skipAutoPublish": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/configs-revisions/{key}/{version}/submit-review`

Submits an `approve`, `request-changes`, or `comment` review on the revision. The verdict belongs to whoever the request acts as; see [Naming who asked](/api/introduction#naming-who-asked). No one can rule on a draft they created. Submitting `approve` or `request-changes` needs Review access. A `comment` is participation rather than a verdict, so it is also open to the Comments permission or draft authority on the entity. Authors and contributors cannot submit `approve` reviews on their own drafts when the org has `blockSelfApproval` enabled.

When `decision` is `approve` and the revision has `autoPublishOnApproval` enabled, the revision is automatically published after approval. The response includes `autoPublished: true` when this happens. Pass `skipAutoPublish: true` to approve without triggering auto-publish.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "decision": "approve",
  "comment": "string",
  "skipAutoPublish": true
}
```

<h3 id="submit-a-review-on-a-draft-revision-4-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» decision|body|string|true|none|
|» comment|body|string|false|Markdown. Why you approved, requested changes or commented.|
|» skipAutoPublish|body|boolean|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» decision|approve|
|» decision|request-changes|
|» decision|comment|

## Retract your own review verdict

<a id="opIdpostConfigRevisionUndoReview"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/configs-revisions/string/0/undo-review \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{}'
```

`POST /v1/configs-revisions/{key}/{version}/undo-review`

Retracts the calling user's own active `approve` or `request-changes` verdict, returning the revision to `pending-review`. Review comments stay in the log. Retracting a `request-changes` can leave the revision approved by someone else, in which case an armed auto-publish fires. The verdict belongs to whoever the request acts as; see [Naming who asked](/api/introduction#naming-who-asked). No one can rule on a draft they created.

> Body parameter

```json
{}
```

|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|

## Schedule (or cancel) a deferred publish

<a id="opIdpostConfigRevisionSchedulePublish"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/configs-revisions/string/0/schedule-publish \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "scheduledPublishAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "lockEdits": true,
    "lockOthers": true,
    "bypassApproval": true,
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/configs-revisions/{key}/{version}/schedule-publish`

Arms a revision to publish automatically at a future time. Pass `scheduledPublishAt` as an RFC3339 timestamp in the future to arm, or `null` to cancel a pending schedule. Requires the `scheduled-revisions` commercial feature and publish permission on the config. A draft that still requires approval must request review first (or be armed with `bypassApproval` by a caller who can bypass).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "scheduledPublishAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "lockEdits": true,
  "lockOthers": true,
  "bypassApproval": true,
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="schedule-or-cancel-a-deferred-publish-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» scheduledPublishAt|body|string(date-time) \| null|true|When to publish, as an RFC3339 timestamp (e.g. `2026-01-31T09:00:00Z` or `2026-01-31T02:00:00-07:00`), or `null` to cancel a pending schedule.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» lockEdits|body|boolean|false|none|
|» lockOthers|body|boolean|false|none|
|» bypassApproval|body|boolean|false|none|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Get merge status for a draft revision

<a id="opIdgetConfigRevisionMergeStatus"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/configs-revisions/string/0/merge-status \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/configs-revisions/{key}/{version}/merge-status`

Runs a dry-run merge of the draft against the current live config and returns any conflicts. Use this before publishing to preview changes and detect conflicting edits.

<h3 id="get-merge-status-for-a-draft-revision-4-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|

> Example responses

## Rebase a draft revision onto the current live config

<a id="opIdpostConfigRevisionRebase"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/configs-revisions/string/0/rebase \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "conflictResolutions": {
      "property1": "overwrite",
      "property2": "overwrite"
    },
    "customValues": {
      "property1": [
        null
      ],
      "property2": [
        null
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v1/configs-revisions/{key}/{version}/rebase`

Updates the draft's base snapshot to the current live state, applying the draft's changes on top. Supply `conflictResolutions` to resolve any conflicting fields. Strategies are `overwrite` (use the draft's value), `discard` (keep the live value), or `union` (merge arrays without duplicates — for array fields like `extends`; pass a `customValues` entry to supply the resolved array yourself).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "conflictResolutions": {
    "property1": "overwrite",
    "property2": "overwrite"
  },
  "customValues": {
    "property1": [
      null
    ],
    "property2": [
      null
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="rebase-a-draft-revision-onto-the-current-live-config-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» conflictResolutions|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» customValues|body|object|false|Custom values to use for `union` strategy fields. Keyed by field name.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[object]|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » **additionalProperties**|overwrite|
|» » **additionalProperties**|discard|
|» » **additionalProperties**|union|

## Publish a draft revision

<a id="opIdpostConfigRevisionPublish"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/configs-revisions/string/0/publish \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "bypassApproval": true,
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/configs-revisions/{key}/{version}/publish`

Publishes the draft and makes its changes live. The caller needs Publish access for the affected environments. When approval is required, the draft must be approved unless the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. If the organization requires rebasing, an out-of-date draft must be rebased first; an authorized caller can instead send `ignoreWarnings: true` to force-publish it. A locked Config cannot be published. A 422 response lists every blocking gate and the available resolution. Publishing a schema change also normalizes descendant Configs according to their inheritance rules.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "bypassApproval": true,
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="publish-a-draft-revision-4-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|skipSchemaValidation|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `skipSchemaValidation` in the request body instead.|
|ignoreWarnings|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `ignoreWarnings` in the request body instead.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» bypassApproval|body|boolean|false|Deprecated and ignored. Approval is bypassed automatically when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access for this resource or when the organization enables the REST API approval bypass. Otherwise, the revision must be approved before it can be published.|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

## Revert the config to a prior revision

<a id="opIdpostConfigRevisionRevert"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/configs-revisions/string/0/revert \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "strategy": "draft",
    "title": "string",
    "comment": "string",
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/configs-revisions/{key}/{version}/revert`

Creates a new draft (or immediately publishes) whose content matches the specified historical revision. Defaults to creating a draft; when the org enables 'reverts bypass approval' it defaults to publishing immediately. Pass `strategy` to override.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "strategy": "draft",
  "title": "string",
  "comment": "string",
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true
}
```

<h3 id="revert-the-config-to-a-prior-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|none|
|version|path|integer|true|none|
|skipSchemaValidation|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `skipSchemaValidation` in the request body instead.|
|ignoreWarnings|query|string \| boolean|false|Deprecated — pass `ignoreWarnings` in the request body instead.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» strategy|body|string|false|Whether to stage the revert as a draft or publish it immediately. Defaults to `draft`, or to `publish` when the org enables 'reverts bypass approval'.|
|» title|body|string|false|Short draft title (e.g. `Enable for beta testers`).|
|» comment|body|string|false|Currently ignored. Use `title` to describe the revert.|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge the warnings listed in a blocked response and continue. This covers experiment guards, locked dependents, and references affected by an archive. When the organization treats schema failures as warnings, it also covers schema and invariant warnings. It never bypasses a rejected Custom Hook. On revision publish endpoints, it can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema validation errors, failed invariants, or schema changes that invalidate dependent resources. This does not bypass a rejected Custom Hook; use `skipHooks` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite a Custom Hook rejection. This does not bypass schema validation; use `skipSchemaValidation` for that. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Otherwise, this field is ignored. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» strategy|draft|
|» strategy|publish|

<h1 id="growthbook-rest-api-releases">releases</h1>

**Beta** — these endpoints are new and may change in backwards-incompatible ways.

Coordinated multi-entity publishing: publish a set of revisions across Feature Flags, Saved Groups, configs, and constants as one all-or-nothing operation, validated against the combined end-state instead of each in-between state. Requires the `releases` commercial feature.

## Atomically publish revisions across multiple entities

<a id="opIdpostReleasePublishRevisions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/releases/publish-revisions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "revisions": [
      {
        "entityType": "feature",
        "id": "string",
        "version": 0
      }
    ],
    "dryRun": true,
    "ignoreWarnings": true,
    "skipSchemaValidation": true,
    "skipHooks": true,
    "comment": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/releases/publish-revisions`

Publishes a set of revisions — at most one per entity — across Feature Flags, Saved Groups, configs, and constants as a single all-or-nothing operation.

Validation, guards, and custom hooks run against the combined end-state of the whole set, so interdependent changes (e.g. a config schema change plus the values that depend on it) publish together even when the in-between states would be invalid.

A blocked publish returns one 422 listing every gate across every item and the flag that clears each. A concurrent change to any target aborts with a 409 and nothing publishes. A failure after the commit starts rolls everything back and emits `revision.publishFailed` for each revision in the set. SDK payloads refresh once per request. Pass `dryRun: true` for the full gate report with zero writes.

Requires the `releases` commercial feature.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "revisions": [
    {
      "entityType": "feature",
      "id": "string",
      "version": 0
    }
  ],
  "dryRun": true,
  "ignoreWarnings": true,
  "skipSchemaValidation": true,
  "skipHooks": true,
  "comment": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="atomically-publish-revisions-across-multiple-entities-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» revisions|body|[[FeatureRevisionRef](#schemafeaturerevisionref) \| [SavedGroupRevisionRef](#schemasavedgrouprevisionref) \| [ConfigRevisionRef](#schemaconfigrevisionref) \| [ConstantRevisionRef](#schemaconstantrevisionref) \| [RevisionIdRef](#schemarevisionidref)]|true|The revisions to publish, at most one per entity.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[FeatureRevisionRef](#schemafeaturerevisionref)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[SavedGroupRevisionRef](#schemasavedgrouprevisionref)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[ConfigRevisionRef](#schemaconfigrevisionref)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[ConstantRevisionRef](#schemaconstantrevisionref)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[RevisionIdRef](#schemarevisionidref)|false|none|
|» dryRun|body|boolean|false|Report every gate and outcome without writing anything.|
|» ignoreWarnings|body|boolean|false|Set to true to acknowledge warnings from experiment guards, schema changes, or archives. It can also force-publish an out-of-date draft when the caller has Bypass draft approvals access for that resource. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipSchemaValidation|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite schema or invariant failures. Validation still runs and the response still reports each failure. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» skipHooks|body|boolean|false|Set to true to publish despite Custom Hook rejections. The caller must have Bypass draft approvals access for Feature Flags, Configs, and Constants in every Project. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» comment|body|string|false|An optional publish comment recorded on every revision in this release — it appears in each entity's revision history and is passed to any custom validation hooks that run for the publish.|

<h3 id="atomically-publish-revisions-across-multiple-entities-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dryRun|boolean|true|none|none|
|bulkPublishId|string|false|none|Correlation token (`pub_…`) stamped on every event this publish emitted. Absent on dry runs.|
|results|[[results](#schemaresults)]|true|none|none|
|gates|[object]|true|none|Dry runs report every gate, cleared and blocking. Real publishes return an empty list — blocking gates fail with a 422 instead.|
|» entityType|string|true|none|none|
|» id|string|true|none|The identifier used in the request.|
|» version|integer|true|none|none|
|» type|string|true|none|Gate kind, e.g. "approval-required".|
|» severity|string|true|none|none|
|» messages|[string]|true|none|none|
|» override|string \| null|true|none|Request flag that clears this gate on retry, if any.|
|» » *anyOf*|string|false|none|none|
|» » *anyOf*|null|false|none|none|

<h1 id="growthbook-rest-api-custom-hooks">custom-hooks</h1>

Sandboxed JavaScript validation hooks that run when features, configs, or their revisions are saved or published. Throwing an Error blocks the save; `addWarning(msg)` raises a soft warning. Hooks are scoped by projects, or pinned to a single feature/config via `entityType`/`entityId`; a config-scoped hook also runs for every config inheriting from it (its whole descendant lineage). Scope can be retargeted on update (or cleared with nulls). Requires an enterprise plan; not available on GrowthBook Cloud.

<h1 id="growthbook-rest-api-usage">usage</h1>

Usage information for metrics in experiments.

## Get metric usage across experiments

<a id="opIdgetMetricUsage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/usage/metrics?ids=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/usage/metrics`

Returns usage information for one or more legacy or fact metrics, showing which experiments use each metric
and some usage statistics. If a metric is part of a metric group, then usage of that metric group counts as
usage of all metrics in the group. Warning: only includes experiments that you have access to! If you do not have admin
access or read access to experiments across all projects, this endpoint may not return the latest usage data across
all experiments. 


<h3 id="get-metric-usage-across-experiments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ids|query|string|true|List of comma-separated metric IDs (both fact and legacy) to get usage for, e.g. ids=met_123,fact_456|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "metricUsage": [
    {
      "metricId": "string",
      "error": "string",
      "experiments": [
        {
          "experimentId": "string",
          "experimentStatus": "draft",
          "lastSnapshotAttempt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
        }
      ],
      "lastSnapshotAttempt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-metric-usage-across-experiments-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response|Inline|

<h3 id="get-metric-usage-across-experiments-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|metricUsage|[[MetricUsage](#schemametricusage)]|true|none|none|

bearerAuth, basicAuth
</aside>

## Replace a Contextual Bandit's rule on a linked feature

<a id="opIdupdateContextualBanditLinkedFeature"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/contextual-bandits/string/linked-feature/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "variations": [
      {
        "variationId": "string",
        "value": "string",
        "config": "string"
      }
    ],
    "description": "string",
    "enabled": true,
    "allEnvironments": true,
    "environments": [
      "string"
    ],
    "allProjects": true,
    "projects": [
      "string"
    ],
    "autoPublish": true,
    "allowUnscopedRules": true,
    "draftVersion": 0
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/contextual-bandits/{id}/linked-feature/{featureId}`

Replaces every `contextual-bandit-ref` rule pointing at this contextual bandit on the feature, keeping each rule's id and position in the rule list. Every field is replaced, so omitted optional fields revert to their defaults. Returns a 400 when the feature has no such rule on the target revision, or when it has several that are not identical to each other. The change lands in a draft revision that auto-publishes when the contextual bandit starts, unless `autoPublish` is set. Targeting (condition, Saved Groups, prerequisites, coverage) is inherited from the contextual bandit and cannot be set on the rule.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "variations": [
    {
      "variationId": "string",
      "value": "string",
      "config": "string"
    }
  ],
  "description": "string",
  "enabled": true,
  "allEnvironments": true,
  "environments": [
    "string"
  ],
  "allProjects": true,
  "projects": [
    "string"
  ],
  "autoPublish": true,
  "allowUnscopedRules": true,
  "draftVersion": 0
}
```

<h3 id="replace-a-contextual-bandits-rule-on-a-linked-feature-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The Contextual Bandit id|
|featureId|path|string|true|The linked feature id|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» variations|body|[object]|true|One entry per Contextual Bandit variation. Every variation must be covered exactly once.|
|» » variationId|body|string|true|Id of the Contextual Bandit variation.|
|» » value|body|string|true|Feature value served for this variation.|
|» » config|body|string \| null|false|Key of the config backing this value, or null when the value is not config-backed. The config supplies the base JSON (and its schema); the value is an override patch merged on top.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|none|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|none|
|» allEnvironments|body|boolean|false|Apply the rule in every environment. Defaults to true.|
|» environments|body|[string]|false|Environments to apply the rule in when not all.|
|» allProjects|body|boolean|false|none|
|» projects|body|[string]|false|none|
|» autoPublish|body|boolean|false|Publish the resulting revision immediately instead of leaving it as a draft.|
|» allowUnscopedRules|body|boolean|false|When the organization requires rules to target specific environments or Projects, set to true to save a rule that applies to All Environments and All Projects. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» draftVersion|body|integer|false|Update the rule on this existing draft revision instead of starting a new one.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "featureId": "string",
  "ruleIds": [
    "string"
  ],
  "revisionVersion": 0,
  "published": true
}
```

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "confirmation": {
    "id": "string",
    "status": "pending",
    "actions": [
      {
        "action": "feature.create",
        "environments": [
          "string"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "summary": "string",
    "url": "string",
    "expiresAt": "string",
    "response": {
      "status": 0,
      "body": null
    },
    "note": "string"
  },
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "code": "unscoped_rule",
  "details": {
    "ruleIds": [
      "string"
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="replace-a-contextual-bandits-rule-on-a-linked-feature-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Resource updated|Inline|
|202|Accepted|Held until a person confirms it in GrowthBook. Poll the Location until the confirmation completes.|[ConfirmationHeld](#schemaconfirmationheld)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="replace-a-contextual-bandits-rule-on-a-linked-feature-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

```bash
      }
    ],

    "enabled": true,
    "allEnvironments": true,

    ],

    ],

```

`POST /v1/contextual-bandits/{id}/linked-feature/{featureId}`

Adds a `contextual-bandit-ref` rule to the bottom of the feature's rule list and links the feature to this contextual bandit. The rule lands in a draft revision that auto-publishes when the contextual bandit starts, unless `autoPublish` is set. Targeting (condition, Saved Groups, prerequisites, coverage) is inherited from the contextual bandit and cannot be set on the rule.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "variations": [
    {
      "variationId": "string",
      "value": "string",
      "config": "string"
    }
  ],
  "description": "string",
  "enabled": true,
  "allEnvironments": true,
  "environments": [
    "string"
  ],
  "allProjects": true,
  "projects": [
    "string"
  ],
  "autoPublish": true,
  "allowUnscopedRules": true,
  "draftVersion": 0
}
```

<h3 id="link-a-feature-to-a-contextual-bandit-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The Contextual Bandit id|
|featureId|path|string|true|The linked feature id|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» variations|body|[object]|true|One entry per Contextual Bandit variation. Every variation must be covered exactly once.|
|» » variationId|body|string|true|Id of the Contextual Bandit variation.|
|» » value|body|string|true|Feature value served for this variation.|
|» » config|body|string \| null|false|Key of the config backing this value, or null when the value is not config-backed. The config supplies the base JSON (and its schema); the value is an override patch merged on top.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|none|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|none|
|» allEnvironments|body|boolean|false|Apply the rule in every environment. Defaults to true.|
|» environments|body|[string]|false|Environments to apply the rule in when not all.|
|» allProjects|body|boolean|false|none|
|» projects|body|[string]|false|none|
|» autoPublish|body|boolean|false|Publish the resulting revision immediately instead of leaving it as a draft.|
|» allowUnscopedRules|body|boolean|false|When the organization requires rules to target specific environments or Projects, set to true to save a rule that applies to All Environments and All Projects. Only set this when a person has explicitly asked you to. If a check blocks you, stop and ask a person instead of working around it.|
|» draftVersion|body|integer|false|Add the rule to this existing draft revision instead of starting a new one.|

```json
  "revisionVersion": 0,
  "published": true
}
```

## Unlink a feature from a Contextual Bandit

<a id="opIddeleteContextualBanditLinkedFeature"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/contextual-bandits/string/linked-feature/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v1/contextual-bandits/{id}/linked-feature/{featureId}`

Removes every `contextual-bandit-ref` rule pointing at this contextual bandit from the feature and drops the feature from the bandit's linked-feature list. The rule removal lands in a draft revision unless `autoPublish` is set. When the feature has no such rule left, only the linkage is cleared.

<h3 id="unlink-a-feature-from-a-contextual-bandit-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The Contextual Bandit id|
|featureId|path|string|true|The linked feature id|
|autoPublish|query|string \| boolean|false|Publish the resulting revision immediately instead of leaving it as a draft.|
|draftVersion|query|integer|false|Remove the rule from this existing draft revision instead of live. Required when the rule hasn't been published yet — omitting it targets the live revision, which has nothing to remove.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "featureId": "string",
  "removedRuleIds": [
    "string"
  ],
  "revisionVersion": 0,
  "published": true
}
```

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "confirmation": {
    "id": "string",
    "status": "pending",
    "actions": [
      {
        "action": "feature.create",
        "environments": [
          "string"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "summary": "string",
    "url": "string",
    "expiresAt": "string",
    "response": {
      "status": 0,
      "body": null
    },
    "note": "string"
  },
  "message": "string"
}
```

## Add or remove Contextual Bandit variations

<a id="opIdupdateContextualBanditVariations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/contextual-bandits/string/variations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "addVariations": [
      {
        "id": "string",
        "name": "string",
        "description": "string",
        "key": "string",
        "screenshots": [
          {
            "path": "string",
            "width": 0,
            "height": 0,
            "description": "string"
          }
        ],
        "values": {
          "property1": "string",
          "property2": "string"
        }
      }
    ],
    "removeVariationIds": [
      "string"
    ],
    "updateVariations": [
      {
        "id": "string",
        "name": "string",
        "description": "string",
        "key": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v1/contextual-bandits/{id}/variations`

Adds and/or removes variations on a Contextual Bandit. Send `addVariations` and `removeVariationIds` independently; both are optional. New arms must carry a `values` entry for each linked feature. Running CBs publish the linked-feature updates; draft CBs stage them until start. Under an approval flow, unapproved drafts leave the added arm `pending` (zero weight, filtered from the SDK) until every linked feature's draft is live. Removed arms are tombstoned; their ids can never be re-added. Weights are reconciled server-side.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "addVariations": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "key": "string",
      "screenshots": [
        {
          "path": "string",
          "width": 0,
          "height": 0,
          "description": "string"
        }
      ],
      "values": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      }
    }
  ],
  "removeVariationIds": [
    "string"
  ],
  "updateVariations": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "key": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-or-remove-contextual-bandit-variations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» addVariations|body|[object]|false|New arms to add. Omit `id` to have the server generate one and `key` to have the server assign the next integer.|
|» » id|body|string|false|none|
|» » name|body|string|true|none|
|» » description|body|string|false|none|
|» » key|body|string|false|none|
|» » screenshots|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » » path|body|string|true|none|
|» » » width|body|number|false|none|
|» » » height|body|number|false|none|
|» » » description|body|string|false|none|
|» » values|body|object|false|Value this new arm serves on each currently-linked feature, keyed by feature id. Required for every linked feature. Encode as a string for every `valueType` (`"true"`, `"5"`, `"{\"a\":1}"`), matching how `feature.defaultValue` is set.|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» removeVariationIds|body|[string]|false|Ids of active arms to remove. Removed arms are tombstoned in place and their ids can never be re-added.|
|» updateVariations|body|[object]|false|Metadata edits to existing active arms. `name`, `description`, and `key` may be changed; values, weights, screenshots, and status are preserved.|
|» » id|body|string|true|none|
|» » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » description|body|string|false|none|
|» » key|body|string|false|New key for the arm. Must be unique across the contextual bandit's arms, including removed ones. The key is what SDKs report in exposure events, so renaming an arm on a running bandit orphans exposures already recorded under the old key.|

<h3 id="update-a-single-dashboard-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Location|string||The confirmation to poll|
|202|Retry-After|integer||Seconds to wait before polling|

bearerAuth, basicAuth
</aside>
