## Create a single dashboard

<a id="opIdcreateDashboard"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/dashboards \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "title": "string",
    "editLevel": "published",
    "shareLevel": "published",
    "enableAutoUpdates": true,
    "updateSchedule": {
      "type": "stale",
      "hours": 0
    },
    "experimentId": "string",
    "projects": [
      "string"
    ],
    "globalControls": {
      "dateRange": {
        "predefined": "today",
        "lookbackValue": 0,
        "lookbackUnit": "hour",
        "startDate": "string",
        "endDate": "string"
      },
      "dateGranularity": "auto",
      "projects": [
        "string"
      ],
      "experimentSearchString": "string"
    },
    "comparison": {
      "enabled": true,
      "mode": "previousPeriod",
      "previousTimeFrame": {
        "predefined": "today",
        "lookbackValue": 0,
        "lookbackUnit": "hour",
        "startDate": "string",
        "endDate": "string"
      }
    },
    "blocks": [
      {
        "type": "markdown",
        "title": "string",
        "description": "string",
        "snapshotId": "string",
        "layout": {
          "x": 0,
          "y": 0,
          "w": 1,
          "h": 1,
          "static": true
        },
        "content": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v1/dashboards`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated.** Use [POST /v2/dashboards](#operation/createDashboardV2) instead.

This endpoint does not accept an `owner` and always assigns the dashboard to the authenticated user. A dashboard created with an organization secret API key, which has no associated user, therefore has no owner. The v2 endpoint accepts an `owner` (userId or email) and requires one when authenticating with an organization secret API key.

|---|---|---|---|

|202|Accepted|Held until a person confirms it in GrowthBook. Poll the Location until the confirmation completes.|[ConfirmationHeld](#schemaconfirmationheld)|

<h3 id="create-a-single-dashboard-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dashboard|[Dashboard](#schemadashboard)|true|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Location|string||The confirmation to poll|
|202|Retry-After|integer||Seconds to wait before polling|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, basicAuth
</aside>

## Create a single dashboard

```bash

  -d '{

      "previousTimeFrame": {
```

|» owner|body|string|false|The userId or email address of the owner. If an email address is provided, it will be used to look up the userId of the matching organization member. If an ID is provided, it will be validated as existing in the organization. Optional when authenticating with a Personal Access Token (PAT): when omitted, the owner defaults to the PAT's user. Required when authenticating with an organization secret API key (which has no associated user): omitting it fails with a 400. A private dashboard created with an organization secret API key can only be retrieved or updated using its owner's Personal Access Token (PAT).|

<h3 id="create-a-single-dashboard-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Resource created|Inline|
|202|Accepted|Held until a person confirms it in GrowthBook. Poll the Location until the confirmation completes.|[ConfirmationHeld](#schemaconfirmationheld)|

<h3 id="create-a-single-dashboard-1-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dashboard|[Dashboard](#schemadashboard)|true|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Location|string||The confirmation to poll|
|202|Retry-After|integer||Seconds to wait before polling|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, basicAuth
</aside>

## Get all dashboards for an experiment

<a id="opIdgetDashboardsForExperiment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/dashboards/by-experiment/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/dashboards/by-experiment/{experimentId}`

<h3 id="get-all-dashboards-for-an-experiment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|experimentId|path|string|true|none|

## Run a Fact Table based visualization

<a id="opIdpostFactTableExploration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/product-analytics/fact-table-exploration \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "datasource": "string",
    "dimensions": [
      {
        "dimensionType": "date",
        "column": "string",
        "dateGranularity": "auto"
      }
    ],
    "chartType": "line",
    "dateRange": {
      "predefined": "today",
      "lookbackValue": 0,
      "lookbackUnit": "hour",
      "startDate": "string",
      "endDate": "string"
    },
    "showAs": "total",
    "chartSettings": {
      "categoryAxisLabel": "string",
      "valueAxisLabel": "string"
    },
    "type": "fact_table",
    "dataset": {
      "type": "fact_table",
      "factTableId": "string",
      "values": [
        {
          "name": "string",
          "rowFilters": [
            {
              "operator": "=",
              "column": "string",
              "values": [
                "string"
              ]
            }
          ],
          "type": "fact_table",
          "valueType": "unit_count",
          "valueColumn": "string",
          "unit": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/product-analytics/data-source-exploration \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "datasource": "string",
    "dimensions": [
      {
        "dimensionType": "date",
        "column": "string",
        "dateGranularity": "auto"
      }
    ],
    "chartType": "line",
    "dateRange": {
      "predefined": "today",
      "lookbackValue": 0,
      "lookbackUnit": "hour",
      "startDate": "string",
      "endDate": "string"
    },
    "showAs": "total",
    "chartSettings": {
      "categoryAxisLabel": "string",
      "valueAxisLabel": "string"
    },
    "type": "data_source",
    "dataset": {
      "type": "data_source",
      "table": "string",
      "path": "string",
      "timestampColumn": "string",
      "columnTypes": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      },
      "values": [
        {
          "name": "string",

            {

              "column": "string",

          ],
          "type": "data_source",
          "valueType": "unit_count",
          "valueColumn": "string",
          "unit": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

## Create a SQL based visualization

<a id="opIdpostSqlExploration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/product-analytics/sql-exploration \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "datasource": "string",
    "dimensions": [
      {
        "dimensionType": "date",
        "column": "string",
        "dateGranularity": "auto"
      }
    ],
    "chartType": "line",
    "dateRange": {
      "predefined": "today",
      "lookbackValue": 0,
      "lookbackUnit": "hour",
      "startDate": "string",
      "endDate": "string"
    },
    "showAs": "total",
    "chartSettings": {
      "categoryAxisLabel": "string",
      "valueAxisLabel": "string"
    },
    "type": "sql",
    "dataset": {
      "type": "sql",
      "sql": "string",
      "timestampColumn": "string",
      "columnTypes": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      },
      "values": [
        {
          "name": "string",
          "rowFilters": [
            {
              "operator": "=",
              "column": "string",
              "values": [
                "string"
              ]
            }
          ],
          "type": "sql",
          "valueType": "unit_count",
          "valueColumn": "string",
          "unit": "string"
        }
      ],
      "hiddenColumns": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  }'
```

## Run a Funnel based visualization

<a id="opIdpostFunnelExploration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/product-analytics/funnel-exploration \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "datasource": "string",
    "dimensions": [
      {
        "dimensionType": "date",
        "column": "string",
        "dateGranularity": "auto"
      }
    ],
    "chartType": "line",
    "dateRange": {
      "predefined": "today",
      "lookbackValue": 0,
      "lookbackUnit": "hour",
      "startDate": "string",
      "endDate": "string"
    },
    "showAs": "total",
    "chartSettings": {
      "categoryAxisLabel": "string",
      "valueAxisLabel": "string"
    },
    "type": "funnel",
    "dataset": {
      "type": "funnel",
      "unit": "string",
      "steps": [
        {
          "name": "string",
          "factTableId": "string",
          "rowFilters": [
            {
              "operator": "=",
              "column": "string",
              "values": [
                "string"
              ]
            }
          ],
          "optional": true,
          "conversionWindow": {
            "unit": "weeks",
            "value": 0.1
          }
        }
      ],
      "concurrencyWindowSeconds": 0,
      "yAxisScale": "count"
    }
  }'
```

## Run a User Journey based visualization

<a id="opIdpostJourneyExploration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/product-analytics/journey-exploration \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "datasource": "string",
    "dimensions": [
      {
        "dimensionType": "date",
        "column": "string",
        "dateGranularity": "auto"
      }
    ],
    "chartType": "line",
    "dateRange": {
      "predefined": "today",
      "lookbackValue": 0,
      "lookbackUnit": "hour",
      "startDate": "string",
      "endDate": "string"
    },
    "showAs": "total",
    "chartSettings": {
      "categoryAxisLabel": "string",
      "valueAxisLabel": "string"
    },
    "type": "journey",
    "dataset": {
      "type": "journey",
      "factTableId": "string",
      "unit": "string",
      "stepColumns": [
        "string"
      ],
      "stepGroups": [
        {
          "column": "string",
          "pattern": "string"
        }
      ],
      "anchorStepValues": [
        "string"
      ],
      "direction": "forward",
      "rowFilters": [
        {
          "operator": "=",
          "column": "string",
          "values": [
            "string"
          ]
        }
      ],
      "path": [
        {
          "value": "string"
        }
      ],
      "lookaheadDepth": 1,
      "optionsPerStep": [
        2
      ],
      "heightScale": "relative"
    }
  }'
```

|» » startAnalysisPeriodAt|body|string(date-time)|false|ISO datetime to move the Holdout from `running` to `analysis-period`. Requires `startAt` while the Holdout is still a draft.|

## Start the Holdout's Analysis Period

<a id="opIdstartHoldoutAnalysis"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/holdouts/string/start-analysis \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v1/holdouts/{id}/start-analysis`

Move the holdout into an analysis phase. New Feature Flags and Experiments can no longer be added, but existing traffic splits remain active for existing and new traffic. Results exclude data from before the analysis period so you can measure the cumulative impact after changes are frozen.

<h1 id="growthbook-rest-api-populations">Populations</h1>

**Beta** — these endpoints are new and may change in backwards-incompatible ways.

Populations define a set of units by the steps they must complete, such as appearing in a fact table. Populations are not yet used in analysis.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|Stable revision id. Newer revisions carry opaque ids; older ones a derived `frev_<version>_<featureId>` form. Both work wherever revision ids are accepted.|
|featureId|string|true|none|The feature this revision belongs to|
|baseVersion|integer|true|none|none|
|version|integer|true|none|none|
|comment|string|true|none|none|
|date|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|status|string|true|none|none|
|createdBy|[EventUser](#schemaeventuser)|false|none|Who performed an action|
|publishedBy|[EventUser](#schemaeventuser)|false|none|Who performed an action|
|defaultValue|string|false|none|The default value at the time this revision was created. When the feature is in Config mode, this is the JSON override patch merged on top of the config (its own keys win); otherwise it is the full value.|
|defaultValueConfig|string \| null|false|none|Optional. A config within `baseConfig`'s family that the default value resolves to instead of `baseConfig` itself. null or omitted means the default is `baseConfig`. The default is exactly this config and carries no overrides of its own.|
|rules|[[FeatureRuleV2](#schemafeaturerulev2)]|true|none|Unified rules array. Each rule carries its own environment scope via `allEnvironments` / `environments`.|
|definitions|object|false|none|none|
|environmentsEnabled|object|false|none|Per-environment enabled state captured in this revision (only present when kill-switch gating is enabled)|
|envPrerequisites|object|false|none|Per-environment prerequisites captured in this revision (only present when prerequisite gating is enabled)|
|prerequisites|[object]|false|none|Feature-level prerequisites captured in this revision. Each entry is a boolean flag ID that must evaluate to true for this flag to be active for a given user.|
|metadata|object|false|none|Metadata fields captured in this revision (only present when metadata gating is enabled)|
|rampActions|[object]|false|none|Pending ramp schedule actions that will be applied when this draft is published|
|autoPublishOnApproval|boolean|false|none|When true, the revision is armed to publish automatically once governance allows (immediately on approval, or on `scheduledPublishAt` if set).|
|scheduledPublishAt|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Target date for a deferred (scheduled) publish. Null/absent means publish as soon as approved.|
|scheduledPublishLockEdits|boolean|false|none|When true, content edits to this draft are frozen while the schedule is pending (rebasing is still allowed).|
|scheduledPublishLockOthers|boolean|false|none|When true, publishing other drafts of this feature is blocked while the schedule is pending.|
|scheduledPublishBypassApproval|boolean|false|none|Whether the schedule was created for an unapproved draft by a caller with Bypass draft approvals access. This kind of schedule cannot be edited; cancel it and create a new schedule instead. Anyone with Publish access can cancel it.|
|scheduledPublishLastError|string|false|none|Set when a due scheduled publish keeps failing (e.g. still awaiting approval, merge conflict). Indicates the schedule is stuck and retrying.|
|autoPublishEnabledBy|string|false|none|User or API key the deferred publish runs as, re-checked when it fires. A key that assumed a member's role is recorded as `<keyId>:<memberId>`.|
|autoPublishEnabledByUser|[EventUser](#schemaeventuser)|false|none|Who armed the deferred publish, with an API key's name|
|scheduledPublishAttempts|integer|false|none|How many times the poller has tried to publish this revision. Read with `scheduledPublishGaveUpAt` to tell a schedule that is still retrying from one that has been parked.|
|scheduledPublishGaveUpAt|string(date-time)|false|none|When the poller stopped retrying. Giving up CLEARS the schedule and disarms auto-publish, so nothing fires again until the revision is re-armed. The draft is left open, with `scheduledPublishLastError` preserved for context.|
|reviews|[object]|false|none|Reviewer verdicts for the current review cycle (one entry per reviewer). Verdicts flip to their -stale variants when draft content changes after submission; the list is cleared when a new review cycle starts. Absent on revisions that predate this field.|

```json
        "string"
      ]
    }
  ],

    {
      "id": "string",
      "condition": "string"
    }
  ],

  "environments": [
    "string"
  ],
  "type": "force",
  "value": "string",
  "config": "string",

  "hashAttribute": "string",
  "fallbackAttribute": "string",
  "seed": "string",
  "hashVersion": 1
}
```

A targeting rule that serves a specific value to users matching the conditions. Set coverage < 1 for a percentage rollout.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|string|false|none|Short note on why the rule exists (e.g. `Beta testers only`).|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|condition|string|false|none|none|
|savedGroups|[object]|false|none|none|
|prerequisites|[object]|false|none|none|
|allEnvironments|boolean|false|none|When true the rule applies to all environments. Omit both scope fields to apply to all environments.|
|environments|[string]|false|none|Environment IDs the rule applies to. Ignored when allEnvironments is true; with allEnvironments false, an omitted or empty list scopes the rule to no environment.|
|type|string|false|none|Use "force" for a standard targeting rule, or "rollout" for a percentage rollout (coverage < 1). Defaults to "force". Both are functionally equivalent; a force rule with coverage < 1 behaves as a rollout.|
|value|string|true|none|The value to serve when this rule matches.|
|config|string \| null|false|none|Key of a config to back this value. When set, `value` is a JSON override patch merged on top of the config; omit or null for a plain value.|
|sparse|boolean|false|none|JSON features only. When true, the rule value is a partial object merged onto the feature's default value instead of replacing it.|
|coverage|number|false|none|Percentage of users to include (0–1). Defaults to 1. When less than 1, hashAttribute is required.|
|hashAttribute|string|false|none|Attribute to hash on for consistent assignment. Required when coverage < 1.|
|fallbackAttribute|string|false|none|Used in place of `hashAttribute` when a user lacks it. Only SDKs with Sticky Bucketing enabled use it.|
|seed|string|false|none|none|
|hashVersion|number|false|none|Hash algorithm version for bucketing. Defaults to 2 (preferred) when not specified.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|force|
|type|rollout|

<h2 id="tocS_ScheduledStopPlan">ScheduledStopPlan</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemascheduledstopplan"></a>
<a id="schema_ScheduledStopPlan"></a>
<a id="tocSscheduledstopplan"></a>
<a id="tocsscheduledstopplan"></a>

```json
{
  "mode": "notify",
  "tiebreakerMetricId": "string",
  "fallback": "notify",
  "fallbackVariationId": "string"
}
```

What happens at the scheduled end date. `notify` keeps the experiment running and just notifies (soft). `auto-ship` (requires the Decision Framework) ships the winning variation and stops; multi-winner ties break on `tiebreakerMetricId` (higher lift); with no clear winner, `fallback` either keeps running (`notify`) or ships `fallbackVariationId`. `force-ship` stops and rolls out `fallbackVariationId`. `stop` is a hard deadline that stops with no rollout. For `force-ship` and `stop`, the Decision Framework verdict (won/lost/inconclusive) is recorded as metadata when available.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|mode|string|true|none|none|
|tiebreakerMetricId|string|false|none|none|
|fallback|string|false|none|What to do at the scheduled end when there is no clear winner. Required when `mode` is `"auto-ship"`; ignored for other modes.|
|fallbackVariationId|string|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|mode|notify|
|mode|auto-ship|
|mode|force-ship|
|mode|stop|
|fallback|notify|
|fallback|force-ship|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|none|
|key|string|true|none|Stable reference handle; used as `@config:key` in values|
|name|string|true|none|none|
|owner|string|false|none|The userId of the owner (or raw owner name/email for legacy records)|
|ownerEmail|string|false|none|The email address of the owner, when the owner can be resolved to a known user.|
|parent|string|false|none|The `key` of the config this one inherits from (lineage parent — the primary spine). Synthesized into `$extends` at resolution time and never stored in `value`.|
|extends|[string]|false|none|Additional composition bases (config `key`s) layered on top of `parent`, in precedence order (later overrides earlier; all override `parent`; this config's own keys win last). Like `parent`, set via this field — never via a `@config:` entry in `value`.|
|value|object|false|none|This config's own base value as a JSON object (its declared fields only — inherited fields are layered in at resolution time, not stored here). Per-environment/project variants are expressed via `scopedOverrides`, not here.|
|scopedOverrides|[object]|false|none|Ordered, first-match-wins environment/project-scoped variant selection. Each entry points at a flavor config (a child config, by `key`) whose value is deep-merged onto this config's resolved value when the (environment, project) scope matches — resolved at build time, per layer. This is how you create an environment-scoped override (as opposed to a plain child config): make a child config for the override value, then add it here with its scope. Send the complete list to replace it; an empty array clears all overrides. Entries must reference existing configs, may not reference this config itself, and may not be unreachable (fully subsumed by an earlier entry).|
|scopedConfig|object|false|none|Present ONLY when this config is an environment/project-scoped override (a "flavor") of another config. Its value is a patch that applies solely within the listed environments/projects, layered onto `parent` at resolution — it is NOT a standalone config. A plain config (including an ordinary child that just inherits from a `parent`) omits this field entirely. Read-only: create/change the relationship via the parent config's `scopedOverrides`, never by setting this directly.|
|description|string|false|none|none|
|project|string|false|none|The project this config belongs to (empty = all projects)|
|archived|boolean|false|none|none|
|schema|object|false|none|This config's own field definitions as a JSON Schema document (its contribution to the family's effective schema). Inherited fields are owned by ancestors and are not repeated here.|
|extensible|boolean|false|none|Whether this config family permits extra keys beyond the declared fields (child configs, feature rules, ad-hoc overrides). Only the root config's flag applies. Absent = inherit the org default.|
|invariants|[object]|false|none|Cross-field validation rules (relational checks JSON Schema can't express, e.g. implications or comparing two fields), evaluated against the resolved value at publish.|
|locked|boolean|false|none|Whether this Config is locked to a published revision. Drafts can still be created and edited while locked, but no change can be published until a user with Bypass draft approvals access unlocks it.|
|experimentGuard|boolean|false|none|Whether the experiment guard is enabled. When enabled, publishing a value used by a running experiment returns a warning that must be acknowledged with `ignoreWarnings: true`. Disabling the guard requires Bypass draft approvals access.|
|lockedRevision|object|false|none|The pinned published revision (present only when `locked`). Fetch it via `GET /configs-revisions/:key/:version` for a value guaranteed not to disappear or mutate — use it to pin reproducible builds.|
|lockedBy|string|false|none|Who locked the config: a member's user ID, or an API key's ID when it acted as itself|
|dateLocked|string(date-time)|false|none|When the config was locked (when `locked`).|
|dateCreated|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|dateUpdated|string(date-time)|true|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier (rs_ prefix)|
|dateCreated|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|dateUpdated|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|name|string|true|none|none|
|entityType|string|true|none|none|
|entityId|string|true|none|none|
|targets|[object]|true|none|Controlled entity references|
|startActions|[object]|false|none|Actions that restore controlled rules to their pre-ramp state. Applied when rolling back or jumping to start, and the base every step accumulates on; the only place a plan can set hashAttribute, seed or hashVersion.|
|steps|[object]|true|none|Ordered ramp steps|
|endActions|[object]|false|none|Actions applied on top of all step patches when the ramp completes. Represents the final desired rule state.|
|startDate|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the ramp fires. Absent/null means immediately on publish; set to a future datetime to delay start and keep the rule disabled until that time.|
|cutoffDate|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Rule-level kill date. When reached, the ramp is completed and the rule is disabled (enabled=false). Use for time-boxed rules that must stop serving on a fixed date regardless of ramp progress. Set to null to clear.|
|requiresStartApproval|boolean|false|none|When true, the ramp holds at step -1 with its rule disabled (zero traffic) until a human approves the start via /actions/approve-step. Composes with startDate ('hold until approved, then arm for that date').|
|startApprovedAt|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the current launch's start was approved. Cleared on every return to step -1 (publish, rollback), re-arming the approval gate.|
|status|string|true|none|none|
|currentStepIndex|integer|true|none|Index of current step; -1 = not yet started|
|startedAt|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|none|
|phaseStartedAt|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Anchor for cumulative interval timing; resets after each approval gate is satisfied|
|pausedAt|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|none|
|nextStepAt|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|When the current step's time gate elapses; null for steps with no interval (pure approval gates) and terminal states|
|nextProcessAt|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|none|
|elapsedMs|integer \| null|false|none|Milliseconds since startedAt (computed at response time, not stored)|
|lockdownConfig|object|false|none|none|
|monitoringConfig|object \| null|false|none|none|
|experimentHealthAction|string|false|none|none|
|currentStepEnteredAt|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|none|
|stepApproval|object \| null|false|none|Approval record for the current step. Valid only while `stepApproval.stepIndex === currentStepIndex`.|
|awaitingApproval|boolean|true|none|Computed at read time: whether a human approval is the gate blocking the schedule right now — either the start-approval gate (`requiresStartApproval` before step 0) or the current step's `holdConditions.requiresApproval` once its time hold (if any) has elapsed. Paused schedules report `false` (the pause is the blocking gate). For monitored steps the approve-step endpoint may still reject an approval until analysis-based gates clear.|
|monitoringStartDate|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the monitored section most recently started (first monitored step entered). Used for no-traffic grace period gating.|
|lastRollbackAt|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|none|
|lastRollbackReason|string \| null|false|none|none|
|monitoringStatus|object \| null|false|none|Read-only monitoring status. Present when monitoringConfig is set.|

|status|ready|
|status|running|
|status|paused|
|status|completed|
|status|rolled-back|
|experimentHealthAction|rollback|
|experimentHealthAction|hold|
|experimentHealthAction|warn|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|string|true|none|none|
|name|string|true|none|none|
|parent|string \| null|true|none|The lineage parent's key (tree spine), or null for the family root.|
|extends|[string]|false|none|Additional composition bases (mixin config keys) layered on top of `parent`. The tree shape follows `parent`/`depth`; these express composition beyond the parent/child spine.|
|project|string|false|none|none|
|archived|boolean|true|none|none|
|depth|integer|true|none|Distance from the family root along the `parent` spine (root is 0).|
|isTarget|boolean|true|none|True for the requested config.|
|incompatibleFields|[string]|false|none|Own value keys whose value no longer conforms to the effective (inherited) field type and must be fixed. Empty when all conform.|
|orphanedFields|[string]|false|none|Own value keys the effective schema no longer declares (e.g. an ancestor removed the field). They still resolve and are served, but nothing validates them and validation rules read them as null; a non-extensible family rejects them on the next changing publish.|

<h2 id="tocS_healthSummary">healthSummary</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemahealthsummary"></a>
<a id="schema_healthSummary"></a>
<a id="tocShealthsummary"></a>
<a id="tocshealthsummary"></a>

```json
{
  "safeToAdvance": true,
  "decision": "advance",
  "decisionReason": "string",
  "signals": [
    "guardrail-failing"
  ],
  "snapshotAt": "string",
  "traffic": {
    "totalUsers": 0,
    "variationUnits": [
      0
    ],
    "srm": {
      "pValue": 0,
      "status": "ok"
    },
    "multipleExposures": {
      "count": 0,
      "percent": 0,
      "status": "ok"
    }
  },
  "metrics": {
    "property1": {
      "id": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "status": "failing",
      "role": "guardrail",
      "relativeLift": 0,
      "absoluteLift": 0,
      "ciHarmBound": 0,
      "pValue": 0
    },
    "property2": {
      "id": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "status": "failing",
      "role": "guardrail",
      "relativeLift": 0,
      "absoluteLift": 0,
      "ciHarmBound": 0,
      "pValue": 0
    }
  }
}
```

Populated when monitoring is enabled and analysis data is available. Contains the current evaluator decision, aggregate traffic health, and per-metric status with effect sizes.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|safeToAdvance|boolean|true|none|True only when every hold condition is cleared: the step interval has elapsed, any required approval has been granted, min sample size is met, and all monitored metrics are within bounds. Equivalent to `decision === 'advance'`.|
|decision|string|true|none|Current evaluator decision for the active step. Incorporates all hold conditions (timing, approval, min sample, metric health). When monitoring data is not yet available, the evaluator returns `hold` with a descriptive `decisionReason`.|
|decisionReason|string|false|none|Human-readable reason for a hold, rollback, or pause decision.|
|signals|[string]|true|none|All active health signals, not just the top-priority one. Useful for surfacing multiple concurrent issues (e.g. SRM + guardrail failing simultaneously). `healthy` is the sole entry when no issues are detected.|
|snapshotAt|string|false|none|ISO timestamp of the most recent successful analysis snapshot.|
|traffic|object|false|none|Traffic health from the latest snapshot. Absent when no snapshot has been taken yet.|
|metrics|object|true|none|Per-metric health keyed by metric ID. Only includes metrics configured as guardrails or signals on this schedule.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|decision|advance|
|decision|hold|
|decision|rollback|
|decision|pause|
|signals|guardrail-failing|
|signals|signal-regression|
|signals|srm|
|signals|multiple-exposures|
|signals|no-traffic|
|signals|below-min-sample|
|signals|healthy|
|signals|awaiting-data|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|approvalNotes|string \| null|false|none|none|
|monitored|boolean|false|none|When true, this step runs A/B traffic analysis while active. Treatment = [0, coverage), control = [0.5, 0.5+coverage). Arms are equal-sized and non-adjacent: step-ups only add users, never reassign existing ones. The UI caps monitored-step coverage at 0.5 so control end never exceeds 1.0. The SDK uses explicit hash ranges on the experiment rule to prevent bucketing shifts across monitored/unmonitored transitions.|
|holdConditions|object|false|none|none|
|actions|[object]|true|none|none|
